deployment-probes.json.description: Machine-readable deployment probes for transport- and operator-posture requirements that are not object-model conformance vectors.

probe.success_condition: for high-security or sovereign profile claims, the completed handshake negotiated TLS group X25519MLKEM768; a peer that does not offer that group is rejected rather than downgraded

cases.name: mention_selector
assertions: selector resolution binds the persisted mention subject_id to the agent DID
controller, slug and original text are audit metadata only
slug changes do not rewrite historical mention targets
ambiguous or unavailable selector claims fail closed

cases.name: ceiling_tighten
assertions: Circle and Strand participation ceilings may only drop bits from their parent
a child that enables act_on_behalf below a disabled parent bit is rejected
a Strand that re-enables a Circle-disabled third-party mention bit is rejected

cases.name: effective_intersection
assertions: effective participation is the bitwise meet of ceiling and controller selection
reply grants materialize only when the effective reply bit is true
act-on-behalf is not granted when the ceiling disables it
tightening the ceiling revokes previously materialized reply grants
unknown or stale ceiling source fails closed to no effective participation

cases.name: selection_within_ceiling
assertions: controller selection must be a subset of the effective ceiling
selection that enables third-party mention above the ceiling is rejected
rejected selections create no capability grants

cases.name: session_overlay
assertions: session scope_details.participation entries are isomorphic to agent_participation_entry
the overlay is a behavior contract and not an authorization boundary
missing backing capability grant still fails the runtime operation

cases.name: third_party_mention_gate
assertions: when accept_third_party_mention is false, non-controller mentions fan out to no agent delivery artifacts
the controller's own mention still delivers
enabling third-party mention later is non-retroactive
subsequent third-party mentions deliver only after the effective bit is true

cases.name: sidecar_ensure_idempotent
assertions: ensure operation id remains ck.self.agent.sidecar_thread.command.ensure
ensure capability action matches the operation id
sidecar profile id remains ck.profile.agent_sidecar_thread.v1

cases.name: sidecar_eligibility_states
assertions: paused agents fail sidecar ensure with agent_paused
deactivated agents fail sidecar ensure with agent_deactivated
default home policy remains context_realm_preferred

cases.name: sidecar_existence_privacy
assertions: callers without sidecar ensure capability receive sidecar_create_denied
sidecar existence is not disclosed via a not_found branch

cases.name: sidecar_multi_agent_publish
assertions: ensure, write, and publish capability actions all remain sidecar-thread scoped
the sidecar capability action trio contains no duplicates

cases.name: agent_provision
assertions: agent provision operation id remains ck.self.agent.command.provision
agent provision capability action matches the operation id
agent grants marked effective_after_first_authorized_key remain inactive before key pairing
missing accountability grants fail with accountability_grant_missing

cases.name: agent_pairing_expiry
assertions: agent key-pair operation id remains ck.gate.account.command.pair_agent_key
expired pairing requests fail with pairing_request_expired
DID mismatch, invalid proof, expired pairing, and deactivated agent errors are all pinned

cases.name: agent_controller_lifecycle
assertions: agent lifecycle operation ids retain canonical namespaces
active to paused to active to deactivated is accepted
deactivated is terminal and resume fails with agent_deactivated
pause while paused fails with agent_paused

cases.name: agent_act_on_behalf
assertions: controller approvals are single-use
approval replay fails with approval_already_consumed
act-on-behalf without authorization_ref, participation, matching grant scope, or fresh approval fails closed
unauthorised sidecar creation fails with sidecar_create_denied

cases.name: agent_session_grant_replay
assertions: session grant issue operation id remains ck.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant
agent_key_proof challenge replay, audience mismatch, and bad signature fail closed
agent session branch rejects invalid proofs, DID mismatch, paused agents, and deactivated agents
accountability grant absence is pinned as accountability_grant_missing

cases.name: session_grant_audience_binding
assertions: proof.audience must match the target resource service audience
request_canonical_digest must cover principal_id, device_id, requested_scope, and audience
requested session grant lifetime is clamped to the Auth Server hard maximum
development_mode=true must not advertise ck.profile.auth_server.v1 in verified_profiles

cases.name: soft_logout_did_proof
assertions: a holder key alone cannot restore a soft_logged_out session
the DID proof transcript covers principal_id, device_id, audience, challenge, request digest, issued_at, and expires_at
verification burns the challenge and only then restores the session to active

cases.name: did_proof_replay_window
assertions: first valid proof burns the challenge
second use of the same challenge fails closed even with a valid signature
audience or origin mismatch fails closed
expires_at - issued_at greater than 300 seconds is rejected
issued_at outside receiver skew is rejected

cases.name: pop_presentation
assertions: valid self write PoP covers method, target-uri, authority, and content-digest
Content-Digest is recomputed against the actual body before trusting the signature
method, path, or body transcript mismatch rejects the request

cases.name: bare_bearer_rejected_protected
assertions: production current-v1 protected endpoints reject bare bearer unless sender-constrained proof is present
public metadata surfaces do not treat bare bearer as session or capability authentication
PoP created/expires outside the replay window is rejected even after replay-cache eviction

fixtures/blob-stream-aead-fixture.json.notes: Adversarial bound cases are declared-field-only: the runner MUST judge them from the envelope's declared segment_size / segment_count / size_bytes values before deriving keys or downloading any segment, and MUST NOT materialise multi-MiB plaintext or ciphertext to exercise them.

cases.name: stream_aead_roundtrip
assertions: multi-segment plaintext with a short final segment decrypts byte-for-byte
incremental segment verification accepts only ascending segment indices
ciphertext_digest is recomputed over the concatenated ciphertext and mismatches fail with digest_mismatch

cases.name: stream_aead_truncation_rejected
assertions: dropping the final legal segment fails finish with segment_stream_truncated
declared segment_count must equal ceil(size_bytes / segment_size)
count mismatches are rejected before a stream can be completed

cases.name: stream_aead_reorder_rejected
assertions: out-of-order segment_index fails with segment_sequence_invalid
repeated segment_index fails with segment_replay
no deterministic reordering or replay recovery is attempted

cases.name: stream_aead_scheme_closure
assertions: unknown stream attachment schemes fail closed with unsupported_attachment_scheme
valid stream envelopes satisfy blob.schema.json#/$defs/encrypted_attachment
envelopes carrying both nonce and nonce_prefix/segment_* fields fail encrypted_attachment oneOf validation

cases.name: stream_aead_bounds_rejected

expected.rule: segment_count MUST equal ceil(size_bytes / segment_size); declared 4 but ceil(2621440 / 262144) = 10

assertions: declared segment_count above 2^20 fails closed with segment_bounds_invalid before any key derivation or segment download
declared segment_size below 1024 or above 8388608 fails blob.schema.json#/$defs/encrypted_attachment bounds and is rejected with segment_bounds_invalid
declared segment_count inconsistent with ceil(size_bytes / segment_size) fails closed with segment_bounds_invalid
receivers never preallocate buffers or download plans from unvalidated declared bounds; cases are judged on declared fields only, no multi-MiB payload is materialised

cases.name: participant_binding_invalid
assertions: unanchored participant_binding issuer maps to participant_binding_invalid at reducer admission
tuple mismatch maps to participant_binding_invalid while preserving schema validity
expired participant_binding maps to participant_binding_invalid
signature verification failure maps to participant_binding_invalid
fully valid participant_binding control is accepted

cases.name: initial_state_accepts_allowed
assertions: scheduled, ringing, and connecting are the only accepted initial states
active and terminal initial states fail with call_state_transition_invalid

cases.name: transition_matrix
assertions: every call-state.md legal transition edge is accepted
representative non-terminal illegal edges fail with call_state_transition_invalid
non-terminal illegal edges are not reported as call_state_terminal

cases.name: terminal_absorbing
assertions: ended, missed, failed, and cancelled reject every outgoing transition
terminal outgoing attempts fail with call_state_terminal
the original terminal head remains unchanged

cases.name: replay_same_state_noop
assertions: same-basis replay of ringing to connecting is idempotent
duplicate equivalent transitions keep the final head at connecting
duplicate equivalent transitions do not surface call_state_transition_invalid

cases.name: concurrent_sibling_bottom
assertions: same-basis ringing to active and ringing to missed siblings produce Bottom
the Bottom kind is conflict
no deterministic winner is selected from the sibling heads

cases.name: recording_retention_lock
assertions: audit_lock blocks recording deletion regardless of retention_expires_at
capture without consent_confirmed fails with recording_consent_required
unlocked expired retention permits deletion

cases.name: recording_result_artifact_shape
assertions: ready recording_result carries ck.schema.call_recording_artifact.v1 metadata
backend-direct recording URLs fail with recording_artifact_pipeline_bypassed
completed deletion carries deletion_audit and erasure_receipt_ref

cases.name: transcribe_lifecycle
assertions: transcription requires ck.call.transcribe capability
transcript artifacts use ck-rtc-transcript-key/v1
SFrame or recording exporter labels are rejected for transcripts

cases.name: moderator_kick_ban
assertions: moderation requires ck.call.moderate capability
device-scoped kicks block only that device
actor-wide bans block every device for that actor

cases.name: p2p_to_sfu_upgrade
assertions: three active participants force p2p calls to sfu mode
sfu mode does not auto-downgrade when participants drop to two
ck.call.summary is accepted only for terminal call states

notes: These vectors pin CBA dual-plane semantics. DataEvent vectors use effects + seal_ref + auth_context and never use preconditions. Control Move vectors use effects + seal_basis and may use preconditions.

Seal delta entries reference only newly sealed control-plane event digests. Cumulative coverage is derived from predecessor_refs[] plus delta[]. DataEvent digests may appear in data_event_set_root / data_view_root observations, but those roots do not confer control-plane finality.
Cell ids follow ck:cell:<component>:<subject>; subject placeholders use dot-safe strings to keep examples unambiguous.

lattice_round_trip.description: SDK lattice round-trip runner coverage for CBA lattice family vectors whose semantics are exercised directly through cokret_core::lattice implementations.

assertions: concurrent_set_surfaces_all_heads
does_not_choose_winner
pn_sum_is_deterministic
inc_dec_replay_order_independent
per_issuer_sequence_order
same_issuer_seq_dedupes_deterministically
gap_after_contiguous_prefix_is_pending_diagnostic
pending_gap_entry_does_not_enter_cell_value
backfill_recompute_is_arrival_order_independent
duplicate_same_issuer_seq_uses_min_entry_id
duplicate_same_transition_idempotent
same_from_different_to_returns_bottom

vectors.name: data_event_accepts_without_seal_finality
vectors.description: A message DataEvent is locally accepted when signature, actor chain, seal_ref, auth_context, capability and data-plane Lattice validation pass. It does not wait for Seal coverage.

vectors.name: data_event_observation_does_not_seal
vectors.description: A Seal may observe DataEvents through data_event_set_root, but the query grade is observed, not sealed.

vectors.name: control_move_requires_seal_basis_and_seal
vectors.description: A membership ban Control Move uses seal_basis for authorization and preconditions. It remains control_pending until covered by a valid Seal.

vectors.name: same_batch_does_not_advance_authorization_basis
vectors.description: An Event earlier in the same submit batch may resolve bytes and causal refs for later Events, but it cannot create a grant used by a later Event in the same batch.

vectors.name: data_plane_conflict_returns_bottom_without_winner
vectors.description: Concurrent incompatible writes to a data-plane cas_register cell return structured bottom. The reducer must not choose a winner by HLC, actor id, arrival order, or Seal observation order.

vectors.name: seal_delta_excludes_data_event_digest
vectors.description: A Seal delta contains newly sealed control-plane event digests only. Including a DataEvent digest in delta is a seal validation failure.

vectors.name: open_set_compaction_preserves_control_roots
vectors.description: A signed compaction Seal must be equivalent to the deterministic control view of its predecessors and preserve control_event_set_root, state_root and fault diagnostics.

vectors.name: seal_canonical_no_self_reference
vectors.description: Seal canonical bytes are computed from signed top-level body fields only. The Seal id and notary_signature are excluded from the transcript.

vectors.name: cas_mixed_basis
vectors.description: cas_register writes on a non-initial settled value require an explicit CBA basis; null-basis blind overwrites fail closed.

vectors.name: auth_context_epoch_pinning_reject
vectors.description: Verifier evaluates key and credential epoch validity at the event seal_ref, not only against the current DID document.

vectors.name: seal_compaction_interval_enforced
vectors.description: Realm seal_compaction_max_interval_ms is a structural obligation: valid full-coverage compaction enables bootstrap, mismatched coverage rejects, and overdue compaction raises health alarms.

vectors.name: inclusion_list_obligation
vectors.description: A multi-signer notary Seal must discharge valid inclusion-list obligations by inclusion, signed reject, or pre-state verification failure proof.

vectors.name: notary_fault_equivocation_quarantine
vectors.description: Two different Seals signed by the same notary in the same slot authorize public equivocation evidence, quarantine the fork, and reject later Seals from that signer.

vectors.name: threshold_forensic_attribution
vectors.description: Threshold notary forensic_attribution must match the quorum-intersection arithmetic rule.

vectors.name: open_set_concurrent_revocation_fail_closed
vectors.description: A DataEvent whose seal_ref is locally valid is re-evaluated against the joined multi-leaf control view when a concurrent revocation branch is observed.

vectors.name: conflict_recovery_move
vectors.description: A bottom=reject control cell recovers only through a sealed Control Move with recovery_capability and a pre-conflict state_witness.

fixtures/circle-scope-fixture.json.description: Machine-contract fixture for Circle effective_scope semantics. Splits actor submit-payload (scope_circle_id only) from canonical reducer-output (tagged effective_scope on Event envelope and materialized object). Covers None->None, same-scope->same-scope, None->Some, Some->None, Some(A)->Some(B) rebind transitions plus negative cases. negative_cases also pin the accepted-Event / materialized-object closure: accepted Circle-scoped DataEvents MUST carry effective_scope, effective_scope MUST agree with scope_circle_id, the signed event_digest binds effective_scope, and content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required rejects plaintext content. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md §6.1 / §6.2 / §7 / §10.2.

submit_payload_shape.description: Actor-supplied input on ck.strand.create / ck.message.create / ck.morph.create / ck.relation.create / ck.space.* writes. MUST carry only scope_circle_id (id:circle | null). MUST NOT carry effective_scope.

canonical_reducer_output_shape.description: Reducer-stamped, immutable tagged scope written to Event envelope and materialized object cell. Two discriminated forms: kind=realm | kind=circle.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.name: none_to_none_noop
scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=null -> scope_circle_id=null. No-op rebind; reducer MUST accept (idempotent same-scope), effective_scope stays {kind:realm}.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.name: same_circle_to_same_circle_noop
scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=Some(A) -> scope_circle_id=Some(A). No-op rebind; reducer MUST accept.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.name: none_to_circle_default_reject
scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=null -> scope_circle_id=Some(A). True rebind; default reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile MAY enable audit-paired high-risk update.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.name: circle_to_none_default_reject
scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=Some(A) -> scope_circle_id=null. True rebind; default reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile MAY enable audit-paired high-risk update.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.name: circle_a_to_circle_b_default_reject
scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=Some(A) -> scope_circle_id=Some(B). True rebind across circles; default reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile MAY enable audit-paired high-risk update.

negative_cases.name: submit_payload_carrying_effective_scope_rejected
negative_cases.description: Actor MUST NOT supply effective_scope in submit payload. Reducer MUST schema_violation with reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed.

negative_cases.name: scope_circle_id_targets_inactive_circle
negative_cases.description: scope_circle_id references a Circle with state != active. Reducer MUST failed_precondition reason=circle_not_active.

negative_cases.name: scope_circle_id_realm_mismatch
negative_cases.description: scope_circle_id references a Circle whose realm_id != object.realm_id. Reducer MUST schema_violation reason=circle_realm_mismatch.

negative_cases.name: accepted_event_missing_effective_scope
negative_cases.description: An accepted durable Circle-scoped Event (e.g. ck.message.create whose Strand scope_circle_id is set) MUST carry the reducer-stamped effective_scope on its envelope. An offline validator / cotest MUST reject an accepted event whose object is Circle-scoped but whose effective_scope is absent, otherwise the §9.3 'Circle scoped event not delivered to non-members' invariant cannot be deterministically replayed. event-envelope.schema.json carries effective_scope as a reducer-stamped field; this vector pins that accepted (post-reducer) Circle events MUST populate it.

negative_cases.name: effective_scope_mismatches_scope_circle_id
negative_cases.description: The reducer-stamped effective_scope MUST be derived from the object's scope_circle_id: scope_circle_id=null -> {kind:realm}; scope_circle_id=C -> {kind:circle, circle_id:C}. A materialized object / accepted event whose effective_scope.circle_id disagrees with its scope_circle_id is corrupt; reducer MUST schema_violation (effective_scope_reducer_managed) on write and a validator MUST reject on read.

negative_cases.name: seal_leaf_effective_scope_tamper
negative_cases.description: effective_scope is part of an Event's canonical bytes, so event_digest = H(canonical bytes) binds it directly. If a Seal later reports the DataEvent inside data_event_set_root, that root is an observational availability/projection proof, not control-plane finality. Mutating effective_scope after signing changes event_digest, so the recomputed digest no longer matches the signed event. Receivers MUST reject with digest_mismatch; this forbids silently re-scoping an accepted event and is why no separate scope field is added to seal.schema.json (the binding is the digest).

negative_cases.name: content_plaintext_under_e2ee_required
negative_cases.description: Realm.content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required requires every Strand/Message/Morph/Blob content effective_scope to be MLS-backed (Realm-default MLS or Circle MLS). A ck.message.create carrying plaintext content (or whose effective_scope resolves to a plaintext Circle with encryption_profile=none) MUST be rejected with failed_precondition reason=content_encryption_floor_violation.

vectors.name: ck.vector.encoding.crypto.ed25519_detached_jws.v1
vectors.description: Ed25519 detached JWS over the canonical proof binding object for a Cokret Event Envelope.

test_private_key_jwk.note: Public conformance test key only. Production profiles MUST reject this test DID/key domain.

vectors.name: ck.vector.encoding.crypto.es256_detached_jws.v1
vectors.description: ECDSA P-256 (ES256, RFC 6979 deterministic) detached JWS over the canonical proof binding object for a Cokret Event Envelope. Optional interop suite gated by ck.profile.signature.ecdsa_p256.v1.

test_private_key_jwk.note: Public conformance test key only (d = fixed seed bytes 0x00..0x1f). Production profiles MUST reject this test DID/key domain. Signature is RFC 6979 deterministic, so this vector is fully reproducible from the seed.

vectors.name: ck.vector.encoding.crypto.mldsa65_raw_detached_signature.v1
vectors.description: ML-DSA-65 (NIST FIPS 204) raw detached signature over the canonical proof binding object bytes (registry proof_kind = raw_detached_signature; no JOSE wrapping). PQC suite gated by ck.profile.signature.pqc.v1.
vectors.keygen_note: Public conformance test key only, derived via FIPS 204 ML-DSA.KeyGen from the recorded 32-byte xi seed (bytes 0x00..0x1f). Production profiles MUST reject this test DID/key domain.
vectors.raw_signing_input: UTF-8 bytes of canonical_binding_payload (detached_payload_b64u is its base64url form, provided for cross-checking only; the signed bytes are the unencoded canonical JSON)
vectors.signature_note: Recorded value produced with the FIPS 204 deterministic variant (rnd = 32 zero bytes). Verifiers MUST only verify; producers are NOT required to reproduce these exact signature bytes (hedged signing is allowed).

negative_cases.name: reject_flipped_signature_bit
negative_cases.description: One bit of the Ed25519 signature is flipped (first signature byte XOR 0x01); everything else is byte-identical to the valid vector.

expected.reason: signature bytes do not verify against the canonical proof binding object

negative_cases.name: reject_alg_none
negative_cases.description: Protected header declares alg=none. The signature segment carries well-formed base64url bytes so the rejection MUST come from the algorithm allowlist, not from shape validation.

expected.reason: alg=none is not an active row of signature-alg-registry.json; critical proofs MUST fail closed before any verification is attempted

negative_cases.name: reject_alg_key_type_mismatch
negative_cases.description: Protected header declares ES256 and the signature genuinely verifies under a P-256 key, but kid resolves to the Ed25519 OKP verification method. The verifier MUST bind alg to the resolved key type (jwk_kty/jwk_crv per signature-alg-registry.json) and fail closed.

expected.reason: declared alg ES256 does not match the resolved verification method key type (OKP/Ed25519); implementations MUST NOT verify with a substituted key

negative_cases.name: reject_truncated_public_key
negative_cases.description: The DID Document publicKeyJwk.x is truncated to 31 bytes; the JWS is the untampered valid vector value.

expected.reason: verification key fails to parse (31 bytes is not an Ed25519 public key length); key material errors MUST fail closed, not fall back to another key

negative_cases.name: reject_non_empty_payload_segment
negative_cases.description: The detached payload is re-attached as the JWS payload segment. The signature still verifies as an attached JWS over the identical signing input, so accepting it would silently downgrade the detached profile; receivers MUST reject on the non-empty payload segment alone.

expected.reason: detached_jws payload segment MUST be empty in compact serialization (encoding.md section 6) even when the attached form would verify

fixtures/cursor-negative-fixture.json.description: Machine-readable negative cursor vectors mirrored from zh/conformance/conformance-vectors.md section 1.16. Complements the positive opaqueness vector ck.vector.encoding.cursor_opaque.core.v1: every case below is a schema-valid-looking ck:cursor: token that a conformant receiver MUST reject before advancing any server-side state. reason_code values are stable codes from error-code-registry.json (invalid_cursor is surfaced under top-level invalid_param).

cases.name: oversized_token
cases.violation: encoded token exceeds the 4KB body cap before any decode work

cases.name: invalid_base64url
cases.violation: token payload is not unpadded base64url

cases.name: malformed_json
cases.violation: decoded body is not valid JSON

cases.name: duplicate_json_key
cases.violation: duplicate JSON key violates canonical JSON ingress rules

cases.name: non_nfc_string
cases.violation: decoded t string value is not Unicode NFC (it carries U+0065 U+0301 instead of the NFC composed form U+00E9); canonical JSON ingress MUST reject. The raw body is intentionally not inlined here so this fixture file itself stays NFC-clean; the base64url token is the authoritative input.

cases.name: inline_positions_rejected
cases.violation: v1 core cursor body carries only the opaque handle; inline position state (s) violates the closed {v,purpose,t,x,h} schema

cases.name: unsupported_version
cases.violation: cursor version is not in supported_versions (v1 core supports only "1")

cases.name: handle_too_short
cases.violation: stateful handle h is shorter than the 22-character minimum (>=128 bits of entropy)

cases.name: non_canonical_timestamp
cases.violation: t must be a canonical UTC Z timestamp; the +00:00 offset form is rejected

cases.name: stream_ttl_exceeds_cap
cases.violation: x - t exceeds the stream-purpose hard TTL cap of 7 days (encoding.md section 8.3 rule 12)

cases.name: barrier_ttl_exceeds_cap
cases.violation: x - t exceeds the barrier-purpose hard TTL cap of 1 hour (encoding.md section 8.3 rule 12)

cases.name: expired
cases.violation: x expiry is in the past

vectors.fixture_freshness_note: All timestamps are pinned so every case stays deterministically rejectable for the spec lifetime: expired cases use year-2020 values (always past), TTL-cap and negative-TTL cases use year-2099 x values (not expired before 2099) with a violation that is checked before any now-relative comparison could differ.
rules: receivers MUST reject every case before advancing subscription position, barrier wait, or any other server-side state

syntax / schema / TTL-bound failures surface as top-level invalid_param with reason_code invalid_cursor; expiry uses cursor_expired; handle lookup or cross-binding failures (not covered here, they need server state) use cursor_integrity_invalid
receivers MUST enforce the 4KB cap on the encoded token before spending base64 or JSON parsing work
TTL bound checks MUST validate t well-formedness first, then t <= x, then t not in the future beyond clock skew, then x - t against the per-purpose cap, so a corrupt t cannot bypass the cap

fixtures/encoding-fixture.json.description: Machine-readable encoding & crypto vectors mirrored from zh/conformance/conformance-vectors.md §1.3-§1.13. Conformance runners MUST execute every vector and compare canonical_bytes / digest / order outputs. The crypto.ed25519_detached_jws vector lives separately in crypto-signature-fixture.json; the rank_order vector covers hex-Base32 rank string ordering (LIST item placement).
fixtures/encoding-fixture.json.generator_semantics: Vectors of kind *_reject_generated carry a `generator` object instead of literal input bytes: the runner MUST construct the input at execution time from the generator parameters (e.g. nesting_depth, array_item_count) following the generator.rule text, so the fixture never stores megabyte-scale literals. Rejection is asserted exactly as for literal-input vectors.

rules: object key MUST be sorted by UTF-16 code unit at every level
array order MUST be preserved as input
string values MUST NOT be rewritten by key sort
NaN / Infinity / -Infinity MUST reject
-0 MUST reject
v1 signed JSON numbers MUST be integers; 1.0 / 1e0 / fractional or exponent decimal spellings MUST reject instead of being canonicalised
signature verification MUST run only after canonicalisation succeeds

rejected_input_classes: duplicate JSON object keys at the same level
lone surrogate or ambiguous escape sequence
non-integer JSON numbers or parser-accepted numbers that cannot be proven to be integers
rules: duplicate keys MUST NOT be silently overwritten by parser default
malformed strings MUST NOT be replaced with U+FFFD before signing
rejection MUST be auditable; reason_code SHOULD be schema_violation, invalid_canonical_json, or invalid_encoding
event digest MUST be derived from canonical bytes after stripping proofs and unsigned, before redaction
event_id MUST appear inside the digest input but does not replace the digest
transport envelope, HTTP headers, sync metadata, and local receive time MUST NOT be hashed
the same event MUST yield the same digest on every Events API and Sync Service

fail_conditions: events array sorted or deduplicated before hashing
proof field included in receipt digest

rules: proof MUST bind event_digest, actor DID, verification_method, and created_at
cross-service / cross-domain verification SHOULD additionally bind domain or audience
actual ed25519 detached JWS for this binding lives in crypto-signature-fixture.json
HLC MUST sort by (unix_ms, logical, node_id_hash)
implementations MUST NOT compare HLC as raw wall-clock string unless the profile guarantees fixed-width lowercase hex such that string compare equals tuple compare

expected_acceptable_outcomes: wait until unix_ms_hex advances, then emit 01970e589d22-0000-a13f9c2e
return local error hlc_logical_overflow before canonical bytes are produced; caller retries
fail_conditions: logical counter wraps to a smaller value while still emitting events
wall-clock skew is forged to escape overflow at the cost of HLC monotonicity or causality
consumer accepts wrap-around values into accepted history

vectors.fixture_freshness_note: Timestamps are fixed at year 2099 deliberately so the static vector cannot expire during normal spec lifetime. Implementations generating their own conformance cursors MUST use fresh `t`/`x` matching their authority's clock; do NOT reuse this fixture's `t`/`x` on the wire.
client_rules: MUST treat cursor as an opaque string and round-trip it verbatim
MUST NOT parse v / purpose / t / h / x to construct the next page request
MUST handle cursor decode failure by treating cursor as opaque, not by aborting the protocol
server_rules: MUST validate v, purpose, x, the full core cursor schema, and h handle binding before honouring cursor
syntax validation failure MUST return invalid_param with reason_code invalid_cursor; TTL failure MUST return cursor_expired; handle lookup or binding failure MUST return cursor_integrity_invalid
fail_conditions: client parses h/x and rebuilds a request

cases.name: e2ee_routing_digest_dedup
cases.notes: In an E2EE realm the plaintext key is the v1 keyed-HMAC routing tag: HMAC-SHA256(key = MLS-Exporter("cokret-reaction-routing-v1", context = realm_id), data = NFC(canonical_emoji)); see zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9. The 32-byte tag is carried in `key` as a 256-bit hex digest (the sha256: prefix below denotes the digest wire-encoding, not the derivation). Two adds with the same routing tag from the same actor in the same epoch collapse to one OR-Set membership; the tag differs in a different epoch because the MLS exporter secret rotates on every commit, so it does not dedup across epochs. realm_id is bound via the exporter context, providing defense-in-depth even if mls_group_id is reused across deployments.

cases.name: e2ee_epoch_rotation_breaks_dedup
cases.notes: Same canonical emoji yields a different routing hash after MLS epoch rotation; the new add is a fresh OR-Set entry, not a duplicate of the pre-rotation one.

cases.name: capability_revoked_blocks_subsequent_add

cases.name: rate_limit_high_rate_reaction_burst

migration_group_definitions.agent_session_namespace_collapse: Superseded by agent_applet_interop_session_rename: the agent capability action namespace and the agent/applet session event kinds now both use the interop_session form.
migration_group_definitions.typed_id_prefix_unabbreviation: Abbreviated typed-id prefixes expanded to full snake_case kind. Single rule: ck:<abbrev>: → ck:<full_kind>: (9 entries).
migration_group_definitions.realm_lifecycle_segment_realignment: Realm lifecycle capability actions flattened from 4 segments (cx.realm.lifecycle.<verb>) to 3 segments (cx.realm.<verb>) to match the corresponding event kind (4 entries). target_event_kinds preserved.
migration_group_definitions.did_id_suffix: Protocol responsibility subjects use the _id suffix even when the value is a DID. actor_did / principal_did / subject_did renamed to actor_id / principal_id / subject_id, and the bare wire fields `actor` (policy check request, bound_to, capability vector request; MIMI consent update request) and `requester` (MIMI consent request) renamed to actor_id / requester_id (6 entries).
migration_group_definitions.agent_key_imperative_verbs: Event kind verbs use imperative action names, not past participles. cx.agent.key.{authorized,revoked,rotated} → cx.agent.key.{authorize,revoke,rotate} (3 entries).
migration_group_definitions.device_imperative_verbs: Same rule as agent_key_imperative_verbs but for device key events (2 entries).
migration_group_definitions.crdt_lattice_snake_case: CRDT lattice enum values use snake_case (5 entries).
migration_group_definitions.hash_to_digest_vocabulary: Wire fields carrying hash output bytes use _digest with self-describing <alg>:<hex>; algorithm selectors use _algorithm; tree roots use _root. _hash is forbidden as wire field-name suffix (~50 entries).
migration_group_definitions.signature_algorithm_vocabulary: Signature and key algorithm selector fields use the full _algorithm suffix; JOSE/JWK nested headers may still use standard alg.
migration_group_definitions.blob_reference_naming: Blob references use <noun>_blob_ref when the role noun is not already blob.
migration_group_definitions.full_word_field_names: Protocol wire fields use full nouns for signature/public_key/base64url material rather than sig/pubkey/b64 abbreviations.
migration_group_definitions.status_axis_timestamp: Status-axis transition timestamps use status_changed_at instead of a bare changed_at.
migration_group_definitions.claim_kind_discriminator: Closed protocol-level claim discriminators use claim_kind; external credential taxonomy selectors may continue to use claim_type.
migration_group_definitions.duration_iso8601: Human-readable policy duration wire strings use ISO 8601 (^P...) as the single v1 format; the self-invented compact ^[0-9]+(ms|s|m|h|d)$ mini-DSL is forbidden. Machine timing fields keep integer _ms / _seconds. See common-fields.md §3.0.2.
migration_group_definitions.frank_to_franking_proof_noun: Moderation franking objects use the full franking_proof noun (4 entries).
migration_group_definitions.verb_noun_bridge_collapse: Capability actions converged back to noun form matching their target event kind. The earlier verb-form action names (.manage / .modify / create_*) are forbidden; new IAM tools can use the event kind string verbatim as the action token. 6 entries; v3 (2026-05-24). See authz/capabilities.md §5.0a.
migration_group_definitions.grant_constraint_single_kind_ids: Grant constraint fields that carry one concrete protocol identifier kind use `_ids`; `_refs` remains reserved for causal/proof/schema/content-addressed or polymorphic reference material.
migration_group_definitions.metadata_encryption_floor_rename: Wire field metadata_encryption_profile renamed to metadata_encryption_floor.
migration_group_definitions.key_backup_kdf_hash_to_digest_algorithm: Key backup KDF parameter algorithm selectors use digest_algorithm; hash is reserved for actual digest material and internal JSON Schema defs.
migration_group_definitions.brand_namespace_cx_to_ck: Wire/brand namespace renamed from the legacy `contrix` brand to `cokret`. Every wire token prefix `cx.` becomes `ck.` and every typed-id prefix `cx:` becomes `ck:` across operation_id, event_kind, schema_id, capability action, id_kind, error code, vector id, and profile id. The bare brand strings `contrix` / `Contrix` and the token prefixes `cx.` / `cx:` are hard_reject on the current wire and in current identifiers (allowed only in CHANGELOG / migration docs / negative drift fixtures). HTTP paths additionally moved to the versionless trust-circle namespace `/_cokret/<segment>/...` (see sync/service-http-binding.md §2.1); the legacy flat paths and `/api/v1` / `/cokret/v1` prefixes are recorded in removed-operation-ids.json. Mechanical, single design decision; the entries below are representative seals, the rule applies to the whole token space.
migration_group_definitions.operation_id_trust_surface_segment: Scheme B: operation_id now encodes its trust-surface classifier as the mandatory leading segment (ck.<surface>.<resource>.<action>, surface in {self,peer,edge,root,find,gate,open}), matching the HTTP path's first segment 1:1. 108 operations gain the surface prefix; peer.* were already compliant and ck.server.describe (pre-auth root meta, no surface segment) is the sole exception. grpc service names gain the PascalCase surface prefix and mq topics the lowercase surface segment in lockstep. Single design decision; entries are mechanical applications.
migration_group_definitions.agent_applet_interop_session_rename: Agent and applet session surfaces renamed from the ambiguous `protocol_session` (which reads as the ambient Cokret protocol) to `interop_session`, naming the external agent-to-agent interop relationship. Event kinds ck.{agent,applet}.protocol_session.* -> ck.{agent,applet}.interop_session.*; the agent capability action namespace ck.agent.session.* (start/cancel/stream_status/attach_artifact/read_transcript) -> ck.agent.interop_session.*; the typed id and schema payload defs use the agent_interop_session_* / applet_interop_session_* short form. Single design decision.
migration_group_definitions.conformance_verifier_neutralization: ServiceDescribe.verified_profiles neutralized away from the downstream tool name cotest: claim_kind enum value cotest_verified → conformance_verified, wire fields cotest_run_id → verification_run_id and cotest_issuer_did → verifier_did. The wire contract binds to the neutral Conformance Verifier role (conformance-suite.md §6.2); cotest survives only as an informative reference-implementation name in prose (3 entries).
migration_group_definitions.cba_notary_seal_rename: CBA terminology family rename (2026-06-11): the Anchor/Anchorer word family is replaced by Seal/Notary across wire fields, typed-id prefixes, cell families, enum values and model names; the Seal cumulative-coverage frontier[] enumeration is retired in favor of predecessor_refs + delta recursion (no direct field successor; the snapshot manifest's boundary `frontier` object and the streaming `frontier` frame kind are true-frontier semantics and keep their names); proposal-era interim spellings (governance_ref, Checkpoint) are forbidden. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md and overview/glossary.md.

tier_rules.v1_profile_catalog: Profiles that belong to the v1 stable catalog. This is not a bundle requirement; implementations MUST claim only the profiles, event kinds, schemas, and operations they actually support.
tier_rules.v1_minimal_interop_floor: Minimum profile for claiming v1 Event Store interop. Higher-level client, service, federation, blob, push, identity, and sovereign profiles remain independently claimable.
tier_rules.extension_profile_implementation: Optional. Tracks implementation profiles outside the v1 minimal interop floor, including evolving external standards (MIMI Internet-Drafts; A2A/ACP/MCP unstandardized agent protocols; Applet registry/audit SLA) and opt-in product/privacy features such as productivity, disappearing messages, calendar events, pins, and search. Implementations claiming v1 core MAY omit these entirely; implementations MUST claim only entries they actually support. When an underlying external standard matures, a replacement profile with stable version pinning can supersede that entry.

profile_tiers.test_build_stance_rule: Test/conformance builds are marked solely by the canonical development_mode=true flag on the ServiceDescribe (see zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.1.2 and zh/sync/service-surface.md §3.0), which gates the test-only /_cokret/_conformance/* debug namespace and forces verified_profiles=[]. There is no separate ck.profile.* test-build profile: a test build is a deployment stance, not a negotiated interop capability.

profiles/conformance-profiles.json.candidate_profiles_tier_rule: Profiles pairing unregistered candidate workflow concept/action names / capabilities with an explicit fail-closed gate. Receivers MUST treat any capability action whose `profile` points to a candidate profile as unknown (risk_tier=high default) unless they implement the profile. Candidate profiles are NOT part of v1 active conformance and SHOULD be promoted (with paired wire Event.kind values registered under `ck.*`) once their underlying surface is formally registered.
profiles/conformance-profiles.json.profile_roles_rule: Every profile id MUST be annotated with exactly one role from the enum {client, server, gateway, directory, admin, interop}. Roles partition the profile namespace so that an implementation MUST NOT mistake e.g. a gateway profile (push_gateway, blob_node) for a client profile, or a deployment / hardening / vector profile (admin role) for a wire-conformance client / server profile. SDK manifests, client-side feature negotiation, and conformance harness loaders MUST consult `profile_roles` before claiming a profile as locally implemented. Roles in spec layer metadata; the per-profile object in `profile_requirements` MAY ALSO carry a `role` field for convenience, but `profile_roles` is the canonical source.

ck.profile.principal_control_realm.v1.description: Realm profile for a principal-scoped durable control stream (the Principal Control Realm role; see zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.7). It is an ordinary Collaboration Realm at the envelope level, but reducers MUST treat fields.purpose=principal_control + this schema_ref as an allowlist-bound control stream, not as a user collaboration space.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Receivers that do not understand ck.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 MUST treat the Realm as an ordinary Collaboration Realm and MUST NOT accept device/session/cross-signing state from it as principal control state.

ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.description: Degraded E2EE profile. Allows `mls_send_pause="advisory"` (cf. §2.4.1) so that low-latency interactive scenarios (real-time AV, collaborative editing, in-game chat) do not block message send on MLS commit completion. Cost: removed members can continue decrypting a small window of subsequent messages. NOT for general chat / collaboration / compliance use. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with ck.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Servers that do not advertise ck.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 MUST reject Realm create / ck.realm.policy_components writes that set mls_send_pause="advisory" (reason: profile_unsupported / mls_send_pause_advisory_requires_e2ee_relaxed_profile). They MUST NOT silently accept the advisory string without honoring the relaxed semantics.

downgrade_declaration_obligation.policy_declaration_required: Realm create or ck.realm.policy_components MUST explicitly declare ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 before mls_send_pause="advisory" is accepted. Out-of-band deployment config, UI-only labels, or a missing governance_binding GroupContext extension MUST NOT be treated as a valid downgrade declaration.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.service_describe_required: The serving implementation MUST advertise ck.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 and the claimed profile in ServiceDescribe before accepting advisory writes or projecting the Realm as relaxed to a peer/facade.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.binding_profile_required: Every MLS governance_binding emitted for a relaxed Realm MUST carry binding_profile="ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1" and the negotiated reducer_profile. Missing binding_profile, binding_profile="ck.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1", or an unsupported profile id is a fail-closed mismatch.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.export_marker_required: Sync metadata, snapshots, backups, exports, and interop mapping receipts that summarize the Realm MUST preserve e2ee_relaxed=true and relaxed_window_max_ms. Consumers that observe advisory semantics without this marker MUST assume the downgrade is undeclared and reject new old-epoch decrypt admission.

client_ui_requirements.banner_warning: Realms declaring this profile MUST display a banner-level warning indicating that kick / ban is not cryptographically immediate; the warning MAY be temporarily collapsed but MUST NOT be permanently dismissable.
client_ui_requirements.invite_warning: When a user invites a new member, the UI SHOULD prompt with 'this Realm uses degraded E2EE' so the invitee can make an informed decision.
client_ui_requirements.export_marker: Sync metadata / backup / export MUST preserve a `e2ee_relaxed=true` marker so downstream consumers know the cryptographic guarantee is relaxed.

downgrade_window_constraint.rationale: Receiving client refuses to admit a message into verified timeline if the gap between receive_at and the most recent membership_change_at exceeds this window with old-epoch decryption.
downgrade_window_constraint.receiver_enforcement: Receiver MUST enforce the hard ceiling independently of any declared deployment value: if a Realm policy event sets relaxed_window_max_ms > absolute_hard_ceiling_ms (300000 ms / 5 min), the reducer MUST reject the policy update with reason_code `relaxed_window_exceeds_ceiling` (mapped from `schema_violation`), and the receiver MUST treat the policy event as failed_precondition. Receivers MUST NOT silently clamp the value to the ceiling, because a silent clamp would let a deployment publish a longer window than receivers honor and split visible policy state across implementations. Negative vector: `ck.vector.e2ee_relaxed.window_exceeds_ceiling.v1` covers (a) reducer reject on policy write > 300000 ms, (b) receiver reject on old-epoch decrypt admission when the gap exceeds the per-policy declared window, and (c) reject when any deployment tries to redefine the ceiling via an unrelated profile.
downgrade_window_constraint.compliance_profile_disabled: Profiles in the compliance / audited tier (ck.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1, ck.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1, and any deployment with active Audit Applet Binding) MUST NOT enable ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Reducer MUST reject the combination with reason_code `e2ee_relaxed_disallowed_in_compliance_profile`. Rationale: compliance assurance presumes the kick-out semantic is cryptographically immediate; the relaxed window contradicts that presumption.

restricted_requires: each federation peer describes a fanout SLA not exceeding the relaxed window
each federation peer explicitly advertises ck.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 when it is expected to accept relaxed old-epoch decrypt admission
federation_guard.interop_floor: Full MLS governance binding (ck.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1) remains the federation E2EE interoperability floor. The relaxed profile (ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1) is a declared downgrade below that floor and is accepted across federation only for restricted/closed deployments that satisfy the bounded-SLA requirements above.

fail_closed_conditions: combination of ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 with ck.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1, compliance-tier E2EE, active Audit Applet Binding, federation_policy=open, or federation_policy=quarantine
restricted federation without peer fanout SLA bounds within relaxed_window_max_ms
governance_binding.binding_profile missing, unsupported, or inconsistent with the Realm downgrade declaration
receiver old-epoch decrypt gap exceeds relaxed_window_max_ms or the absolute hard ceiling of 300000 ms
ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.compliance_unfit: Compliance / regulatory contexts that require 'kick-out is immediately effective' MUST NOT use this profile. Use non-E2EE Realm (encryption_profile="none") + enclave channels instead. Spec deliberately does not allow further relaxation than this profile; deployments needing more leniency are out of v1 E2EE scope.

ck.profile.auth_server.v1.description: Cokret v1 Auth Server profile. Auth Servers verify login factors (password / passkey / OIDC / SSO / recovery), issue short-lived audience-bound `ck.session.grant` artefacts, expose session-grant introspection / revocation, and MAY surface a `ck.self.policy.query.check` decision endpoint. Auth Servers are NOT canonical identity registries (DID documents / key logs live in `ck.profile.identity_registry.v1`) and are NOT principal servers (no Realm-authoritative event acceptance). Coauth is the reference implementation. See zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md, zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5, zh/conformance/conformance-profiles.md §9a.

ck.profile.push_gateway.v1.description: Push gateway base profile. Provides the device registration / notify operation surface. All implementations claiming this profile MUST also implement ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 (default interop privacy baseline) — see zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §2.2 / §5.1. Visible-payload variants are opt-in only via ck.profile.push_gateway.visible_notification.v1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: strip unsupported plaintext fields

ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1.description: Default push gateway privacy baseline. Every implementation claiming ck.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile. Provider-facing payloads MUST NOT carry stable identifying fields (principal DID, sender DID, Realm id / name / avatar, Strand id / name, Message id, event id, device DID URL, reaction value, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key). Payloads MUST be restricted to per-(recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route) pairwise pseudonym push_target_id + closed-enum wakeup hint fields (wakeup_kind, badge_count, unread_increment, l10n_key). See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §2.2 / §4.5 / §5.1 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5a.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: MUST fail closed; gateways unable to enforce blind wakeup MUST NOT claim ck.profile.push_gateway.v1

additional_requirements.stable_identifier_ban_must: Provider payload MUST NOT contain principal DID, sender DID / handle, Realm id / name, Strand id / name, Message id, event id, device DID URL, reaction emoji, attachment filename, IP, geolocation, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key.
additional_requirements.pseudonym_scope_must: push_target_id MUST be a pairwise pseudonym scoped to (recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route); MUST NOT be reusable across Principal Server contexts.
additional_requirements.default_claim_must: Any implementation claiming ck.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile and MUST NOT advertise downgrade switches that disable blind wakeup.

ck.profile.push_gateway.visible_notifica.description: Opt-in push gateway profile for deployments that require visible notification fields (e.g. titles, sender labels) in provider payloads. Claiming this profile is permitted ONLY when (1) Realm policy explicitly lists the gateway in plaintext_visible_services AND declares visible_notification allowance, (2) per-device opt-in is recorded in ck.device authorization state, and (3) the client UI clearly surfaces that visible-notification mode is active. Even when claimed, payloads MUST stay minimised: no message body, no DID URL, no cross-Realm stable correlation key, no IP / geolocation, no free-form text outside the profile-declared field set. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §5.1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim; deployments that cannot guarantee Realm policy + device opt-in + UI disclosure MUST NOT claim this profile

additional_requirements.policy_gate_must: Realm policy MUST list the gateway service DID in plaintext_visible_services with visible_notification explicitly allowed.
additional_requirements.device_opt_in_must: Each receiving device MUST record an opt-in flag in its authorization state; absent opt-in, sender / Realm service MUST fall back to blind wakeup.
additional_requirements.ui_disclosure_must: Client UI MUST clearly indicate visible notification is active to the user.
additional_requirements.payload_minimisation_must: Even when claimed, payload MUST NOT carry message body, DID URLs, cross-Realm stable correlation keys, IP / geolocation, or untyped free-form text.

ck.profile.push_gateway.matrix_passthrou.description: Interop compatibility profile for Matrix push gateway passthrough. Implementations claiming this profile MAY accept Matrix-shaped push gateway payloads as an external interop bridge to Matrix push gateways but MUST NOT mix this profile with ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 on the same notify path: the Matrix push gateway shape carries identifying fields incompatible with the default Cokret privacy baseline. Bridges MUST partition traffic so that any peer or device negotiated under ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 (i.e. the default v1 baseline) NEVER receives a matrix_passthrough payload. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §5.1 and zh/conformance/conformance-profiles.md §11.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim; bridges that cannot partition traffic MUST NOT claim this profile

additional_requirements.partition_must: Bridges MUST partition push traffic so that Cokret v1 default-baseline peers (ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1) NEVER receive matrix_passthrough-shaped payloads.
additional_requirements.no_default_mixing_must: Implementations MUST NOT advertise both ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 and ck.profile.push_gateway.matrix_passthrough.v1 as applying to the same (recipient_service_did, device) tuple.
additional_requirements.interop_only_must: This profile is interop-only; it MUST NOT be used as a substitute for ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 in default Cokret deployments.

additional_requirements.e2ee_key_source_must: Client binding adapter MUST derive frame keys from Cokret MLS-Exporter with label ck-rtc-frame-key/v1 (length=19 bytes, Context=canonical_json({realm_id, call_id, focus_id, epoch_id, participant_identity, device_id}), KDF.Nh=32 bytes), where participant_identity/device_id come from the verified ck.call.state.participants[] and participant_binding. additional_requirements.recording_pipeline_must: Backend-generated recording artifacts MUST strand through Cokret authenticated blob upload (media-and-blob.md) with recording_initiator_capability_ref. Direct backend-to-storage paths are forbidden (recording_artifact_pipeline_bypassed).

Declaring this sub-profile requires declaring ck.profile.media_service_binding.v1. Optional in v1 cycle; not part of v1 mandatory conformance set. See zh/crypto-media/bindings/livekit.md.

The Account Authority MAY be co-located in the same process/node as the principal server (see architecture.md §2.8) but keeps a distinct service DID and boundary. A deployment MAY delegate to a shared/external auth server, but MUST declare the delegation in service-describe auth_metadata so the inherited trust dependency (control over account recovery, device enrollment, and DID continuity) is explicit and auditable. Sources: overview/architecture.md minimal-deployment topology, sync/service-surface.md §2.5.

additional_requirements.sender_constrained_session_pop_must: Per RFC 9700 (BCP 240) sender-constrained-token guidance, production current-v1 protected endpoints MUST reject bare Authorization: Bearer presentation unless it is bound by DPoP, an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature, detached JWS, mTLS, or equivalent sender-constrained proof. For this high-security profile, regular writes (any request advancing actor_seq / Realm frontier or producing durable side effects) and sensitive reads MUST use RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature whose signing key is the session's session_public_key delegated by ck.session.grant, binding @method/@target-uri/@authority, content-digest (when body present), and participating Idempotency-Key, with created/expires inside the existing replay window. Public metadata surfaces may return only unauthenticated public responses when no valid proof is present; they MUST NOT treat bare bearer as session/capability authentication. See api-conventions.md §3.2 and service-http-binding.md §2.5.
additional_requirements.mls_last_resort_forbidden_must: Realms claiming this profile MUST NOT allow last-resort KeyPackage join: services MUST NOT advertise ck.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1 for those Realms, claim responses MUST NOT return last_resort=true packages, and requesters MUST treat any last_resort=true claim record as profile-forbidden and fail closed.

ck.profile.matrix_compat.v1.description: Optional Matrix interop compatibility profile. Declares wire-shape parity for the Matrix-derived surfaces: to-device queue, /keys/upload|query|claim, push gateway facade, cross-signing key hierarchy, SAS verification message strand. Account-aggregate sync is NOT covered: Cokret v1 chose a streaming push form (ck.self.account.stream.subscribe / GET /account/subscribe with NDJSON frames) over Matrix's long-poll /sync, so wire-shape parity is not claimed for this surface — Matrix clients MUST adapt the account-aggregate consumption loop. Implementations claiming this profile MUST treat the ck.* names of the listed surfaces as semantically equivalent to their Matrix counterparts so that Matrix client SDK code can be reused for those surfaces with only adapter changes. This profile does NOT add new wire fields; it is a conformance assertion about behavioural equivalence on the listed surfaces.

These bare names are not v1 wire Event.kind values. The action remains in the canonical capability registry so prose can reference it stably, but receivers that do not implement this profile MUST treat `ck.realm.join.review` as unknown (capability-action-registry.json registry_rules: 'Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default)'). Claiming the profile commits the implementation to the candidate join-policy workflow surface defined in zh/governance/join-policy.md. This profile is not part of v1 active conformance; it will be promoted with registered `ck.*` Event.kind values when join-policy is formally registered.

ck.profile.circle_seal_cadence.fixed_5m..description: Named cadence profile for confidential Circle sub-seal commitments. Implementations claiming this profile MUST emit ck.circle.seal_commit on a fixed time cadence (5 minutes, max jitter 30 seconds), MUST include empty-batch commitments, and MUST NOT use event-count or activity-triggered public commitments. Mobile energy saving may batch private sub-seal upload, but MUST NOT relax the public Realm seal cadence.

period_ms.rationale: Public Realm seal commitment cadence is fixed at 5 minutes for this profile.

max_jitter_ms.rationale: Bounded scheduling jitter; implementations MUST NOT encode activity by delaying beyond this window.

empty_batch_commitments.rationale: No-activity intervals still emit commitments to avoid leaking activity frequency.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim; confidential Circle deployments MUST NOT claim an event-count cadence as equivalent

ck.profile.cross_signing.reset.v1.description: Hardening profile for high-risk cross-signing reset. Claimants MUST accept ck.cross_signing.reset only with one valid reset proof family, enforce generation monotonicity, clock skew, and replay rejection, and require a successor ck.cross_signing.publish within the recovery window. Verification rules and reason codes are normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4.

max_clock_skew_seconds.rationale: Maximum allowed deviation between `ck.cross_signing.reset.issued_at` and receiver local clock. Default 300s mirrors policy-decision freshness windows; receivers MAY tighten down to 60s for high-assurance deployments or relax up to 900s for federated peers with documented clock skew. Beyond the configured value receivers MUST emit cross_signing_reset_clock_skew_exceeded.

publish_recovery_window_seconds.rationale: Maximum interval after an accepted reset within which the successor ck.cross_signing.publish MUST be observed; receivers MUST otherwise enter the 'no usable SSK/USK' state from §14.2 step 5. Default 24h matches the §14.1 normative requirement.

reset_replay_cache_min_retention_seconds.rationale: Minimum retention for the (principal_id, previous_generation) replay-rejection cache used by §14.4 通用规则. MUST be at least `publish_recovery_window_seconds + 3600` so that no late-arriving duplicate reset can bypass the cache before the successor publish window closes. Default = 24h + 1h slack.

ck.profile.circle_conformance.v1.description: Conformance profile pinning the machine-contract surface for Circle (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary; see zh/models/circle.md). Splits actor submit-payload (scope_circle_id only) from canonical reducer-output (tagged effective_scope on Event envelope + materialized object), and pins the Circle event-kind family, member-state transition table, encryption-profile compatibility, and scope-rebind reducer-reject semantics. Required by implementations that emit or consume Circle events or that materialize Circle-scoped Strand / Message / Morph / Relation / Space objects.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: implementations that cannot enforce canonical reducer-stamped effective_scope MUST NOT claim ck.profile.circle_conformance.v1; receivers MUST treat any unknown Circle event-kind as schema_violation

additional_requirements.submit_payload_must: Submit payload for ck.strand.create / ck.message.create / ck.morph.create / ck.relation.create / ck.space.create / ck.space.parent MUST carry only scope_circle_id (id:circle | null). Reducer MUST reject any submit payload that also carries effective_scope (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed).
additional_requirements.canonical_reducer_output_must: Reducer MUST stamp tagged effective_scope on accepted Event envelope and materialized object cell. effective_scope is immutable per-event; later scope_circle_id rebinds MUST NOT re-interpret historical events.
additional_requirements.scope_rebind_default_reject_must: Default reducer MUST reject scope_circle_id rebind (None<->Some, Some(A)->Some(B)) with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile-declared audit-paired rebind MAY be permitted, but MUST emit ck.audit.accessed pairing.
additional_requirements.circle_encryption_profile_floor_must: Circle.encryption_profile may be none or mls_rfc9420. Reducer MUST reject plaintext Circle creation or update when the parent Realm encryption_profile is mls_rfc9420 or the effective content_encryption_floor is e2ee_required (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor).
additional_requirements.circle_content_encryption_floor_must: Circle.content_encryption_floor (allow_plaintext | e2ee_required) is optional and symmetric with Circle.metadata_encryption_floor: when omitted it inherits the parent Realm content_encryption_floor, and the effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, Circle content_encryption_floor). Reducer MUST reject a Circle floor below the effective floor and MUST reject content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required on an encryption_profile=none Circle (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor). See zh/models/circle.md §7.
additional_requirements.encryption_floor_ratchet_must: The effective content_encryption_floor and effective metadata encryption floor of any scope (Realm-default or Circle) are one-way ratchets: monotonically non-decreasing over time. A ck.realm.policy_components or ck.circle.update that lowers the effective content floor from e2ee_required to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected (reason=content_encryption_floor_downgrade); one that lowers the effective metadata floor MUST be rejected (reason=metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade). Tightening is always allowed. Vectors: ck.vector.e2ee.content_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ck.vector.e2ee.metadata_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ck.vector.circle.content_floor_below_realm_rejected.v1, ck.vector.e2ee.in_place_enable.v1.
additional_requirements.circle_membership_subset_must: Circle.members MUST be a strict subset of parent Realm.members; reducer MUST reject ck.circle.member.state -> join when the target actor is not a `join` member of the parent Realm (reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member).
additional_requirements.scope_invariant_must: Sync Service MUST NOT deliver events with effective_scope.kind=circle to actors not in that Circle's member frontier at the event's causal frontier (see zh/models/circle.md §9.3 scope-delivery invariant).

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ck.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ck.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

actions.notes: Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.
Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.actor_id == envelope.actor_id and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.actor_id != envelope.actor_id.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ck.audit.accessed pair (same model as ck.strand.watch.set.others).

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ck.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ck.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ck.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.

event_mapping_kind_definitions.same_name: Action maps one-to-one to an identically named durable event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.non_event_surface: Action authorizes read/projection/signaling behavior that does not emit a durable reducer event.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.aggregate_admin: Action intentionally covers a bounded administrative family of event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.polymorphic_object: Action covers the same object-lifecycle verb across multiple object event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.scope_suffix_variant: Action adds actor/scope/role qualifiers while reducer admission targets a shared event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.operation_verb: Action token names an operation/command verb that does not match its target event kind name(s); reducer admission resolves the resulting event kind(s) via target_event_kinds. Literal action matching per the actions[] rule applies; carries no aggregate-admin family semantics.

wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.ephemeral_event: Transient sync/federation/app signal; MUST NOT be persisted as durable Event Envelope history.

admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a self-authored proof bound to the subject principal's identity (DID-bound signature / proof of possession with bounded freshness). Reducer MUST verify actor == subject and a fresh, replay-protected proof; no capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing or stale proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-DID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by one or more named capability actions listed in admission_capabilities. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant per capability-action-registry. Fail-closed.

registry_rules: Standard ck.* effect kinds MUST appear in this registry when used by a DataEvent effect, Control Move effect, or Event Envelope payload router.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.
Entries with wire_scope=ephemeral_event MUST be carried only on ephemeral channels and MUST NOT advance Seal coverage, governance state_root, or reducer state.

Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into shared Realm data-plane history or control-plane Seal history.

Reducer-input durable kinds MAY declare cell_family, cell_subject, plane, sealed, lattice, bottom, and (cas_register only) initial_value. cell_family is a stable ck.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, a payload field path, or a composite descriptor; plane MUST be data or control; sealed is a boolean and MUST be true iff plane=control. plane/sealed are the machine-readable authority for DataEvent versus Control Move routing and plane_cross_write validation; payload prose is explanatory. bottom is reject or expose. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any DataEvent or Control Move effect has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` Control Move predicates implements singleton-once-set cells.

Registered exemption: protocol-singleton cells that are not written through a single event_kind are NOT indexed here. Currently the only such cell family is ck.component.notary.v1 (per-Realm notary cell, lattice=cas_register, bottom=reject): its genesis value comes from the ck.realm.create payload notary object and subsequent changes are ordinary notary-finalized Control Moves; its canonical definition lives in zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 4.4. Any future cell family without a single writer kind MUST be added to this exemption list explicitly.

Lattice MUST be one of: core types or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log; or extension types lww_register, rga (only declarable on cells with cell_role in {ui_affordance, content, draft, cosmetic} and only valid for receivers that implement ck.profile.collaborative_text.v1; receivers without that profile MUST fail closed with unsupported_lattice_type when an event_kind references a cell using lww_register or rga). Authorization, policy, notary, membership, and lifecycle cells MUST NOT use lww_register or rga.

State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvent effects are locally accepted against seal_ref, Control Move effects are finalized by Seals, and per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic. Event Envelope routing fields MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

Every active durable reducer-input event_kind MUST have a machine-readable admission source: either at least one capability action targets it (capability_action_registry.target_event_kinds), or it declares an admission class from admission_class_definitions. capability_gated events MUST list the authorizing action(s) in admission_capabilities. Enforced by lint_artifacts.py; no active durable reducer-input event may lack an admission source (fail-closed).

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ck.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.

event_kinds.payload: Organization-authorized Realm relationship statement or revocation

Typed Realm link graph edge. link_kind declares governance / discoverability / import-export / confidential-extension semantics; it is never generic parent/child containment and never implicitly propagates membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Realm preview / peek policy for directory card, stripped state, history stub, and plaintext history snippet projections

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer. payload = {realm_id, strand_id}; reducer projects payload.strand_id into the Realm projection default_strand_id (single authoritative pointer; avoids multi-default dirty state). Reducer MUST verify the referenced strand_id already exists in this Realm (a projected, non-tombstoned Strand); a dangling reference MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. Strand-side is_default is a derived marker (strand_id == realm.default_strand_id), never independent storage; clients discover the default Strand deterministically from the Realm projection default_strand_id or the Strand projection is_default, NOT from any UUID-reuse implementation detail. Authorization is the standard Realm-admin gate (hold ck.realm.admin, or the same-name action ck.realm.set_default_strand).
Enabled Realm policy components set. Payload MUST carry monotonic policy_revision; reducer rejects rollback or gaps and policy_frontier_digest MUST cover policy_revision.

Constraints on member delivery_binding: which binding_source values are admissible, which recipient services are allowed, which endorsers are required, whether DID Document fallback / unroutable membership are permitted, who may sign rebind. Governs reducer acceptance of ck.member.state{membership=join}.delivery_binding (see governance/join-policy.md §5.1).
