Plaintext-visible services declaration outside E2EE boundary
Per-parent inheritance policy; one entry per source Realm
Realm tombstone lifecycle facet (terminal pointer to successor)
Realm destroy lifecycle facet (terminal decommission marker)
Circle create (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary). Initializes independent MLS group and epoch-0 governance binding only when encryption_profile=mls_rfc9420. See zh/models/circle.md §3, §5.
Circle patch (ck.patch.v1 with path NOT containing realm_id / encryption_profile). Modifies title / summary / display / directory_visibility / join_rule / history_visibility.
Circle tombstone (terminal). Triggers lifecycle cascade per zh/models/circle.md §9.2.

Circle membership state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ck.member.state (invite/join/knock/leave/ban), scoped to a Circle. Reducer MUST first validate the target actor is a parent Realm `join` member, otherwise failed_precondition reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member. See zh/models/circle.md §9.1.

Reducer-derived: Circle sub-seal commits opaque sub_seal_head_digest to the Realm Seal stream at the Circle's profile-defined cadence. MUST use time-based ticks + empty-batch commitment to avoid leaking activity frequency. See zh/models/circle.md §10.2.

Issuer-signed endorsement that a subject DID (typically an agent / service / hosted actor) is accountable_principal_ids the issuer for a declared scope (employment / contracted_service / agent_operator / etc.). Required to verify `Actor Profile.accountable_principal_ids[]` entries; reducer strips unverified DIDs from accountable_principal_ids. See zh/models/actor.md §3.3.1.

Notary equivocation evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id plus the two conflicting Seal wire objects: same (realm_id, notary_seq) slot with different canonical bytes, or a notary_seq=k+1 Seal that does not descend from the same signer's notary_seq=k Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1). Admission is verification-only: any Realm member MAY submit and the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted and reducer MUST NOT require one. Reducer MUST re-verify both signatures and the slot rule, then add a per-signer fault record to the notary_fault cell. Once a fault record is accepted: receivers MUST reject later Seals signed by the fault signer, the two conflicting Seals and their descendants enter fork_quarantine, and Realm-wide pause applies only when no eligible signer remains.

Notary censorship evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id, the signed control-plane receipt, the seal_ref of the Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the pending Control Move, a control_event_set_root non-membership proof for the censored event digest, and the missing rejection-or-defer proof (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Admission is verification-only: the receipt holder MAY submit; the receipt signature plus the non-membership proof are the complete authorization. This evidence does NOT automatically disqualify the notary: reducer adds an audit fault record that MUST raise governance alarms, feeds inclusion-list / recovery obligations, and is evaluated by governance or the genesis recovery path.

Realm-scoped MemberIdentity segment replacement event. Append-only log entry that may supersede prior ck.member.identity.update events via payload.replaces[] without overloading ck.profile.update patch semantics.

Strand business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at; ck.strand.update patch on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on the Strand's discussion track that 'references' this event, and the event log's own actor_id / created_at is the audit source. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=strand_already_terminal; state=archived yields strand_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond these hard invariants.

Unified Strand tracks patch. payload.patch uses ck.patch.v1 against the Strand.tracks map: keys are track names (e.g. `synthesis`, `discussion`), values are patch ops that may toggle enabled, set is_primary, or modify profile / metadata on a track entry. Atomic across multiple tracks.

Strand move between Spaces (target_space_id in payload). Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (board_space_id, strand_id); the contains Relation list_space_id->strand_id is derived from cell value, not a separate truth source. Plane ruling (CBA): ck.component.strand.position.v1 defaults to sealed=true (control plane), so ck.strand.move is a Control Move carrying seal_basis; Realm schema MAY redeclare the cell family as data-plane mv_register + user-pick or per-object sequencer per authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.4 and models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6.

Strand reorder within Space. Writes the same cell as ck.strand.move; effect.list_space_id MUST equal head_eq.list_space_id (rank-only update). Plane ruling follows ck.strand.move: same cell family, same default sealed=true control-plane declaration (models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6).

Set or clear a per-(strand, actor) watch subscription. Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (strand_id, watcher_actor_id). Payload carries level in {mentions_only, participating, all, muted} (or null to clear, equivalent to mentions_only). Default invariant: payload.watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope actor_id, unless writer holds ck.strand.watch.set.others. Cross-actor writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ck.audit.accessed event with access_kind=watch_set_others. The watches Relation (actor --watches--> strand) is a derived projection of this cell, not a separate truth source — direct ck.relation.create relation_kind=watches MUST schema_violation. See models/strand-and-message.md §8.

Space metadata update (title, rank, kind-specific fields)

Publish executor MUST atomic-consume the nonce; reuse fails closed (reason=approval_already_consumed).
Controller rejection of a draft / action request (CKP-0008 §4.8.1). Draft transitions to rejected; agent runtime MUST NOT continue publish attempts.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form ck:<kind>:<uuid> unless a special form below applies.

Storage implementations MAY store raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ck:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The UUID segment MUST be RFC 9562 UUID version 7 (48-bit Unix-millisecond timestamp + 4-bit version=7 + 12-bit rand_a + 2-bit variant=10b + 62-bit rand_b), serialized as the canonical 36-character lowercase hex form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-7xxx-Nxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` where N ∈ {8,9,a,b}.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.
special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference; distinct from ck:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.
special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
special_forms.description: Realm-scoped pseudonymous credential reference; validated by the E2EE profile. v1 core uses Realm as the boundary; Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as a content-addressed canonical Seal hash.
Store canonical tuple fields separately when indexing cell state.
Store the scope string as an opaque deployment-level identifier; it appears in server describe, Realm policy, and high-risk proof transcripts.
special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk proofs (e.g. ck.cross_signing.reset §14.1). NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.

id_kinds.description: Moderation appeal ID — opaque key for the ck.component.moderation.appeal.v1 cell. Created by ck.moderation.appeal.submit; referenced by review / decision / close events. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.

Agent interop session ID. Note the cross-surface naming: this typed ID uses the short form `agent_interop_session`, while the corresponding event kinds use the full form `ck.agent.interop_session.{start,status,result}` and capability actions use `ck.agent.interop_session.{start,cancel,stream_status,attach_artifact,read_transcript}`. The three surfaces all refer to the same session concept; downstream tooling MUST NOT assume `ck:<event-prefix>:<uuid>` mechanical derivation.
Directory-local announce ingest record ID. It is typed and UUIDv7-shaped for validator consistency, but it is scoped to the issuing Directory and is not a global federated object authority.
Audit Applet Binding ID. Created by ck.audit.applet_binding and referenced by audit session request/authorize/notice/release events.
Audit release session ID. Threads ck.audit.session.request, authorize, notice, release, and close events for one bounded historical audit window.
Audit release manifest ID. Created by ck.audit.release for a sealed historical release under an active audit binding/session.

Stable identifier for one chain of encrypted backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_class). A pair MAY have multiple series during rotation or migration; the active series is selected by the signed active-series record, not by server return order. Used by ck.schema.key_backup.v1.series_id and recovery strands to detect rollback. See identity/key-management.md §7.6.
Blob metadata row ID; content-addressed blobs use the special digest form

SFU-local participant handle (CKP-0010). Scope limited to `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`; derived from `(realm_id, call_id, focus_id, device_id, issuer_service_did, issued_at_bucket)` by the media service token issuer. MUST NOT carry any actor-identifying material; only appears in `ck.call.state.participants[].participant_identity` and in `participant_binding`. The wire value MUST use the canonical UUIDv7-shaped `ck:rtc_participant:<uuid>` form; implementations MAY derive the random bits from the media-service token input, but the version and variant nibbles MUST satisfy the UUIDv7 pattern.
Abstract capability definition reference ID; signed grant objects use ck:grant:<uuid>.

Circle object ID — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. See zh/models/circle.md.

Device identifier (ck:device:<uuid>). A device is a typed ID scoped to an owning principal, NOT a DID and NOT an actor principal. Device keys are registered as verification methods under the owning principal DID via ck.device.authorize.
Signed capability grant object ID used by ck.schema.capability.v1 and grant/revoke references.

Stable session identifier bound by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof and MLS Welcome replay during one recovery strand. Referenced by ck.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 and by §15 recovery proofs. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Space object ID — structural grouping object inside a Realm (board, list, swimlane, calendar bucket, etc.). Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership / policy / E2EE group; resolves to the containing Realm.
Realm object ID — security / sync / auth / E2EE boundary. Always carries membership, policy, history_visibility, MLS group binding, and federation policy.

operation_registry.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Cokret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see capability_tiers); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>. The kind segment MUST be one of query, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex query body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (query/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

capability_tiers.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Cokret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
capability_tiers.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Cokret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
capability_tiers.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Cokret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
capability_tiers.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

operations.notes: Managed-DID (account-authority) device enrollment, device-lifecycle.md §5.4 / key-management.md §5.0.6. The authenticated session asks its designated enrollment authority to mint a service_attested ck.device.authorize for this session's own device; the authority signs with its persistent enrollment key (never the principal SSK) and returns the full Event. The caller submits it verbatim to POST /_cokret/self/events. Distinct from pair_device (§2.1), which lands an existing-device SAS/QR approval and carries a pairing_code; enroll_device is the bootstrap / first-device path where no sibling device can approve.

Account Authority single-call grant exchange. The response is the client-visible SessionGrantOutcome; any Principal-side local session provisioning is internal to the Account Authority. There is no separate client-visible grant-to-bearer exchange step: the client presents the returned ck.session.grant directly to /_cokret/self/* with a DPoP proof (api-conventions §3.3). For proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange, the Account Authority exchanges the authorization code at the issuer token_endpoint and validates issuer/state/nonce/redirect_uri/principal/device/audience binding before issuing the grant; the client MAY omit principal_id at first sign-in, in which case the Account Authority derives/mints the principal DID and returns it in SessionGrantOutcome.principal_id.

DPoP-bound session-grant rotation (account-lifecycle §4.1, device-lifecycle §3.3). An authorized device presents a DPoP holder proof for the grant's cnf.jkt plus a fresh DID/device proof bound to principal_id, device_id, audience, request_canonical_digest, challenge, issued_at, and expires_at; expires_at - issued_at MUST be <=300s. The old grant is single-use revoked. Account Authority-local op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): the Account Authority has already validated the client-visible ck.gate.account.command.logout request, then calls this operation with service-to-service authentication to log out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the presented ck.session.grant and terminate that session's grant rotation chain. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they only call ck.gate.account.command.logout. HTTP-only S2S op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Principal Server validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and optional S2S holder confirmation) and learns whether it is active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Principal Server can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_cokret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); clients do not send a separate introspection-proof header on self-path requests. session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. Authenticated by the configured session_grant_introspection_bearer (server-local); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The handler validates the current ck.session.grant + DPoP, terminates the Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain through ck.gate.account.command.logout_auth_session when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Probe the public ck.agent.endpoint registry for an agent's declared external protocol endpoints; returns the projection of an accepted ck.agent.endpoint event (no controller-private fields). Authorized by the ck.agent.protocol.discover capability action (profile ck.profile.agent_runtime.v1). See agent-protocol-interop.md §5.1 / §11 / §12.

Optional Account Authority browser redirect landing / handoff for deployments that use an OIDC redirect URI under /_cokret/gate/account. It MUST NOT issue or return SessionGrantOutcome, ck.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance remains ck.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant.

source_signature_anchor.node_to_applet: Source-Service-DID current service DID verification method; Destination-Service-DID MUST equal the Applet registration service_did.
source_signature_anchor.applet_to_cokret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; DID part MUST equal Source-Service-DID and the active effective install service_did.

operations.notes: Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. HTTP binding is POST because the request is a batch command against a queue collection, deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key), and does not replace a single URI-addressed message resource. Queue pruning is only via ck.self.device_messages.command.ack.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages from=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.
Writes requester-side ck.contact.requested fact and requester-side consent grants for requested scopes; MUST NOT write target consent or accepted fact.
Target-side accept/reject of a contact request. Accept writes target-controlled consent grants; reject writes no consent.
Holder contact projection from contact facts plus consent-derived directional scopes; account-data contact notes are local decoration only.
Holder-side contact tombstone. Default revocation is limited to contact-managed active consent dots.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ck.self.contact.command.tombstone(block_peer) blocked_subjects writes.
Idempotent resolver for accepted contacts. Requires accepted contact projection and direct_message consent; create=true creates canonical DM Realm, main Strand, and binding.

Builds a ck.circle.create Operation in the named parent Realm and routes it through the local accept pipeline. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_ref, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor permits plaintext.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Builds ck.circle.member.state. Activating another actor requires ck.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule.
Builds ck.circle.member.state with membership=leave for the path actor_id.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.
Builds ck.circle.archive; transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_active).

Builds ck.circle.restore; transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_archived). Restore re-enables new writes after pending MLS membership removals are settled.
Builds ck.circle.tombstone (terminal). Response surfaces the terminal state with empty members.

Resource-side appeal against an operator takedown. The appeal packet MUST bind takedown_id, resource id, appellant DID, argument/evidence digest, requested_outcome and created_at, signed by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate; the Directory returns a signed decision receipt. See discovery-directory.md §8.7.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ck.events.query. Semantically identical (same selector / cursor / order / filter / include_completeness parameter set, same response shape including optional range_completeness). Choose when URL length would exceed practical limits (large realms[]/actors[] arrays, complex filters object) or when query parameters would be logged inadvertently by proxies. Non-HTTP transports MUST use the canonical ck.self.events.query.scan binding (SelfEvents/Query / self.events.query.scan), not expose this variant as a separate gRPC or MQ operation.
Dereference a known set of event_id / event_digest references to full EventEnvelope objects. Point lookup by identifier, not a range scan — use ck.self.events.query.scan for selector-based reads.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Durable self event submission, including ck.invite.claim. For ck.invite.claim, the receiving Realm reducer is the authoritative state machine: it MUST match token_commitment, re-check verification_service_did allowlist against current Realm policy, reject claim_nonce replay, perform pending -> claimed / membership-proposal effects, and run expiry cleanup before accepting.
Federation peer Events surface describe. This endpoint describes the server-to-server peer event bindings; it is not a client self/events binding.

Federation peer frontier probe. Requires service-to-service authentication, Source/Destination service DID headers, trust-domain headers, and Realm federation_peer authorization. It returns the federation peer frontier response shape on the dedicated peer trust surface.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ck.self.events.query.scan, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ck.peer.events.query.scan. Semantically identical to GET /_cokret/peer/events; use it when federation selectors or filters are too large or sensitive for query strings.

Federation peer event reference resolution for missing prev_refs / causal references. Requires authorized federation peer service authentication and applies the same reference-disclosure and history-visibility rules as peer event query.

Federation peer event push. Body is EventsSubmitFederationRequestBody and the caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers. Federated ck.invite.claim events are still decided by the destination Realm reducer, which MUST enforce token_commitment, current allowlist re-check, claim_nonce replay rejection, membership proposal conversion, and expiry cleanup; peer ingress prechecks are not state authority.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-DID equal to invite_address.recipient_service_did, a ck.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server contact fact delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-DID equal to contact_address.recipient_service_did, and a signed ck.contact.* envelope the recipient projects into the target holder's contact projection without re-signing.
Federation peer snapshot manifest head for snapshot-assisted bootstrap. Requires service-to-service authentication and Realm federation_peer authorization.

Canonical broadcast ephemeral send operation for ck.schema.ephemeral_envelope.v1. Carries ck.presence, ck.typing, ck.receipt.read, and ck.call.signal; MUST NOT persist the signal as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Media service token exchange operation (CKP-0010). Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ck.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend types (livekit / mediasoup / janus / cokret-native); only backend_token shape is type-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Read the currently accepted ck.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Publish a signed ck.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation for the authenticated principal. HTTP binding is POST because the principal/authority is derived from authenticated proof and signed policy state rather than a URI-addressed resource slot. Servers MUST verify auth_data.signed_fields, signature authority, version monotonicity, and supersedes linkage before accepting.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.
Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_cokret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version is negotiated via *.describe / supported_operations (see sync/api-conventions.md).
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ck.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Builds a ck.realm.link Move from realm_id -> target_realm_id. The reducer runs realm_link_* validators (cycle detection, self-reference, kind validation); a rejected payload returns 422 with the canonical reason code (e.g. realm_link_cycle, realm_link_self_reference).

Writes a tombstoning ck.realm.link Move (status=tombstoned) for the (realm_id, target_realm_id, link_kind) triple. link_kind defaults to governed_by; callers may override via the link_kind query param.

Returns the merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ck.realm.inheritance_policy. inheritance_mode=none when no inheritance policy is projected (implicit inheritance is forbidden).

Returns the projected ck.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organizations hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hints are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.
Reads the projected ck.realm.policy_server config. Returns not_found when neither the Realm nor its governed_by ancestor chain declared one. from_org_fallback=true marks an inherited config.

Builds a ck.realm.policy_server Move (admission capability ck.policy.manage). Reducer validates URL scheme and on_timeout enum. This admin DTO is a simplified projection of the canonical payload (server_id/endpoint/public_keys/applies_to/fail_mode).
Tombstones the per-Realm ck.realm.policy_server cell so callers fall back to the governed_by chain or local-only capability check. Empty success response.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Builds a ck.realm.archive Move. The archived facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; archived=false clears the archived facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies.

Builds a ck.realm.freeze Move. The frozen facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; frozen=true rejects ordinary non-exempt writes with realm_frozen and frozen=false clears the freeze facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies.

Builds a terminal ck.realm.tombstone Move with a successor_realm_id. The tombstoned state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state.
Builds a terminal ck.realm.destroy Move. The destroyed state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ck.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.
Returns the organization-inherited effective moderation policy view: inheritance chain, organization policy layers, the Realm's own override, and merged effective rules.

Writes a Realm moderation-policy override (ck.realm.moderation_policy). Only the Realm owner may write; an override that loosens an action an organization policy denies requires explicit organization approval embedded in the document, otherwise the server returns requires_organization_approval.
Lists holder-private consent cells where the caller is holder or peer. Each cell projects the current effective consent for a (holder, peer, consent_scope).
Reads one consent cell. Requires peer and consent_scope query params; caller MUST be holder or that peer. Returns not_found when no cell exists.
Builds a ck.consent.grant Control Move on the holder's consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (holder or an explicitly authorized controller/agent).

Builds a ck.consent.revoke Control Move enumerating the active grant dots for the (consent_id, peer, consent_scope). Revoking consent_scope=any cascades all concrete scopes; revoking a concrete scope leaves others intact.
Opens a pending consent request from the authenticated peer to a holder. peer_did defaults to and MUST equal the authenticated actor; the holder account MUST exist.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.
Reads one account_data entry by data_type key. Returns not_found when the key is unset.

Builds a ck.account_data.set actor-private write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.
Deletes one account_data entry and fans out an actor-private update to the holder's other devices.

Builds a ck.read_cursor.advance actor-private write for (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope, position). Multi-device convergence is by HLC max with device_id tiebreak; the cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Space lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface that materializes a View{kind=collection} projection such as board/list/table/calendar. The response is a derived read model computed from signed Events, reducer profile, View definition, and the returned frontier; it is not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Holder-bound service wrapper around ck.profile.update / Actor Profile projection. Request body is a closed patch over display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>; profile_fields.bio is the canonical personal bio field and avatar_url is not accepted on the Cokret protocol path.

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, presence, unread / notification counts). Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available. Symmetric with ck.self.events.stream.subscribe — both are streaming subscriptions, differing only in scope (self.events.stream.subscribe = per-Realm event log; self.account.stream.subscribe = account-aggregate). `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same principal/device/filter scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After. Presence changes are sent through ck.self.ephemeral.command.send, not this read-only stream subscription.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ck.self.device_messages.command.ack.

success_shape_kind_definitions.service_describe: ServiceDescribe object returned by a describe endpoint.
success_shape_kind_definitions.schema_resource: Response body is a canonical artifact JSON Schema resource.
success_shape_kind_definitions.inline_response: Endpoint-specific inline object schema in OpenAPI.
success_shape_kind_definitions.operation_result: Generic OperationResult envelope; operation row MUST carry generic_binding.
success_shape_kind_definitions.event_stream: Long-lived event stream rather than a single JSON success body.
success_shape_kind_definitions.metadata_headers: Metadata-only success expressed through HTTP headers.

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ck.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ck.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

actions.notes: Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.
Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.actor_id == envelope.actor_id and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.actor_id != envelope.actor_id.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ck.audit.accessed pair (same model as ck.strand.watch.set.others).

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ck.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ck.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ck.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.

event_mapping_kind_definitions.same_name: Action maps one-to-one to an identically named durable event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.non_event_surface: Action authorizes read/projection/signaling behavior that does not emit a durable reducer event.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.aggregate_admin: Action intentionally covers a bounded administrative family of event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.polymorphic_object: Action covers the same object-lifecycle verb across multiple object event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.scope_suffix_variant: Action adds actor/scope/role qualifiers while reducer admission targets a shared event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.operation_verb: Action token names an operation/command verb that does not match its target event kind name(s); reducer admission resolves the resulting event kind(s) via target_event_kinds. Literal action matching per the actions[] rule applies; carries no aggregate-admin family semantics.

registry/digest-suite-registry.json.description: Canonical digest suite vocabulary for v1 typed digest values. A digest suite is the registered tuple (canonicalization, hash_algorithm). The suite canonical_id is the wire prefix in `<suite>:<lowercase_hex>` typed digest values and the value space of the Realm `digest_algorithm` field.
registry/digest-suite-registry.json.suite_id_grammar: suite_id = hash_id | canonicalization_id '.' hash_id ; each segment matches [a-z0-9_]+ ; at most one dot. A bare hash_id (no dot) denotes canonicalization=json_jcs for historical wire compatibility.
registry_rules: A digest suite id without a dot denotes canonicalization=json_jcs (canonical JSON per zh/conformance/encoding.md §2). The bare ids sha256/blake3 are therefore JSON-canonicalization suites; their wire semantics are unchanged from earlier v1 drafts and existing signed bytes are unaffected.

Suites are registered as explicit tuples. Implementations MUST NOT combine canonicalization ids and hash ids freely; only suites present as rows in this registry exist, and only status=active rows are valid on wire.

A suite prefix not present as an active row MUST fail closed with unsupported_digest_algorithm when it appears in a critical field (event_digest, state_root, prev_refs / refs digest, seal id, receipt digest); in non-critical metadata receivers MAY record it as unknown and preserve raw bytes (zh/conformance/encoding.md §3.2).
status=reserved rows pin the wire prefix and profile gate but MUST NOT appear on wire until every activation_requirements entry is met and the row is flipped to active in a registry release.

Realm digest_algorithm MUST hold exactly one active suite id; every digest produced inside that Realm MUST use the declared suite. A digest whose suite prefix differs from the Realm's declared suite MUST be rejected (schema_violation), except on a Transition Seal's previous_state_root. Suite transition only via ck.profile.hash_transition.v1 (zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.2).
Schema enum values for digest-suite selector fields (e.g. realm.digest_algorithm) MUST be generated from active rows' canonical_id.

The hash_strength_order below is consumed by the suite-transition no-downgrade rule and applies to the hash_algorithm component only; canonicalization component changes are lateral and carry no strength relation.

The registry is intentionally minimal: new hash algorithms (e.g. SHA-3 family for algorithm diversity, post-quantum hash families) and new canonicalizations enter additively as new rows with their own profile gates and conformance vectors; the <suite>:<hex> wire form needs no rewrite. KDF/ciphersuite algorithm selectors elsewhere in the spec (e.g. key-backup PBKDF2 digest_algorithm, VOPRF SHA-512) are separate value spaces and are NOT digest suites.

hash_strength_order.note: Performance-side order; v1 treats registered hashes as equal collision strength. Extended when post-quantum or diversity hashes are registered.

canonicalizations.definition: Cokret canonical JSON (RFC 8785 / JCS narrowed profile), zh/conformance/encoding.md §2.
canonicalizations.notes: Implied by bare (dot-free) suite ids; never written as an explicit dotted prefix segment in v1.

canonicalizations.definition: CBOR deterministic encoding (RFC 8949 §4.2) under the Cokret profile to be pinned by ck.profile.encoding.cbor.v1 (encoding rules, CDDL, schema-agnostic JSON<->CBOR type mapping, conformance vectors).
canonicalizations.notes: Reserved until ck.profile.encoding.cbor.v1 is fully specified. The mapping MUST be schema-agnostic (JSON string -> CBOR text string, JSON integer -> CBOR integer); canonicalization MUST NOT depend on schema knowledge.

suites.security_note: v1 default; all receivers MUST support. SHA-2 family, not post-quantum but Grover-degraded strength remains acceptable; migration path via suite transition.
Best throughput (parallelizable); recommended for blob CID and high-volume paths.

activation_requirements: ck.profile.encoding.cbor.v1 fully specified: deterministic encoding rules pinned by directly adopting an upstream standardized deterministic CBOR profile (CDE, draft-ietf-cbor-cde, or dCBOR, draft-mcnally-deterministic-cbor) under draft-pinning discipline (draft change = new profile version) rather than a bespoke ruleset, CDDL for envelope and canonical objects, schema-agnostic JSON<->CBOR type mapping
Per-suite conformance vectors published (canonical bytes, event_digest, state_root, receipt digest)
Suite transition vectors published for json_jcs -> cbor transition Seals
suites.security_note: Deterministic CBOR canonicalization with SHA-256. Same hash strength as sha256; the suite exists to enable encode-once/sign-the-bytes verification and MLS/COSE ecosystem alignment for Realms that opt in at create time.

codes.description: JSON body cannot be parsed.
Query parameters cannot be parsed or violate endpoint rules.
Parsed input does not satisfy the declared schema contract.
A required parameter is missing.
A parameter value is syntactically or semantically invalid.

A downstream service response was syntactically valid transport data but did not satisfy the expected protocol contract, including directory/projection/service-call schema mismatch or missing required pagination/error fields.
Authentication material is missing or invalid.
Session, token, or grant has expired.
Session-grant rotation targeted a grant that was already single-use consumed (rotated). Treated as a credential-compromise signal; the rotation chain SHOULD be terminated. See account-lifecycle §4.1.

Session-grant rotation refused because the underlying Auth Server browser session has been logged out (finished). The rotation chain cannot be resumed; full re-authentication is required. See account-lifecycle §4.1.
Session-grant rotation requested an audience different from the grant's bound audience. Audience MUST NOT change across rotation.
Session was soft-logged-out and must be refreshed.
The principal account is locked. Existing session grants are invalidated and protected requests MUST fail closed; new session issuance MAY surface the same code with a 403 policy-denial status.
The principal account is suspended. Existing sessions may observe account state where permitted, but new session issuance and writes MUST fail closed with this code.
The principal account is deactivated. Existing session grants are invalidated and protected requests MUST fail closed; new session issuance MAY surface the same code with a 403 policy-denial status.

The principal account is in terminal erasure_pending state. Existing session grants are invalidated and protected requests MUST fail closed with this code instead of a generic unauthenticated response.
A soft-logout refresh, OIDC callback, re-auth, or sensitive account transition requires a fresh DID-bound or authorized-device proof; a refresh token alone is insufficient.
A required signature or proof does not verify.

A service-to-service request that MUST carry a per-delivery RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature presented only Authorization: Bearer with no Signature. Applies to Applet transaction push in both directions (node->Applet and app/bridge->cokret edge inbound). See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §7.3.1.

A per-delivery RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature failed verification, Content-Digest did not cover the canonical body, or source_service_did disagreed with the Source-Service-DID header / signature transcript. See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §7.3.1.

A per-delivery HTTP Message Signature created/expires parameters fell outside the protocol freshness window (expires-created over 300s, created skew over +/-30s, or expires already past), including byte-identical replays after the bounded replay cache evicted the entry. Window judged per zh/sync/federation.md §3.2. See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §7.3.1.
Directory ingest rejected an announce or withdraw because the signed resource payload does not authorize this Directory service DID.
Directory ingest rejected the resource because it is outside the directory's advertised accept policy.
Directory ingest rejected a resource governance proof because its detached signature is invalid or cannot be canonicalized.
Directory ingest rejected a signed payload because its as_of timestamp is outside the configured freshness window.
Directory ingest or cross-service projection could not verify declared source_refs against the authoritative principal server, resource source, or signed projection frontier.
Directory ingest rejected a governance proof because the signing key is not valid for the resource DID document's current epoch.
A service-call TTL is outside the operation's allowed range, including directory ttl_seconds outside [1, max_ttl_seconds] or ephemeral ttl_ms beyond the advertised kind-specific limit.
Directory ingest rejected an announce because an active withdrawal or operator takedown blocks acceptance of the resource.
Directory ingest rejected an announce because policy_revision or as_of is older than the indexed entry.
Capability, policy, or visibility rules deny the request.
The target Realm is frozen, archived, tombstoned, or otherwise closed to ordinary writes.
A required claim, attestation, or presentation is missing.
A realm-level policy refuses the requested write or fanout (read-receipts §2.5: ck.receipt.read drops when disclosure='disabled'; retry_after_ms is null because retry will not change the outcome).

A Realm, organization, account, holder-disclosure, agent, or deployment policy explicitly denied the requested operation after syntactic validation and authentication succeeded. Use a narrower code when a more specific registry entry applies.

A child Realm's read-receipt policy attempted to cross the parent's compliance floor (parent disclosure='required' → child 'optional' or 'disabled') without the parent explicitly setting allow_child_privacy_tightening_against_required=true. Reducer MUST reject the offending ck.realm.read_receipt_policy Move with this wire code. See zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5.
ck.self.ephemeral.command.send rejected the envelope because the actor lacks the kind-specific broadcast capability or Realm policy disables that ephemeral kind.
ck.self.ephemeral.command.send rejected ttl_ms because it is absent when required or outside the service's advertised kind-specific range.
ck.self.ephemeral.command.send could not enqueue or fan out the transient signal because the ephemeral channel is temporarily unavailable; durable Event history is not affected.
The target does not exist or is not visible to the requester.
The path is inside the protocol namespace but not implemented by the service.
The path exists but the HTTP method is not supported.
A generic state conflict occurred.
An optimistic concurrency precondition failed.
Causal dependencies, prev_refs, refs[role=authorized_by], or actor-chain constraints are violated.
A required dependency is missing and may be recoverable via backfill or retry.
The target Strand discussion track is disabled.
The referenced encryption epoch is stale or unavailable.
The same idempotency key or stable identifier was reused with different canonical content.
No valid fractional rank exists between the requested bounds; a rebalance or different position is required.
The producer cannot allocate a fresh HLC logical counter in the current millisecond without violating monotonicity.
The request or blob exceeds declared size limits.
A declared digest does not match the transferred content.
Encrypted envelope AAD digest does not match the canonical normalized AAD.
Encrypted payload digest does not match the declared encrypted envelope content.
Required encrypted content key, MLS epoch, or authorized key share is not currently available.
Encrypted content or MLS epoch is bound to an application state root that cannot be verified against accepted state.
An auditable E2EE decrypt receipt was invalidated by backfill, witness, or state verification.
A DID cannot be resolved or validated under the active resolver policy.
Storage, bandwidth, or compute quota was exceeded.
A semantic protocol limit was exceeded even though the request body itself may be well-formed, such as a bounded recurrence expansion that cannot be returned within the v1 maximum result count.
The caller exceeded the current rate limit policy.
A wait-for, long-poll, or upstream dependency timed out.
The service frontier is behind the causal frontier required by the request.

A federation high-assurance peer has missed proactive frontier probes or produced invalid/divergent frontier evidence and is quarantined for the affected Realm until fork resolution succeeds. See zh/sync/federation.md §4.5.3.

A pending write, cache entry, snapshot claim, or downstream grant depends on a grant that has been revoked, superseded, expired, or revoked through an ancestor grant. The dependent action MUST fail closed or be quarantined until re-authorized.
Device recovery proof or authorization references an SSK generation that does not equal the current accepted cross-signing publish generation for the principal.
The opaque cursor (ck:cursor:...) has a valid shape but its `x` expiry is in the past. Client MUST request a fresh cursor (initial /account/subscribe, /snapshot/head, or new write barrier).

Cursor integrity check failed for the v1 stateful opaque handle (client-sync §12.1, canonical body `{v, purpose, t, x, h}`): the `h` handle is unknown / revoked / expired / cross-bound, or its stored binding (principal, device, service, filter_digest, purpose) does not match the authenticated request. Distinct from cursor_expired (TTL) and cursor_unrecognized (cross-service portability miss). Client MUST clear local cursor cache and restart from initial /account/subscribe.

Cursor integrity is valid but the issuing service has explicitly revoked this cursor authority before TTL expiry. Endpoint MUST NOT advance subscription position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state; caller MUST restart from a fresh cursor. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors and unaffected (client-sync.md §10.1).
The cursor decoded successfully but cannot be used by this service because it is a stateful handle issued by another service. Caller MUST restart sync from a fresh cursor.
Event submission rejected an actor chain sequence number that is duplicate, skipped without allowed repair evidence, or inconsistent with the actor frontier.
The supplied seal_ref, seal_basis, or frontier token is older than the freshness window required for this operation or policy tier.
The supplied seal_ref or seal_basis leaf does not identify a Seal known to the receiving service for the target Realm.
A token, invite, notification, or delivery request names an audience that is unknown or not visible to the caller.
Blob upload, head, download, or presign verification found that the transferred content digest does not match the declared digest.
The referenced blob, upload slot, or presigned blob authority has expired.
A blob presign request or presigned URL token is malformed, out of policy, expired, or fails integrity checks.
The blob operation exceeds actor, Realm, organization, or deployment storage/bandwidth quota.
The supplied cursor fails syntax, schema, purpose, binding, or integrity validation before the operation can advance state.

A service-attested ck.device.authorize names an executed_by / authority_did that is not designated as an enrollment authority by the principal DID document (resolved at the event's accepted-at), or its authorization_ref delegation does not cover device authorization.
The referenced device id is unknown, not visible, or no longer active for the target principal.
A DID operation attempted to create or register a DID that already exists under the registry's uniqueness rules.
The requested DID cannot be found under the active identity registry and anti-enumeration policy.
The requested DID exists in historical registry state but has been deactivated, revoked, or superseded.
The service cannot currently produce the requested frontier because required seal, reducer, or witness state is unavailable.
A handle or alias exists but lacks a verifiable current claim binding for the requested operation.
A key upload, claim, consume, or device-message operation reuses one-time key material or a claim nonce outside the allowed single-use window.
An MLS KeyPackage claim/consume/revoke operation targeted a KeyPackage that has already been consumed by a Welcome.
The referenced MLS KeyPackage is unknown, expired, revoked, or not visible to the caller under the active claim policy.
No suitable one-time key or KeyPackage remains available for the requested device, principal, cipher suite, or profile.
The request depends on policy state older than the freshness window required for this operation or risk tier.
The policy service, policy frontier, or policy proof required for this operation is temporarily unavailable.
The referenced principal DID or account principal is unknown or not visible to the caller.
The push gateway or downstream push provider could not be reached or is unavailable for this route.
The notification payload exceeds the push profile, provider, or deployment size limit.
The requested push target, device route, or notification subscription is unknown or no longer visible.
The supplied push token is malformed, fails provider validation, or is not bound to the authenticated principal/device.
The push token or registration id is unknown, revoked, expired, or already unregistered.
The submitted item or operation result was quarantined by moderation, abuse, fork, policy, or risk handling and is not accepted as ordinary visible state.
The snapshot issuer, witness quorum, or signing authority cannot be verified for the requested Realm and manifest time.
The requested snapshot head or snapshot artifact is not currently available from this service.
A subscription stream dropped events or account updates and the client must follow the server-directed recovery path.
A subscription stream cannot safely continue from the supplied cursor; the client must resync from a fresh cursor or snapshot.
Generic request, query, batch, or envelope size limit exceeded. More specific blob/push/payload variants may be used when available.
The DID method is syntactically valid but not supported by the active identity registry or resolver policy.
The requested media, call, recording, or SFU policy is not supported by the service or negotiated media profile.

SDP / ICE media negotiation failed after the request passed authorization and schema validation. Clients MAY retry with a fresh offer or rejoin flow; services MUST NOT treat this as authorization success for any durable call-state transition.
A required protocol feature is not supported.
The service does not accept the requested active standard Event kind.
The operation is registered but this deployment has not implemented the endpoint or binding.
The requested projection cannot be claimed complete under the current supported feature set or dependency frontier.
An internal service error occurred.
The service is temporarily unavailable or cannot currently satisfy the request.
The service or a required upstream dependency is unavailable; callers MAY retry according to Retry-After / next_retry_at when provided.

The submitted Realm policy combination (discoverability × join_rule × history_visibility) violates the v1 normative compatibility matrix in zh/discovery/discovery-directory.md §3.1. Reducer keeps the prior accepted state.

A Realm or Circle attempted to use history_visibility=restricted, or to authorize a restricted history/key-share range, without an effective ck.realm.history_sharing_policy covering the target scope. Reducers and key sources MUST fail closed. See zh/governance/history-visibility.md.

The requested Event range, backfill window, preview field, or E2EE history key share is not visible to the caller under the target Event's T0 history_visibility and the current safety policy. Non-enumerating surfaces MAY map this to not_found. See zh/governance/history-visibility.md.

A directory/resolve/search/projection request attempted to obtain a stripped preview, history stub, history snippet, or token-scoped preview that is not allowed by the effective ck.realm.preview_policy. External responses that must be non-enumerating MAY map this to not_found. See zh/governance/history-visibility.md §4.
Realm create rejected: notary_profile=single_did was declared without a recovery_notary in a different controlling organization, in violation of zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.
The implementation does not support a lattice type referenced by the Realm schema (e.g., lww_register or rga without ck.profile.collaborative_text.v1). Receivers fail closed.

Caller requested an operation that relies on a Realm-declared profile or feature this service has not declared in ck.server.query.describe.supported_features / supported_profiles. The server MUST fail-closed and MUST NOT silently downgrade to a permissive interpretation.

A third-party (3PID) invite claim targeted a join-rule Realm whose continuation profile is outside v1 base conformance (e.g. knock_restricted) and the deployment has not declared the required candidate profile in ck.find.directory.query.describe / ck.account.describe. The verification service MUST reject the token claim instead of silently downgrading. See zh/sync/third-party-invites.md §4.3.

Reducer state-machine precondition failed. Carried with a reason_code in the {strand,space,morph}_not_active / _not_archived family or the {strand,space,morph,message,relation}_already_terminal family, or with object-specific reasons like space_parent_cycle. See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.1.

CBA plane invariant failed: a Control Move's effects[] wrote a data-plane cell, or an Event violated a hard data-schema plane invariant. Terminal failure state; the write MUST NOT be bypassed as cas_conflict. See zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §13 and zh/sync/service-http-binding.md (write outcomes).
CBA lattice join produced bottom (irreconcilable state) for the event's effects. Terminal failure state per zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §13; MUST NOT be reported as cas_conflict.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when ck.self.direct_conversation.command.resolve is called for a peer without an accepted contact projection, or after the requester has tombstoned that contact. Consent alone is not sufficient for the contact direct-conversation resolver. See zh/identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when ck.self.direct_conversation.command.resolve has an accepted contact but cannot verify target-holder active consent_scope=direct_message or any for the requester. See zh/identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md and zh/identity/consent-model.md §6.2.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when ck.self.direct_conversation.command.resolve (create=true) cannot resolve the peer DID to a valid principal / control state, so no KeyPackage claim or Realm create is attempted. See zh/identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md §6.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when ck.self.contact.command.respond attempts to accept or reject a request that has already been accepted, rejected, tombstoned, withdrawn, or otherwise left the pending state.

Sub-reason for failed_precondition when ck.self.contact.command.respond targets a contact request older than contact_request_pending_ttl. The request projection is expired and requester-side contact-managed consent must be revoked.

The digest suite prefix in a typed digest value (e.g. sha256:<hex>, cbor.sha256:<hex>) is not an active row of artifacts/registry/digest-suite-registry.json supported by the receiver (unknown id, unregistered tuple, or reserved suite) on a critical field. See zh/conformance/encoding.md §3.1-§3.2. Dual-registered (also a reason_code): all three algorithm-agility fail-closed errors (unsupported_digest_algorithm / unsupported_signature_alg / unsupported_hpke_suite) appear in both `codes` (top-level service error) and `reason_codes` (per-item sub-reason); see zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §1.1.1.

Proof / event signature `alg` is not in the conformance signature-algorithm allowlist (artifacts/registry/signature-alg-registry.json) on a critical field. One of the three algorithm-agility fail-closed errors; dual-registered as a service code and a reason_code (see unsupported_digest_algorithm). See zh/conformance/encoding.md §6.1.

HPKE suite id on an application-layer sealed surface is not an active row of artifacts/registry/hpke-suite-registry.json (unknown, inactive, or reserved-but-not-activated). One of the three algorithm-agility fail-closed errors; dual-registered as a service code and a reason_code (see unsupported_digest_algorithm). Receivers MUST fail closed rather than infer suite parameters from the AEAD name. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5.2.
Seal coverage has gaps within the receiver's control auth-chain backfill bound; soft-fail per zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md.
E2EE franking proof cannot be produced for the requested ciphertext (sender did not include franking sidecar). See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.4.
TURN REST-style ephemeral credential is past its TTL; client MUST request a fresh credential. See zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §4.1.
Federation sender used an obsolete member delivery binding frontier; response carries new_recipient_service_did and handover_frontier so the sender can retry at the current service.
Federation sender continued using a previous recipient_service_did after the handover grace window expired; sender MUST resolve the current binding and retry there.

An accepted member delivery binding could not be resolved to a reachable recipient_service_did after the bounded retry limit; sender MUST NOT fall back to the DID Document CokretPrincipalServer entry. Surfaced to the upstream sender as a diagnostic after the second failure so it can quarantine pending events and await rebind. See zh/governance/join-policy.md §5.1.4.
Idempotency cache replay is served only as a historical diagnostic after key or binding state changed; receivers MUST NOT perform new reducer side effects.

An Applet registration or transaction attempted to enter a Realm without an explicit grant from the Realm owner, Realm admin, or Realm-policy-authorized registry/authz service. Namespace claims and self-signed applet registration are insufficient. See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §4.

ck.self.applet.command.install recomputed the canonical InstallPlan from the submitted Applet Package, approved_scopes, effective_scope, and current Realm/Circle policy, and the recomputed plan_digest did not exactly match the submitted plan_digest. Server MUST fail closed and require a fresh preview/approval before fan-out. See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §4b.

An Applet, bot actor, or Applet-managed Ghost Actor attempted to join an E2EE Realm / MLS group without the independent E2EE join authorization required by ck.profile.applet_e2ee_join.v1. Ordinary message/write capability grants do not imply MLS join authority. See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §12.

A revoked effective Applet install attempted a future write, transaction push side effect, delegated action, widget token use, or E2EE join. Reducers and service-call handlers MUST fail closed after ck.self.applet.command.revoke / ck.capability.revoke has taken effect. See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §4b.

`ck.self.account.command.update_profile` received an `avatar_blob_ref` that is not a valid Cokret Blob reference, does not resolve under the caller's profile/avatar policy, or points to a blob the server cannot authorize for profile display. Protocol profile updates MUST use `avatar_blob_ref`; `avatar_url` is only a compatibility-layer input outside the Cokret protocol path.

`ck.self.account.command.update_profile` received a patch path outside the account self-service allowlist (`display_name`, `avatar_blob_ref`, `profile_fields.<key>`). Handle, lifecycle, principal, actor_kind, accountability, authorization, and handle-claim paths MUST be rejected instead of silently ignored.

`ck.gate.account.command.revoke_session` targeted a session grant that is unknown, already inactive, or not owned by the current principal. Implementations SHOULD use a uniform response shape that does not disclose another principal's session grant existence.

`ck.gate.account.command.revoke_session` supplied more than one mutually exclusive selector (`target_grant_id`, `target_device_id`, `all_sessions=true`) or otherwise failed selector closure. Receivers MUST reject instead of choosing one selector implicitly.
Recipient device no longer holds the review capability required for member application review delivery.
Actor is not a member of the target Realm or scoped membership set for this operation.
Call does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
Call exists but its signaling window has expired.
Call answer was already accepted and the operation is not idempotent for this participant.
Caller lacks permission to create, join, answer, or modify the media session.
Service refused to issue ICE configuration for this call or participant.
Requested SFU or media focus is not allowed by Realm policy or media service binding.
Realm or call policy requires E2EE and the requested media path did not satisfy it.
Recording or transcription is denied by Realm policy or participant consent state.
Morph profile attempted to widen or replace schema_ref in a way that violates create-locked morph type rules.
A Morph update attempted to change an immutable morph_type after creation.

reason_codes.description: Sentinel value indicating an item or decision succeeded with no further reason.
Event was rejected because the active capability constraint requires approval evidence (per zh/authz/capabilities.md §6 / §8) and none was supplied.
No active capability grant authorises ck.message.create on the targeted Strand track for the actor.
The capability grant cited as authority was revoked at a frontier causally preceding this event; reducer rejects.
Concurrent grant/revoke ordering cannot be deterministically resolved with currently available history; recipient SHOULD backfill or escalate to manual review rather than picking a winner.

Revocation / grant freshness cannot be established for a high-risk, cross-domain, or delegated action. Receiver MUST fail closed and return freshness diagnostics instead of treating missing revoke evidence as allow.
A ck.realm.create event attempted to create a Realm id whose genesis cell is already set. Reducer MUST reject the duplicate create without rewriting create-locked fields.

A ck.realm.organization statement failed organization-side authorization: payload.authorization.proof did not verify against the organization DID control state, threshold governance quorum, or the verification_method, or issuer_role is not allowed for the relationship. This is the generic organization-consent failure used when no more specific realm_organization_* reason applies. Downstream implementations MUST emit this exact code rather than inventing a bare string.

A ck.realm.organization statement whose authorization.issuer_role is governance_service or account_authority omitted authorization.delegation_ref, or the referenced delegation does not resolve to a live organization DID delegation whose purpose covers ck.realm.organization and the requested relationship/control_scopes.

A ck.realm.organization statement is outside its validity window: the evaluation time is before payload.not_before, after payload.expires_at, or outside the referenced delegation's validity period. Schema validation passes; the reducer MUST reject the statement as expired or not-yet-valid.

A ck.realm.organization statement asserts a control_scope (or relationship) that the verified organization-side authorization or its delegation does not cover. The endorsement boundary in payload.control_scopes exceeds what the proof/delegation grants.

A ck.realm.organization statement lacks the Realm-side acceptance layer: the writing principal does not hold ck.realm.admin and the event is not part of an allowed create-bootstrap initial-configuration batch. Realm-side acceptance is independent of the organization-side proof.
A Realm bootstrap batch placed a facet event before the ck.realm.create event that establishes the creator membership and Realm create cell.
A ck.realm.policy_components update skipped one or more monotonic policy_revision values. Reducer MUST reject instead of accepting a discontinuous policy frontier.
An sealed moderation quarantine or fast-path quarantine was lifted, and clients viewing the Realm should surface that affected content became visible again.

A fast-path moderation quarantine signal was recorded but its sealed Control Move has not yet arrived; clients MAY temporarily hide the target and MUST switch display once the sealed decision lands (policy-server.md §7.2).
A moderation control cell resolved to bottom under conflicting sealed Control Moves; downstream decisions depending on the cell fail closed until the split is resolved (policy-server.md §7.2).

A soft-logout recovery DID proof was rejected because expires_at is missing or its freshness window exceeded the bound (expires_at - issued_at > 300s, or issued_at skew beyond tolerance); see account-lifecycle.md §4 and identity-did.md §5.1.
A Realm attempted to combine ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 with an open or quarantine federation policy, or with restricted federation that lacks a bounded fanout SLA within the relaxed E2EE window.
