registry/hpke-suite-registry.json.description: Canonical HPKE (RFC 9180) suite vocabulary for v1 application-layer public-key sealing surfaces that are NOT carried inside MLS: key-backup `recovery_public_key` envelopes, did_recovery envelopes, to-device sealed material (`ck.secret.send`), member-application reviewer envelopes and file-transfer key envelopes. An HPKE suite is the registered triple (KEM, KDF, AEAD) per RFC 9180; its canonical_id is the wire scheme / `hpke_suite` selector value. This is the fourth algorithm-agility registry, symmetric to signature-alg-registry.json, digest-suite-registry.json and mls-ciphersuite-registry.json. MLS group messages keep their own HPKE internals via mls-ciphersuite-registry.json and are out of scope here.
registry/hpke-suite-registry.json.suite_id_grammar: suite_id = 'ck.hpke_' kem_id '_aead_' aead_id '.v' major ; each id segment matches [a-z0-9]+ . The canonical_id is the full wire string; it is NOT freely composed from parts — only suites present as rows below exist, and only status=active rows are valid on wire.
registry_rules: Only suites present as rows in this registry exist. Implementations MUST NOT compose KEM/KDF/AEAD ids freely; only status=active rows are valid on wire.

A suite id not present as an active row MUST fail closed with unsupported_hpke_suite when it appears in an HPKE-sealed surface (key-backup recipient_method=recovery_public_key, ck.secret.send, member-application encryption_envelope, file-transfer key_envelope). Receivers MUST NOT infer suite parameters from the AEAD name alone.

Schema enum values for HPKE suite selector fields (e.g. ck.schema.key_backup.v1 encryption.hpke_suite, the ck.secret.send / member-application / file-transfer envelope `scheme` const) MUST be generated from active rows' canonical_id.

When a surface carries both an explicit `hpke_suite` selector and an AEAD `name`/profile field, the AEAD MUST equal the selected suite's aead; a mismatch MUST be rejected (schema_violation). A surface MAY omit the selector only where a single default-MUST suite is pinned by its defining document, in which case the absent selector denotes that row.

status=reserved rows pin the wire id and profile gate but MUST NOT appear on wire until every activation_requirements entry is met and the row is flipped to active in a registry release. Receivers MUST fail closed (unsupported_hpke_suite) on a reserved suite id seen on wire before activation.

The registry is intentionally minimal: new KEM families (post-quantum / hybrid), new KDFs and new AEADs enter additively as new rows with their own profile gates and conformance vectors; the ck.hpke_*_aead_*.v* wire form needs no rewrite. Per RFC 9180, base-mode single-shot sealing derives its AEAD nonce internally from the key schedule, so HPKE-sealed surfaces carry no wire nonce and have no nonce-reuse obligation (contrast the symmetric key-backup methods, which pin nonce uniqueness in zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5).

kem_strength_order.note: Classical KEMs are treated as equal classical strength; the hybrid xwing row is strictly stronger (adds ML-KEM-768 post-quantum confidentiality). Consumed by any future no-downgrade rule on suite transition.

suites.security_note: v1 default-MUST application-layer HPKE suite. KEM DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) and KDF HKDF-SHA256 are RFC 9180 base; the AEAD is XChaCha20-Poly1305 (extended 192-bit nonce, outside RFC 9180's base AEAD registry but widely implemented), retained as the v1 default for the to-device / member-application / file-transfer envelopes that already pin this id. Classical (not post-quantum).
All-RFC-9180 suite for key-backup recovery_public_key envelopes on platforms with AES hardware acceleration. Classical.
All-RFC-9180 suite (96-bit-nonce ChaCha20-Poly1305) for software-only platforms preferring the base RFC 9180 AEAD over the extended-nonce XChaCha variant. Classical.
P-256 KEM for WebAuthn/FIDO2/PKI key-agreement interop, mirroring the ECDSA-P256 signature row. Profile-gated; receivers not advertising ck.profile.hpke.p256.v1 fail closed. Classical.

activation_requirements: ck.profile.kem.hybrid_xwing.v1 fully specified with the X-Wing KEM draft pinned (draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem) under MIMI-style draft-pinning discipline (draft change = new profile version)
Per-suite HPKE conformance vectors published (KEM encap/decap, key schedule, sealed bytes)

Coverage-priority alignment recorded: key-backup envelope before MLS KeyPackage (static ciphertext backups are the primary Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later target; reuses the reserved ck.aead.hybrid_kem.* namespace)
suites.security_note: Reserved post-quantum hybrid KEM (X25519 + ML-KEM-768) per the encryption-and-audit.md §2 PQ roadmap. Hybrid confidentiality: secure if either X25519 or ML-KEM-768 holds. Not on wire until activated.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form ck:<kind>:<uuid> unless a special form below applies.

Storage implementations MAY store raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ck:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The UUID segment MUST be RFC 9562 UUID version 7 (48-bit Unix-millisecond timestamp + 4-bit version=7 + 12-bit rand_a + 2-bit variant=10b + 62-bit rand_b), serialized as the canonical 36-character lowercase hex form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-7xxx-Nxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` where N ∈ {8,9,a,b}.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.
special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference; distinct from ck:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.
special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
special_forms.description: Realm-scoped pseudonymous credential reference; validated by the E2EE profile. v1 core uses Realm as the boundary; Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as a content-addressed canonical Seal hash.
Store canonical tuple fields separately when indexing cell state.
Store the scope string as an opaque deployment-level identifier; it appears in server describe, Realm policy, and high-risk proof transcripts.
special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk proofs (e.g. ck.cross_signing.reset §14.1). NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.

id_kinds.description: Moderation appeal ID — opaque key for the ck.component.moderation.appeal.v1 cell. Created by ck.moderation.appeal.submit; referenced by review / decision / close events. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.

Agent interop session ID. Note the cross-surface naming: this typed ID uses the short form `agent_interop_session`, while the corresponding event kinds use the full form `ck.agent.interop_session.{start,status,result}` and capability actions use `ck.agent.interop_session.{start,cancel,stream_status,attach_artifact,read_transcript}`. The three surfaces all refer to the same session concept; downstream tooling MUST NOT assume `ck:<event-prefix>:<uuid>` mechanical derivation.
Directory-local announce ingest record ID. It is typed and UUIDv7-shaped for validator consistency, but it is scoped to the issuing Directory and is not a global federated object authority.
Audit Applet Binding ID. Created by ck.audit.applet_binding and referenced by audit session request/authorize/notice/release events.
Audit release session ID. Threads ck.audit.session.request, authorize, notice, release, and close events for one bounded historical audit window.
Audit release manifest ID. Created by ck.audit.release for a sealed historical release under an active audit binding/session.

Stable identifier for one chain of encrypted backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_class). A pair MAY have multiple series during rotation or migration; the active series is selected by the signed active-series record, not by server return order. Used by ck.schema.key_backup.v1.series_id and recovery strands to detect rollback. See identity/key-management.md §7.6.
Blob metadata row ID; content-addressed blobs use the special digest form

SFU-local participant handle (CKP-0010). Scope limited to `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`; derived from `(realm_id, call_id, focus_id, device_id, issuer_service_did, issued_at_bucket)` by the media service token issuer. MUST NOT carry any actor-identifying material; only appears in `ck.call.state.participants[].participant_identity` and in `participant_binding`. The wire value MUST use the canonical UUIDv7-shaped `ck:rtc_participant:<uuid>` form; implementations MAY derive the random bits from the media-service token input, but the version and variant nibbles MUST satisfy the UUIDv7 pattern.
Abstract capability definition reference ID; signed grant objects use ck:grant:<uuid>.

Circle object ID — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. See zh/models/circle.md.

Device identifier (ck:device:<uuid>). A device is a typed ID scoped to an owning principal, NOT a DID and NOT an actor principal. Device keys are registered as verification methods under the owning principal DID via ck.device.authorize.
Signed capability grant object ID used by ck.schema.capability.v1 and grant/revoke references.

Stable session identifier bound by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof and MLS Welcome replay during one recovery strand. Referenced by ck.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 and by §15 recovery proofs. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Space object ID — structural grouping object inside a Realm (board, list, swimlane, calendar bucket, etc.). Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership / policy / E2EE group; resolves to the containing Realm.
Realm object ID — security / sync / auth / E2EE boundary. Always carries membership, policy, history_visibility, MLS group binding, and federation policy.

registry/mls-ciphersuite-registry.json.description: Canonical MLS (RFC 9420) ciphersuite vocabulary for v1 KeyPackage cipher_suites[] negotiation and server describe surfaces. Completes the algorithm-agility registry symmetry with digest-suite-registry.json, signature-alg-registry.json and hpke-suite-registry.json.
registry_rules: Schema / describe enum values for MLS ciphersuite fields MUST be generated from active rows' canonical_id.

A ciphersuite not present as an active row MUST fail closed in KeyPackage claim / group negotiation (unsupported ciphersuite); receivers MUST NOT accept unregistered suites even if the underlying MLS library supports them.

New suites (e.g. ChaCha20-Poly1305 for AES-accelerator-less devices) enter additively as new rows with their own profile gates and conformance vectors; the registry stays minimal for classical suites, but pre-registers post-quantum hybrid rows as status=reserved to match the HPKE / TLS PQ pre-registration discipline (hpke-suite-registry.json, transport-bindings.md §5).

status=reserved rows pin the canonical_id, profile gate and activation_requirements but MUST NOT appear on wire until every activation_requirements entry is met and the row is flipped to active in a registry release. Receivers MUST fail closed (unsupported ciphersuite) on a reserved suite seen in KeyPackage cipher_suites[] or group negotiation before activation — same discipline as encryption-and-audit.md 'MLS 内容 KEM 边界'.

ciphersuites.security_note: RFC 9420 mandatory-to-implement suite; classical X25519 KEM (not post-quantum; hybrid KEM migration path reserved via ck.aead.hybrid_kem.* namespace and future hardening profile).

activation_requirements: ck.profile.kem.hybrid_xwing.v1 fully specified with the X-Wing KEM draft pinned (draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem) under MIMI-style draft-pinning discipline (draft change = new profile version)
IETF/IANA MLS ciphersuite code point assigned for the X-Wing hybrid suite and recorded here as rfc9420_id (registry release required; receivers MUST NOT improvise a private code point)
Per-suite MLS conformance vectors published (KeyPackage encoding, welcome/commit KEM encap/decap, group key schedule)

Coverage-priority alignment recorded: activates only after the HPKE X-Wing row (hpke-suite-registry.json ck.hpke_xwing_aead_xchacha20poly1305.v1) — static ciphertext backups are the primary Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later target, MLS group KEM is the second wave
ciphersuites.security_note: Reserved post-quantum hybrid MLS suite (X-Wing = X25519 + ML-KEM-768 KEM; AES-128-GCM; Ed25519 signatures) per the encryption-and-audit.md PQ roadmap and 'MLS 内容 KEM 边界' scoping note. Hybrid confidentiality: secure if either X25519 or ML-KEM-768 holds. Not on wire until activated; receivers MUST fail closed on this suite before activation.

registry/mls-extension-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of Cokret-defined MLS (RFC 9420) GroupContext extensions occupying the MLS private-use ExtensionType range 0xF000-0xFFFF. Maintained so SDKs and conformance tooling have a single machine-readable entry for each active Cokret MLS extension codepoint.

private_use_range.reference: RFC 9420 §17.6; IANA MLS Extension Types registry (private-use range)

extensions.name: mls_governance_binding
extensions.carries: Cokret Realm/Circle governance binding inside the MLS GroupContext

registry/morph-type-decision-table.json.describes: Canonical merge precedence for the four declaration sources that can contribute to 'what a Morph is and what it allows'. Mirrors morph.md §4. Reducers, capability checks, query/projection paths, and conformance tests MUST follow this table.

precedence.notes: Declares the field set, types, requiredness, transition rules. Always read for field validation.

Tightens the order-1 declaration inside a single Realm (allowed facets subset, writable fields subset, required schema_refs, required capability actions). MUST NOT widen order-1; widening attempts produce `schema_violation` at Realm accept time.
Wire-stable string key. Create-locked so capability grant selectors do not silently break.
Pure hint. Reading facets to make a security / state-machine / interop decision is a conformance bug.

conflict_resolution.rationale: Facet is a hint, not a contract.
Field + capability are truth; facet is presentation hint only.

conformance_must_test: Reading order-4 facets to decide authorization → MUST fail.
Reducer field validation that ignores order-2 tightening → MUST fail.
Mutating morph_type after create → MUST fail with `morph_type_immutable`.
Order-2 morph_type_profile that widens order-1 schema → MUST be rejected at Realm accept time with `schema_violation` / `morph_profile_widens_schema_ref`.

registry/operation-registry.json.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Cokret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see capability_tiers); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>. The kind segment MUST be one of query, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex query body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (query/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

capability_tiers.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Cokret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
capability_tiers.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Cokret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
capability_tiers.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Cokret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
capability_tiers.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

operations.notes: Managed-DID (account-authority) device enrollment, device-lifecycle.md §5.4 / key-management.md §5.0.6. The authenticated session asks its designated enrollment authority to mint a service_attested ck.device.authorize for this session's own device; the authority signs with its persistent enrollment key (never the principal SSK) and returns the full Event. The caller submits it verbatim to POST /_cokret/self/events. Distinct from pair_device (§2.1), which lands an existing-device SAS/QR approval and carries a pairing_code; enroll_device is the bootstrap / first-device path where no sibling device can approve.

Account Authority single-call grant exchange. The response is the client-visible SessionGrantOutcome; any Principal-side local session provisioning is internal to the Account Authority. There is no separate client-visible grant-to-bearer exchange step: the client presents the returned ck.session.grant directly to /_cokret/self/* with a DPoP proof (api-conventions §3.3). For proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange, the Account Authority exchanges the authorization code at the issuer token_endpoint and validates issuer/state/nonce/redirect_uri/principal/device/audience binding before issuing the grant; the client MAY omit principal_id at first sign-in, in which case the Account Authority derives/mints the principal DID and returns it in SessionGrantOutcome.principal_id.

DPoP-bound session-grant rotation (account-lifecycle §4.1, device-lifecycle §3.3). An authorized device presents a DPoP holder proof for the grant's cnf.jkt plus a fresh DID/device proof bound to principal_id, device_id, audience, request_canonical_digest, challenge, issued_at, and expires_at; expires_at - issued_at MUST be <=300s. The old grant is single-use revoked. Account Authority-local op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): the Account Authority has already validated the client-visible ck.gate.account.command.logout request, then calls this operation with service-to-service authentication to log out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the presented ck.session.grant and terminate that session's grant rotation chain. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they only call ck.gate.account.command.logout. HTTP-only S2S op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Principal Server validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and optional S2S holder confirmation) and learns whether it is active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Principal Server can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_cokret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); clients do not send a separate introspection-proof header on self-path requests. session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. Authenticated by the configured session_grant_introspection_bearer (server-local); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The handler validates the current ck.session.grant + DPoP, terminates the Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain through ck.gate.account.command.logout_auth_session when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Probe the public ck.agent.endpoint registry for an agent's declared external protocol endpoints; returns the projection of an accepted ck.agent.endpoint event (no controller-private fields). Authorized by the ck.agent.protocol.discover capability action (profile ck.profile.agent_runtime.v1). See agent-protocol-interop.md §5.1 / §11 / §12.

Optional Account Authority browser redirect landing / handoff for deployments that use an OIDC redirect URI under /_cokret/gate/account. It MUST NOT issue or return SessionGrantOutcome, ck.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance remains ck.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant.

source_signature_anchor.node_to_applet: Source-Service-DID current service DID verification method; Destination-Service-DID MUST equal the Applet registration service_did.
source_signature_anchor.applet_to_cokret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; DID part MUST equal Source-Service-DID and the active effective install service_did.

operations.notes: Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. HTTP binding is POST because the request is a batch command against a queue collection, deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key), and does not replace a single URI-addressed message resource. Queue pruning is only via ck.self.device_messages.command.ack.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages from=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.
Writes requester-side ck.contact.requested fact and requester-side consent grants for requested scopes; MUST NOT write target consent or accepted fact.
Target-side accept/reject of a contact request. Accept writes target-controlled consent grants; reject writes no consent.
Holder contact projection from contact facts plus consent-derived directional scopes; account-data contact notes are local decoration only.
Holder-side contact tombstone. Default revocation is limited to contact-managed active consent dots.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ck.self.contact.command.tombstone(block_peer) blocked_subjects writes.
Idempotent resolver for accepted contacts. Requires accepted contact projection and direct_message consent; create=true creates canonical DM Realm, main Strand, and binding.

Builds a ck.circle.create Operation in the named parent Realm and routes it through the local accept pipeline. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_ref, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor permits plaintext.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Builds ck.circle.member.state. Activating another actor requires ck.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule.
Builds ck.circle.member.state with membership=leave for the path actor_id.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.
Builds ck.circle.archive; transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_active).

Builds ck.circle.restore; transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_archived). Restore re-enables new writes after pending MLS membership removals are settled.
Builds ck.circle.tombstone (terminal). Response surfaces the terminal state with empty members.

Resource-side appeal against an operator takedown. The appeal packet MUST bind takedown_id, resource id, appellant DID, argument/evidence digest, requested_outcome and created_at, signed by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate; the Directory returns a signed decision receipt. See discovery-directory.md §8.7.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ck.events.query. Semantically identical (same selector / cursor / order / filter / include_completeness parameter set, same response shape including optional range_completeness). Choose when URL length would exceed practical limits (large realms[]/actors[] arrays, complex filters object) or when query parameters would be logged inadvertently by proxies. Non-HTTP transports MUST use the canonical ck.self.events.query.scan binding (SelfEvents/Query / self.events.query.scan), not expose this variant as a separate gRPC or MQ operation.
Dereference a known set of event_id / event_digest references to full EventEnvelope objects. Point lookup by identifier, not a range scan — use ck.self.events.query.scan for selector-based reads.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Durable self event submission, including ck.invite.claim. For ck.invite.claim, the receiving Realm reducer is the authoritative state machine: it MUST match token_commitment, re-check verification_service_did allowlist against current Realm policy, reject claim_nonce replay, perform pending -> claimed / membership-proposal effects, and run expiry cleanup before accepting.
Federation peer Events surface describe. This endpoint describes the server-to-server peer event bindings; it is not a client self/events binding.

Federation peer frontier probe. Requires service-to-service authentication, Source/Destination service DID headers, trust-domain headers, and Realm federation_peer authorization. It returns the federation peer frontier response shape on the dedicated peer trust surface.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ck.self.events.query.scan, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ck.peer.events.query.scan. Semantically identical to GET /_cokret/peer/events; use it when federation selectors or filters are too large or sensitive for query strings.

Federation peer event reference resolution for missing prev_refs / causal references. Requires authorized federation peer service authentication and applies the same reference-disclosure and history-visibility rules as peer event query.

Federation peer event push. Body is EventsSubmitFederationRequestBody and the caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers. Federated ck.invite.claim events are still decided by the destination Realm reducer, which MUST enforce token_commitment, current allowlist re-check, claim_nonce replay rejection, membership proposal conversion, and expiry cleanup; peer ingress prechecks are not state authority.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-DID equal to invite_address.recipient_service_did, a ck.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server contact fact delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-DID equal to contact_address.recipient_service_did, and a signed ck.contact.* envelope the recipient projects into the target holder's contact projection without re-signing.
Federation peer snapshot manifest head for snapshot-assisted bootstrap. Requires service-to-service authentication and Realm federation_peer authorization.

Canonical broadcast ephemeral send operation for ck.schema.ephemeral_envelope.v1. Carries ck.presence, ck.typing, ck.receipt.read, and ck.call.signal; MUST NOT persist the signal as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Media service token exchange operation (CKP-0010). Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ck.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend types (livekit / mediasoup / janus / cokret-native); only backend_token shape is type-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Read the currently accepted ck.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Publish a signed ck.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation for the authenticated principal. HTTP binding is POST because the principal/authority is derived from authenticated proof and signed policy state rather than a URI-addressed resource slot. Servers MUST verify auth_data.signed_fields, signature authority, version monotonicity, and supersedes linkage before accepting.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.
Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_cokret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version is negotiated via *.describe / supported_operations (see sync/api-conventions.md).
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ck.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Builds a ck.realm.link Move from realm_id -> target_realm_id. The reducer runs realm_link_* validators (cycle detection, self-reference, kind validation); a rejected payload returns 422 with the canonical reason code (e.g. realm_link_cycle, realm_link_self_reference).

Writes a tombstoning ck.realm.link Move (status=tombstoned) for the (realm_id, target_realm_id, link_kind) triple. link_kind defaults to governed_by; callers may override via the link_kind query param.

Returns the merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ck.realm.inheritance_policy. inheritance_mode=none when no inheritance policy is projected (implicit inheritance is forbidden).

Returns the projected ck.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organizations hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hints are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.
Reads the projected ck.realm.policy_server config. Returns not_found when neither the Realm nor its governed_by ancestor chain declared one. from_org_fallback=true marks an inherited config.

Builds a ck.realm.policy_server Move (admission capability ck.policy.manage). Reducer validates URL scheme and on_timeout enum. This admin DTO is a simplified projection of the canonical payload (server_id/endpoint/public_keys/applies_to/fail_mode).
Tombstones the per-Realm ck.realm.policy_server cell so callers fall back to the governed_by chain or local-only capability check. Empty success response.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Builds a ck.realm.archive Move. The archived facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; archived=false clears the archived facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies.

Builds a ck.realm.freeze Move. The frozen facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; frozen=true rejects ordinary non-exempt writes with realm_frozen and frozen=false clears the freeze facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies.

Builds a terminal ck.realm.tombstone Move with a successor_realm_id. The tombstoned state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state.
Builds a terminal ck.realm.destroy Move. The destroyed state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ck.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.
Returns the organization-inherited effective moderation policy view: inheritance chain, organization policy layers, the Realm's own override, and merged effective rules.

Writes a Realm moderation-policy override (ck.realm.moderation_policy). Only the Realm owner may write; an override that loosens an action an organization policy denies requires explicit organization approval embedded in the document, otherwise the server returns requires_organization_approval.
Lists holder-private consent cells where the caller is holder or peer. Each cell projects the current effective consent for a (holder, peer, consent_scope).
Reads one consent cell. Requires peer and consent_scope query params; caller MUST be holder or that peer. Returns not_found when no cell exists.
Builds a ck.consent.grant Control Move on the holder's consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (holder or an explicitly authorized controller/agent).

Builds a ck.consent.revoke Control Move enumerating the active grant dots for the (consent_id, peer, consent_scope). Revoking consent_scope=any cascades all concrete scopes; revoking a concrete scope leaves others intact.
Opens a pending consent request from the authenticated peer to a holder. peer_did defaults to and MUST equal the authenticated actor; the holder account MUST exist.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.
Reads one account_data entry by data_type key. Returns not_found when the key is unset.

Builds a ck.account_data.set actor-private write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.
Deletes one account_data entry and fans out an actor-private update to the holder's other devices.

Builds a ck.read_cursor.advance actor-private write for (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope, position). Multi-device convergence is by HLC max with device_id tiebreak; the cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Space lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface that materializes a View{kind=collection} projection such as board/list/table/calendar. The response is a derived read model computed from signed Events, reducer profile, View definition, and the returned frontier; it is not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Holder-bound service wrapper around ck.profile.update / Actor Profile projection. Request body is a closed patch over display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>; profile_fields.bio is the canonical personal bio field and avatar_url is not accepted on the Cokret protocol path.

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, presence, unread / notification counts). Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available. Symmetric with ck.self.events.stream.subscribe — both are streaming subscriptions, differing only in scope (self.events.stream.subscribe = per-Realm event log; self.account.stream.subscribe = account-aggregate). `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same principal/device/filter scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After. Presence changes are sent through ck.self.ephemeral.command.send, not this read-only stream subscription.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ck.self.device_messages.command.ack.

success_shape_kind_definitions.service_describe: ServiceDescribe object returned by a describe endpoint.
success_shape_kind_definitions.schema_resource: Response body is a canonical artifact JSON Schema resource.
success_shape_kind_definitions.inline_response: Endpoint-specific inline object schema in OpenAPI.
success_shape_kind_definitions.operation_result: Generic OperationResult envelope; operation row MUST carry generic_binding.
success_shape_kind_definitions.event_stream: Long-lived event stream rather than a single JSON success body.
success_shape_kind_definitions.metadata_headers: Metadata-only success expressed through HTTP headers.

registry/operations-error-mapping.json.description: Canonical mapping from canonical operation_id (artifacts/registry/operation-registry.json) to the error codes the operation MAY emit. Derived from prose error policy in zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.3 and from error-code-registry.json scope/description. Receivers of an operation SHOULD treat any error code listed here as a known reply shape; codes that map only to the universal failure surface (e.g. internal_error, service_unavailable) are not repeated per operation. cross-link target for zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.3.

rules.universal_codes: Every protected operation MAY additionally return any of: unauthenticated, auth_expired, soft_logged_out, account_locked, account_suspended, account_deactivated, account_erased, did_proof_required, invalid_signature, capability_denied, schema_violation, bad_json, bad_query, missing_param, invalid_param, rate_limited, too_large, conflict, internal_error, service_unavailable, not_implemented, unsupported_feature, unsupported_event_kind. These are the universal failure surface and are NOT repeated in each operation entry.
rules.operation_specific: operation_specific[] lists the error codes that are semantically tied to this operation's domain logic (event ingest, key claim, blob upload, push gateway, directory ingest, ...). An entry may name either a top-level code from error-code-registry.json `codes` or a sub-code from its `reason_codes` section (carried under a top-level code such as failed_precondition or schema_violation). Consumers discriminate by first matching the entry against the registry's top-level `codes` set; an entry not found there is a reason_code and matches the error reply's `reason_code` field rather than its top-level `code`. Receivers SHOULD recognize and surface these codes specifically.
rules.endpoint_aliases: Each operation entry lists its canonical HTTP method+path alias for human navigation; alternative bindings (gRPC, MQ) inherit the same error code set.
rules.operation_coverage: Every operation_id in artifacts/registry/operation-registry.json MUST appear exactly once in operations[]. An empty operation_specific[] means the operation has no domain-specific reply shape beyond the universal failure surface.

operations.description: Account registration creates or binds a deployment-local account record to principal_id. The request uses principal_id rather than did, does not accept handle, and handle evidence can only be returned as signed ck.schema.handle_claim.v1 data or digest/ref.
No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

Enrolls a device via the principal's designated enrollment authority. proof_invalid when the enrollment proof / controller binding does not verify against the authority designated in the principal DID document; duplicate_conflict when the device record already exists; failed_precondition when the enrollment-authority designation is absent or stale at the accepted-at frontier. See zh/identity/key-management.md §5.0.6 and zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.2.

Account Authority session grant issuance. Shared by human user_session and agent runtime branches (CKP-0008 §4.6): when `proof.proof_kind="oidc_code_exchange"`, `proof_invalid` covers issuer/discovery/state/nonce/redirect_uri/code_verifier/principal/device/audience binding failures; when `proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`, agent-specific failure codes apply — `proof_invalid` for transcript / nonce / audience binding failures of the agent_key_proof, `verification_method_principal_mismatch` when the verification_method DID does not match `principal_id`, `agent_paused` / `agent_deactivated` for lifecycle-gated rejections of the target agent principal, and `accountability_grant_missing` when the controller's accountability grant over the agent has been revoked or lapsed its freshness window so the agent is no longer eligible to receive a session grant (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md §9.1).

Session grant/access-token revocation. Empty body revokes the current request's session grant; cross grant/device/all_sessions selectors require fresh proof and never revoke device authorization or write durable ck.account.status.

DPoP-bound session-grant rotation (account-lifecycle §4.1). Single-use: a consumed grant cannot be rotated again (grant_already_consumed); the audience is locked to the prior grant (audience_mismatch); rotation is refused once the underlying browser session is logged out (session_logged_out). The caller MUST present a holder proof signed by the key bound into the grant's cnf.jkt plus a fresh DID/device proof bound to principal_id, device_id, audience, request_canonical_digest, challenge, issued_at, and expires_at. Missing proof material returns did_proof_required; invalid signature, replay, transcript, device binding, or freshness semantics return proof_invalid.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): a validated client-visible account /logout is represented by service-to-service authentication, and the Auth Server logs out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the supplied grant so the rotation chain cannot be resumed. Idempotent: re-presenting an already-logged-out, revoked, unknown, or pruned auth session/grant succeeds with the chain treated as terminated. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they retry ck.gate.account.command.logout.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). Read-only validation: returns active/status/grant-metadata in a 200 body (including not_found / audience_mismatch as statuses, not error replies), so it has no operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface (e.g. bad_json for a malformed id, the universal auth codes when the introspection bearer is missing).

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): the only client-visible logout entry. It validates the current ck.session.grant + DPoP, terminates the Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain, and completes or durably schedules Principal-side local account/device session cleanup plus to-device/push removal. Does not write ck.account.status, emit ck.device.revoke, or erase durable device authorization. Idempotent — no domain-specific failure beyond the universal surface.
Native personal agent runtime key pairing (CKP-0008 §4.5). 412 responses use these codes; pairing into an already-deactivated agent principal is terminal.

Provision a native personal agent principal (CKP-0008). The op is the aggregate `ck.self.agent.command.provision` capability action (capability-action-registry.json) and fans out `ck.profile.create` + `ck.identity.accountability_grant` + `ck.agent.key.authorize` + `ck.capability.grant`. `accountability_grant_missing` is returned when the orchestrator cannot write or validate the fan-out `ck.identity.accountability_grant` (controller lacks `ck.self.agent.command.provision` authority or its required constraints, the candidate grant fails accountability schema checks, or a concurrent state cell makes the grant unauditable). Other ineligibility reasons surface as `failed_precondition`.
not_found is returned both for nonexistent agent principals and for agents not visible to the caller (uniform failure surface, matches ck.self.events.resource.get pattern).
agent_paused is returned for idempotent re-pause; agent_deactivated is terminal.

Resume revalidates controller, agent key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability grant freshness; any stale precondition fails closed. Sidecar exposure re-disclosure failure surfaces as failed_precondition with reason=`sidecar_exposure_ack_required`.
agent_deactivated is returned for idempotent re-deactivation of an already-terminal agent.
Wire op ck.self.agent.command.rotate_key corresponds to event kind ck.agent.key.rotate; rotation MUST NOT widen scope or extend the retiring key's TTL.
Attaches a capability grant to the agent. capability_denied surfaces controller-side delegation refusal; agent_paused / agent_deactivated guard the lifecycle gate.
not_found is returned for nonexistent grant_id and for grants not attached to this agent (uniform failure surface).

Idempotent ensure (CKP-0009 §4.2.1): server-derived dedupe keys are `(realm_id, controller_principal_id)` for the sidecar Circle and `(controller_principal_id, normalized_context_ref)` for the private Strand / reuse identity — `agent_principal_id` is NOT part of either key, so all eligible agents of the same controller share one sidecar per Realm. Clients MUST NOT supply Idempotency-Key. sidecar_create_denied is a deliberately generic precondition that hides whether a sidecar with the same derived short_name already exists (existence privacy).

No operation-specific error codes beyond the universal failure surface.

registry/profiles-dependency-graph.json.description: DAG view of profile inheritance / dependency / mutual-exclusion edges. Derived from profile_requirements[<profile_id>].{inherits, depends_on, mutually_exclusive_with} in conformance-profiles.json. Consumed by zh/conformance/conformance-profiles.md §2.1 visualization tooling. Profiles whose only relationship is to be claimable on their own (no inherits / depends_on / mutually_exclusive_with) MAY be omitted from the edges[] list; they still appear in nodes[].

edge_kinds.inherits: A profile that inherits another transitively re-declares its required_endpoints / required_event_kinds / required_schemas / required_capability_actions. Inheritance edges are transitive and form a DAG (no cycles).
edge_kinds.depends_on: A profile that depends_on another MUST be claimed alongside that target profile; absence of the target MUST cause the claimant to be treated as unsupported.
edge_kinds.mutually_exclusive_with: Profiles linked by this edge MUST NOT be claimed together; reducer / discovery MUST reject the combination (typically with reason_code conflicting_*_profiles).

cycle_check.tooling_hint: Consumers of this artifact MUST topologically sort `edges[]` filtered by kind=='inherits' to verify cycle-freeness before using it as a profile inheritance resolver.

policy.normative_source_rule: Once a CKP is accepted and merged, implementation requirements live only in zh/, artifacts/schemas, artifacts/registry, artifacts/openapi, artifacts/profiles, and artifacts/fixtures. Proposal files remain rationale and history.

registry/vector-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of conformance vector identifiers. Every ck.vector.* identifier referenced by prose or fixtures MUST appear here, and every row MUST point at the prose or fixture source that defines it.

vectors.description: Applet transaction push source signature anchor: per-delivery RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature covering method/target/authority/content-digest/source-service-did/destination-service-did/idempotency-key, source_signature_anchor persisted into the idempotency/replay record, duplicate body/anchor conflicts fail closed, and source service authentication does not replace Event actor/applet/capability checks.
field_access.sensitive_fields read projection handling: redact/hash/omit remove original values, hash uses keyed/salted digest discipline, and unenforceable handling falls back to omit.

Streaming chunked AEAD (ck.blob.stream_aead.v1) happy path: multi-segment plaintext with a short final segment is split, per-segment AEAD encrypted, segment-wise downloaded and incrementally verified, and the top-level ciphertext_digest is recomputed and matches per media-and-blob.md section 3.3.

Streaming AEAD truncation: a dropped final segment, a last segment whose flag stays 0x00, or segment_count exhausted without last_segment_flag=0x01 MUST be rejected with segment_stream_truncated and buffered plaintext discarded.
Streaming AEAD ordering: out-of-order / skipped / gapped segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_sequence_invalid; a repeated segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_replay.

Streaming AEAD scheme closure: an unknown attachment scheme MUST fail closed with unsupported_attachment_scheme (no fallback decrypt); an envelope carrying both whole-file nonce and chunked nonce_prefix/segment_* fields MUST fail blob.schema.json encrypted_attachment oneOf validation.

Streaming AEAD declared-bounds negatives (declared fields only, no multi-MiB payload materialised): segment_count above 2^20, segment_size below 1 KiB or above 8 MiB, and segment_count inconsistent with ceil(size_bytes / segment_size) MUST all be rejected fail-closed (schema_violation, reason_code segment_bounds_invalid) before key derivation or any segment download.
Accepts the three legal first call states and rejects active or terminal first states.
Covers every legal call lifecycle transition and representative non-terminal illegal transitions.
Terminal call states reject every attempted outgoing transition with call_state_terminal.
Same-basis replay of the same from/to transition is idempotent and does not create a divergent head.
Same-basis sibling transitions to different states return fsm bottom instead of selecting a winner.

Recording retention: audit_lock blocks deletion (legal_hold_active) regardless of retention_expires_at, and entering a capturing recording_state without consent_confirmed fails with recording_consent_required.

Recording ready results MUST carry ck.schema.call_recording_artifact.v1 metadata bound to the recording start event, Cokret blob pipeline, recording exporter label/context, retention policy, deletion audit trigger, and erasure receipt.

Transcription requires ck.call.transcribe (transcription_denied otherwise), and transcript artifacts MUST use the ck-rtc-transcript-key/v1 exporter label with a dedicated Context (transcription_artifact_pipeline_bypassed otherwise).
Moderator kick/ban requires ck.call.moderate (call_moderation_unauthorised otherwise); removed_participants[] gates token re-issue with call_participant_removed.

P2P calls converge to SFU when participants exceed two, reusing the oldest_membership no-vote session_focus election; mode does not auto-downgrade, and ck.call.summary is gated on a terminal call state (call_summary_invalid otherwise).
resolve_agent_selector failure branches for missing, hidden, and unauthorized selectors return the same status, body shape, error class, and timing bucket.
resolve_handle failure branches for missing, hidden, and unauthorized handles return the same status, body shape, error class, and timing bucket.
on_last_read converges by principal-level aggregate contributions and read_trigger_window_ms; offline devices receive expiry stubs and shred keys when they reconnect.
Read-trigger expiry anchors are derived from anonymous aggregate contributions and MUST NOT reveal reader identity or reader counts to other clients or services outside the aggregate boundary.
Duplicate, stale, out-of-order, or cross-bound read-trigger contributions MUST NOT refresh anchors, double-count readers, or expire the wrong message.
ECDSA P-256 (ES256, RFC 6979 deterministic) detached JWS golden vector over the canonical proof binding object, mirroring the ed25519 vector structure for the optional interop signature suite.

ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) raw detached signature golden vector over the canonical proof binding object bytes (registry proof_kind raw_detached_signature; keygen from a recorded xi seed, signature published as a recorded value that verifiers only verify).

Executable signature negative family: bit-flipped signature, alg=none, alg/key-type mismatch (ES256 header resolving to an Ed25519 key), truncated public key, and a non-empty detached-JWS payload segment that still verifies in attached form; every case MUST be rejected with the recorded error_code.

Hand-written deterministic CBOR bounds: a definite-length array declaring/carrying 65537 items (generator-described, built by the runner) exceeds the v1 cap of 65536 items per array/map and MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_bounds_invalid) without preallocating from the declared count.

CBOR indefinite-length item (raw bytes bf616101ff, the indefinite-length map {_ "a": 1}) violates RFC 8949 section 4.2 deterministic encoding and MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_not_deterministic); locks the SDK's existing indefinite-length rejection on the mls_governance_binding decode path.

CBOR capacity bomb: a byte string header declaring 4294967295 bytes with only 4 bytes of remaining input (raw bytes 5affffffffdeadbeef) MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_bounds_invalid) before any buffer is allocated from the declared length.

Canonical structure depth cap: a JSON object nested 65 levels deep (generator-described, built by the runner; top-level container = depth 1) exceeds the v1 maximum nesting depth of 64 (objects and arrays combined) and MUST be rejected (reason_code structure_depth_exceeded) with bounded recursion; a depth-64 control input MUST be accepted.

Federation ingress authentication-failure family (unknown peer / not authorized / target absent) returns indistinguishable responses within one timing bucket per relation.md section 4.5 sampling rules.

service_binding_ref.reducer_profile_digest is computed per federation.md section 4.1.1 from the reducer-profile-registry.json digest_input row (Cokret canonical JSON, sha256); receiver recomputes and byte-compares, rejecting the whole batch with reducer_profile_mismatch on any divergence.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ck.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1 (DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / ChaCha20-Poly1305): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ck.hpke_x25519_aead_aes256gcm.v1 (DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ck.hpke_p256_aead_aes256gcm.v1 (DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM, profile-gated interop suite): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

Realm reducer authority for ck.invite.claim: binding_proof and subject_proof signature transcripts, token_commitment match, verification_service_did allowlist re-check, claim_nonce replay rejection, pending -> claimed membership-proposal conversion, and expiry cleanup are enforced before acceptance.

New passphrase_kdf backup envelopes below the unconditional base KDF floor (Argon2id memory_kib>=65536 / iterations>=3 / parallelism>=1; PBKDF2 iterations>=600000 with allowed digest_algorithm) MUST be rejected.
Key backup retrieval requires a session-bound unlock proof (ck.schema.key_backup_unlock_proof.v1); any binding mismatch or bearer-token-only access fails closed before ciphertext is returned.

Last-resort KeyPackage (ck.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1): when the normal pool is empty, claim MAY return last_resort=true; the package is reused across multiple Welcomes within the same intended_realm_id, consume is idempotent (stays published, never keypackage_already_consumed), and each consumption emits an append-only audit record per encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

Last-resort KeyPackage forced rotation: on next online the holder MUST rotate the last-resort package (new init key, old marked rotated) and trigger an MLS self-update Commit on every group joined via it to advance the epoch and close the forward-secrecy weakening window.

Last-resort KeyPackage Realm affinity, optionality, and profile gating: cross-intended_realm_id reuse MUST be rejected with last_resort_realm_affinity_violation; a server not declaring the feature MUST fail closed on an empty pool and MUST NOT return a last_resort package, with explicit last-resort fallback returning last_resort_not_supported; high_security_organization and sovereign_deployment Realms MUST treat last-resort as forbidden even when the service supports the feature.
MIMI Provider Facade directory claims are accepted only when the Cokret profile and pinned MIMI Internet-Draft versions match.
ck.mimi.room_binding projects a MIMI room onto a Realm or Strand scope without making the MIMI room canonical truth.
MIMI key-material exchange maps to the Cokret KeyPackage claim lifecycle: the claimed package is single-use, becomes consumed after Welcome, and enumeration-sensitive failures share one public shape.
MIMI message/content ingress preserves the original envelope digest and MIMI message identity when mapping into Cokret events.
MIMI identifier queries use private-contact-discovery semantics and do not expose a raw contact graph or reachability proof.
MIMI consent state is isolated from Cokret Realm read/write capability grants.
MIMI proxy download obeys asset privacy policy and does not return direct object-store URLs when provider proxying is required.
Unsupported MIMI draft versions fail closed or require a new profile without silently mutating the v1 reducer profile.

Appeal verdict transitions are atomic: overturn without a same-batch ck.moderation.decision.lift is rejected with appeal_overturn_missing_lift; modify requires a same-batch new decision matched by modify_decision_ref.

E2EE franking proof construction, report submission, and moderator-side verification roundtrip per content-moderation.md section 3.4; digest mismatch or minimal-disclosure violations downgrade or reject the proof.

E2EE moderation evidence packages are encrypted to the authorized moderation recipient, target only reported events, carry reporter signature evidence, and reject MLS epoch/history secrets or unrelated plaintext.

Deterministic ck.morph.schema_migrate transformation: a ck.transform.rename.v1 rule renames a Morph field and leaves unrelated fields untouched; the post-migration fields projection is canonical-JSON byte-equal across replays.

Deterministic ck.morph.schema_migrate transformation: a ck.transform.default_backfill.v1 rule backfills a new optional field with a fixed default while preserving existing fields; idempotent and replay-deterministic.
Seal canonical bytes exclude id and notary_signature; verifier recomputes the typed id and signature payload digest from signed top-level fields only.
cas_register writes on non-initial state require an explicit CBA basis: Control Move preconditions or equivalent DataEvent causal/lattice proof; null-basis blind overwrites fail closed.
open_set concurrent revocation is evaluated against the joined control view; revoked or bottom authorization cells fail closed without a freshness window.
bottom=reject control cell recovery accepts only a sealed conflict-recovery Move with valid recovery_capability and pre-conflict state_witness; negative cases pin recovery_witness_* reasons.
Expired policy decisions and decisions bound to an older auth/policy/membership frontier MUST be rejected on replay; receivers fail closed and re-request the policy check.
Receivers recompute the RFC 8785 JCS request_canonical_digest of the presented request body; mismatch with the signed bound_to transcript MUST reject the decision.

Sender-constrained session PoP: a write request with a valid RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature (kid = current grant session_public_key, covering @method/@target-uri/@authority/content-digest) is accepted; a signature whose transcript mismatches the method/path/body digest fails verification and is rejected per api-conventions.md section 3.2 and service-http-binding.md section 2.5.

Production current-v1 protected endpoints MUST reject bare Authorization: Bearer unless it is bound by DPoP, an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature, detached JWS, mTLS, or equivalent sender-constrained proof; high-security profiles additionally require RFC 9421 PoP for regular writes / sensitive reads; a PoP signature whose created/expires falls outside the replay window MUST be rejected.

High-assurance snapshot inclusion-challenge sampling verifies sufficient event_id and actor_seq_range coverage, recomputes the event-set Merkle root, rejects commitment-root mismatch, and rejects silent actor sequence gaps.

Client events.query backfill with include_completeness=true detects withheld actor branches via ck.attestation.range_completeness verification; feature-less servers ignore the parameter; single_source attestation does not satisfy high-assurance realms.
Canonical JSON object key ordering follows UTF-16 code units for supplementary-plane keys.
Blind-index stale postings after revocation, visibility tightening, redaction, expiry, or epoch rotation MUST not produce unauthorized recall.
Search hit is not an authorization proof; unauthorized or unverifiable hits return non-enumerating stubs.
Directory search, privacy-preserving search, and bridge interop surfaces stay separated and do not leak private plaintext.
Receiver rejects sender_nonce_prefix collision or nonce prefix mismatch.
Receiver rejects repeated per-device AEAD nonce counter.
Receiver rejects pure random 96-bit nonce profile for v1 encrypted attachments.
mv_register join/validate_op convergence for the same CBA Event set.
counter join/validate_op convergence for the same CBA Event set.
ordered_log join/validate_op convergence for the same CBA Event set.
fsm join: identical (from,to) sibling transitions converge idempotently; same-from different-to siblings return bottom (reject path).
ordered_log issuer sub-chain seq gap yields contiguous_prefix plus pending_gap diagnostics; deterministic recompute after backfill.
directory_visibility=realm_members exposes only the Realm-member preview field set and gives non-Realm callers the same locked stub/timing bucket as members-only circles.
RSVP occurrence key canonicalizes recurrence instance local wall-clock start in the event timezone.

reports/operation-schema-index.json.description: Generated DTO index for registered operations with request_schema_ref/response_schema_ref. JSON Schema files remain the canonical source; this report is a machine-readable summary for SDK/conformance tooling and prose drift review.

schemas/account-data-operations.schema.j.title: Cokret Account Data Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/account-data-operations.schema.j.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface actor-private account_data operations (ck.self.account_data.*). PUT builds a ck.account_data.set actor-private write; the server stores content verbatim (clients own canonical encoding and, for sensitive keys, client-side encryption). data_type keys are dot-delimited namespaces validated against account-data-type-registry.json. See spec/v1/zh/discovery/client-preferences.md.

data_type.description: Dot-delimited account_data namespace key (e.g. ck.contacts.realm.<realm_id>, ck.account.blocklist). Control chars / whitespace / path separators are forbidden so the key is URL- and log-safe.

content.description: Caller-supplied opaque payload, stored verbatim. Any JSON value.
Caller-supplied opaque payload. Server stores it verbatim; canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption are the client's responsibility. Any JSON value.

schemas/account-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Account Self-Service Operation DTOs
schemas/account-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for account self-service operations: viewer, register, profile update, and session revocation.

handle_claim_ref.description: Opaque reference to a signed ck.schema.handle_claim.v1 claim, such as an event ref, issuer-local receipt ref, or content-addressed artifact ref.

propertyNames.description: ck.self.account.command.update_profile only accepts display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>. The bio is carried as profile_fields.bio.

is_server_admin.description: True when the authenticated principal is a deployment server administrator (the server's configured admin principal set). Operator-only product surfaces (e.g. organization creation) gate their UI on this. Reducer/config-derived, not a stored account field; absent or false means non-admin.

schemas/account-subscribe-frame.schema.j.title: Cokret Account Subscribe Frame
schemas/account-subscribe-frame.schema.j.description: Single NDJSON frame on the ck.self.account.stream.subscribe streaming channel (GET /_cokret/self/account/subscribe, Content-Type: application/x-ndjson). Each newline-delimited line is one frame object. Discriminated by the `kind` field: `delta` carries account-aggregate data (cross-Realm frontier, to_device, account_data, device_lists, presence, notifications, unread counts); the other kinds are control frames that mirror ck.self.events.stream.subscribe (`catchup_complete`, `frontier`, `heartbeat`, `dropped`, `resync_required`, `unauthorized`). `dropped` and `resync_required` MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms` as a server-directed minimum delay before opening another account subscribe stream for the same principal/device/filter scope.

cursor.description: Stream cursor (purpose='stream'). On `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` frames it points to the position covered by this frame; pass back as `after=` on the next subscribe call to resume. REQUIRED on `dropped` frames as the account-aggregate catch-up start for `GET /account/subscribe?after=<cursor>&catchup=true`. MUST be present on `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` / `dropped`; absent on `heartbeat` / `resync_required` / `unauthorized`.

realms.description: Per-Realm map on `delta` frames. Keys are `ck:realm:*`; values are that Realm's aggregate timeline/state/account-data entry. Membership lifecycle (`join` / `invite` / `knock` / `leave`) is carried by the events inside the Realm entry.

account_data.description: Account-scoped private data updates on `delta` frames.

partial.description: When true on a `delta` frame, the per-Realm timelines are limited (truncated); client SHOULD backfill via ck.self.events.query.scan for any Realm whose timeline carries `limited=true`.

priority.description: Optional server-side priority hint for the frame (UX scheduling).

reconnect_after_ms.description: Optional server-directed minimum delay, in milliseconds, before opening another `ck.self.account.stream.subscribe` stream for the same principal/device/filter scope. MAY appear only on `dropped` and `resync_required` frames. This is a stream reconnect hint, not a generic error retry field; it does not apply to unrelated API calls. Clients MUST wait at least this delay before reconnecting, and servers MUST reject earlier reconnect attempts with `429 rate_limited` plus `Retry-After`.

ack_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever messages[] is non-empty. Bound server-side to (principal_id, device_id, queue high-water position of this batch) and covering this batch plus all previously delivered messages. NOT a cursor: no ck:cursor: wire form, no cursor schema/TTL/purpose. The client passes it verbatim to ck.self.device_messages.command.ack AFTER durably persisting the batch payloads; queue deletion happens only through that explicit ack, never through stream cursor advancement (client-sync.md §10.1).

lost.description: SHOULD be set true when the server has dropped unacknowledged messages for this device (expiry or capacity) since the device's last acknowledged position. Clients SHOULD trigger key recovery paths (key backup / key re-request) and MUST NOT silently assume the queue was complete.

limited.description: True when this account subscribe to_device batch is truncated because the device queue exceeds the stream frame budget. When true, `next_cursor` is REQUIRED and the client MUST continue with ck.self.device_messages.query.list?from=<next_cursor>; the top-level account stream cursor MUST NOT be used as the to-device queue pagination cursor.

next_cursor.description: Read-only to-device queue continuation cursor for ck.self.device_messages.query.list?from=... . It is not an acknowledgement and MUST NOT delete queued messages; queue deletion happens only through `ack_token` passed to ck.self.device_messages.command.ack.

prev_cursor.description: Stream cursor pointing backward in the timeline for backfilling history before this batch.

preview_only.description: Fallback path of client-sync.md §5.2: when timeline.limited=true and the server does not return realm_sync_entry.state_at_window_start, it MUST set preview_only=true. Clients then render window-start events as preview only.

state_at_window_start.description: Derived projection-only state at the timeline window start, for rendering correctness when timeline.limited=true (client-sync.md §5.2 path (a)). NOT part of state hash / frontier / causal graph. When timeline.limited=true the server MUST return either this field or timeline.preview_only=true.

actor_profiles.description: Display context for actors appearing in the window (display_name, avatar_blob_ref, ...), keyed by principal DID.

realm_metadata.description: Realm-level Lattice cell values at window start (title, summary, join_rule, ...).

e2ee_epoch.description: MLS epoch hint at the window start (epoch number + key_ref).

members.description: Lightweight roster hint derived from effective ck.member.state, effective ck.member.identity.update references, and currently visible handle-claim evidence. Entries MUST NOT carry display fields or naked handle strings directly; handle strings may appear only inside signed ck.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects.

members_limited.description: True when members[] is truncated and MUST NOT be treated as the complete Realm roster.

members_next_cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor for continuing member roster retrieval.

event_states.description: Per-event protocol-state views (event_id + event_state) for reducer-input events carried by this entry. The 'bottom' detail object lives separately in 'bottoms' below — keyed by cell, not duplicated per event — so wire body is not doubled. Receivers correlate event_state=failed_bottom with the cell-level bottom diagnostic via the cells listed in bottom.cells[]. See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

event_state_reason_code.description: Optional short reason code (e.g., 'recovery_witness_missing'). For failure detail beyond the enum.

bottoms.description: Structured Bottom diagnostics for cells whose effective Lattice join resolved to ⊥ under the current CBA query basis. Each entry pins (cell, status, bottom). See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

subject_id.description: Optional disclosed principal / holder DID for this member. Omit when subject disclosure is only available inside encrypted MemberIdentity or not authorized for the caller. Required whenever handle claim evidence or digest hints are included.

identity_event_ids.description: Effective ck.member.identity.update event ids for this actor after replacement refs are applied.

member_display_state_digest.description: Digest over the effective identity event references plus the current visible handle claim digest set for this roster entry.

identity_events.description: Optional inline effective ck.member.identity.update Event envelopes. When present these are the original events, not query-time re-encryption or projection rewrites. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because plaintext or decryptable identity events can disclose the same member subject.

handle_claim_digests.description: Digests of currently visible effective ck.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects for this member in the current Realm context. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because stable claim digests are linkable across contexts. Absence is not proof that the member has no handle.

handle_claims.description: Optional inline signed handle claim evidence. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, and every included claim MUST have claim.subject equal to subject_id. Services may omit this for privacy, size, or freshness; clients can backfill by subject via ck.find.directory.query.list_handles_for_subject.

handle_claims_limited.description: True when handle_claims[] is truncated or replaced by digest-only hints. Clients MUST NOT interpret missing claims as no handle.

oneOf.description: Catch-up replay or initial baseline completed; no data fields are allowed.
Cursor-only frontier advancement; no data fields are allowed.
