effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the key material. Realm-default history uses {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle history uses {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}. Implementations MUST NOT infer key scope from strand_id or track.

policy_digest.description: Hash of the effective Realm/Circle policy root used to authorize this historical key share.

membership_frontier_digest.description: Optional hash of the membership frontier evaluated for history visibility and recipient membership.

realm_id.description: Parent Realm identifier. MUST equal effective_scope.realm_id.

circle_id.description: Present only when effective_scope.kind='circle'. MUST equal effective_scope.circle_id.

effective_scope.description: Tagged MLS governance scope. Realm-default groups use {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle groups use {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}. This field, not Strand id or track, determines key and membership scope.

binding_profile.description: Explicit profile that defines how this governance binding is interpreted. Full E2EE uses ck.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1; the only v1 downgrade profile is ck.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Receivers MUST fail closed when this field is missing, unsupported, inconsistent with the Realm profile declaration, or used to imply a downgrade without the matching policy/profile declaration.

reducer_profile.description: Reducer profile identifier used to interpret membership_frontier, policy_root, capability_root, and covered_seals_cell semantics. Receivers MUST fail closed when this field is missing or does not match the reducer profile negotiated for the Realm/federation peer.

mls_governance_binding.$comment: Schema requires the tagged scope and circle_id presence rules. Reducers/verifiers must additionally compare realm_id == effective_scope.realm_id and, for circle scope, circle_id == effective_scope.circle_id; JSON Schema cannot express cross-field equality for these string values.

mls_genesis_payload.$comment: Schema requires both effective_scope and governance_binding. Reducers/verifiers must additionally compare effective_scope with governance_binding.effective_scope; JSON Schema cannot express deep cross-field equality.

effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the MLS group created at epoch 0. MUST match governance_binding.effective_scope.

base_epoch.description: Expected previous MLS epoch. MUST equal governance_binding.previous_epoch.

next_epoch.description: Committed next MLS epoch. MUST equal governance_binding.next_epoch.

applet_registration_payload.description: Payload for ck.applet.registration. Durable Realm-history Event registering an Applet (bridge / bot / Ghost Actor namespace). Field vocabulary: zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §4 and zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §1 (the authoritative machine schema is applet.schema.json, which documents the applet object snapshot; the wire Event payload is this closed class). An Applet's capability to enter a Realm MUST be granted by that Realm's owner / admin / authorized registry-authz service; a self-signed registration alone MUST NOT write to a Realm (reason=applet_registration_unauthorized). registration MUST be signed by the controller DID (proof per models/event-and-patch.md §3).

applet_id.description: Stable applet identifier: a DID or the typed-id form ck:applet:<uuidv7>.

service_did.description: DID of the service hosting the applet runtime.

controller_did.description: DID of the Applet controller / external system; signs the registration.

namespaces.description: Applet namespace claims (actors / realms / handles patterns). Namespace match alone never grants write capability.

webhook_auth.description: Transaction push HTTP signature policy copied from the Applet package. webhook_auth.key_ref is the Applet service DID URL used as the app/bridge->cokret inbound source signature anchor and is bound to this registration_epoch; node->Applet pushes verify the Cokret source service DID from Source-Service-DID instead.

manifest.description: Applet manifest snapshot (capability requirements, supported intents, etc.).

proof.description: Controller-DID detached signature over the canonical registration object (excluding proof). An empty proof object MUST be rejected as schema_violation; required proof fields per models/event-and-patch.md §3.

applet_bridge_error_payload.description: Payload for ck.applet.bridge_error. Durable Realm-history Event recording a bridge / external-network failure. Field table: zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7. MUST bind realm_id, failed_transaction_ref, retriable, and visibility_scope; missing any required field MUST be rejected as schema_violation. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

failed_transaction_ref.description: Reference to the failed transaction / source Event. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

error_class.description: Closed error category for aggregation / alerting. See zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7.

visibility_scope.description: Closed visibility scope enum for the error event. Clients MUST honor it and MUST NOT expose bridge-internal detail to unrelated members.

external_ref.description: External network reference (protocol / network id). MUST NOT contain unauthorized external plaintext.

message.description: Human-readable summary. MUST NOT leak unauthorized external plaintext.

retry_after_ms.description: Suggested retry delay; meaningful only when retriable=true.

applet_interop_session_start_payload.description: Payload for ck.applet.interop_session.start. Parallel to ck.agent.interop_session.start but applet-scoped. Field vocabulary: applet.schema.json (session_id correlates start/status; params are caller-supplied, opaque to the Cokret protocol and interpreted per applet manifest). Unlike ck.agent.* there is NO canonical applet session state machine in v1.

session_id.description: Per-invocation correlation id pairing start with the matching status event.

params.description: Caller-supplied parameters. Opaque to the Cokret protocol; bridge interprets per applet manifest.

applet_interop_session_status_payload.description: Payload for ck.applet.interop_session.status. Parallel to ck.agent.interop_session.status but applet-scoped. runtime_status is the bridge-implementation-defined status (applet.schema.json) — v1 does NOT mandate a canonical applet session state machine; the field is named runtime_status (not status) to keep applet snapshots distinguishable from the canonical agent session state machine. detail is a free-form bridge-side surface.

runtime_status.description: Bridge-implementation-defined runtime status. Bridges MAY restrict the set further in their applet manifest.

detail.description: Bridge-side detail surface (echo response, error context, bridge identifier, etc.). Bridges document their own schema.

mimi_room_binding_payload.description: Payload for ck.mimi.room_binding. Writes the ck.component.mimi.room_binding.v1 cell whose subject is payload.mimi_room_uri (see event-kind-registry.json cell_subject). Authoritative field set: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §3. The binding is a projection of a Cokret Realm/Strand discussion track into a MIMI room; it is not canonical truth. Creation / update / revocation MUST hold ck.policy.manage, ck.realm.admin, or an equivalent interop capability. E2EE MIMI rooms MUST bind mls_group_id and pass the MLS Governance Binding covered_seals_cell precondition.

mimi_room_uri.description: MIMI room URI. Cell subject for ck.component.mimi.room_binding.v1.

binding_scope.description: Cokret Realm + Strand scope this MIMI room projects. strand_id MUST point at an accepted Strand with discussion track enabled inside realm_id; the MIMI room timeline only projects that Strand's discussion track.

hub_provider.description: Service DID explicitly delegated by Realm policy, Organization DID, or participant DID to host the hub role.

mls_group_id.description: MLS group id. MUST be present for E2EE MIMI rooms.

policy_root.description: Digest of the Cokret policy component projection bound to this MIMI room binding.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the binding. Initial status MUST be proposed or accepted; legal transitions are defined in zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2. accepted bindings authorize projection; revoked bindings stop new MIMI writes; migrating stops new writes until a verified migration proof returns the binding to accepted or revoked.

effective_scope.description: Governance boundary for the report. Defaults to the Realm scope when absent; Circle-scoped targets MUST resolve to the target Circle and route only to scoped moderators/admins.

moderation_decision_payload.description: Payload for ck.moderation.decision. An sealed moderation decision that writes an or_set add effect onto the ck.component.moderation_state.v1 cell whose subject is target_ref (the moderated target_event_id / target_object_id canonical string). See zh/authz/policy-server.md §7.1 and zh/governance/content-moderation.md §2.6 / §8.1. The decision verb is the runtime result set hard_deny / soft_deny / quarantine / require_review (all lower snake_case; allow is never sealed and soft_deny does not itself write the cell). The optional action carries the finer-grained §5.3 moderation_policy action family. The actor MUST independently hold ck.realm.moderation_policy or ck.policy.manage; refs[role=authorized_by] SHOULD reference the Policy Server signed decision for audit (not a capability source).

target_ref.description: The moderated target (event / object). Canonical string of this ref is the ck.component.moderation_state.v1 cell subject.

decision.description: Runtime decision verb (content-moderation.md §2.5 / §8.1). Lower snake_case; implementations MUST NOT introduce uppercase or camelCase variants.

issuer.description: Actor or service DID issuing the sealed moderation decision. Reducers use it as part of the or_set add tag and appeal separation-of-duties check.

request_canonical_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the moderated request or event preview bound to the Policy Server decision. Part of the moderation_state or_set add tag.

action.description: Optional finer-grained §5.3 moderation_policy action family entry that the decision verb maps to (content-moderation.md §8.1).

reason_code.description: Machine-readable diagnostic. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes.

policy_decision_ref.description: Reference to the Policy Server signed decision used as risk evidence. Audit / replay only; not a capability source.

modify_decision_ref.description: Set when this decision is the new decision emitted atomically by an appeal verdict=modify (content-moderation.md §5.5.2); reducer verifies it matches the same-batch appeal event id.

moderation_decision_lift_payload.description: Payload for ck.moderation.decision.lift. Writes an or_set remove effect on the same ck.component.moderation_state.v1 cell, removing the tag previously added by the decision identified by decision_ref. See zh/authz/policy-server.md §7.1 and zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.2 (appeal verdict=overturn MUST pair a lift whose target equals decision_ref in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction).

target_ref.description: The moderated target whose ck.component.moderation_state.v1 cell the lift mutates. Same cell subject as the original ck.moderation.decision.

decision_ref.description: Reference to the prior ck.moderation.decision Event whose sealed tag is being removed.

audit_applet_binding_payload.description: Payload for ck.audit.applet_binding. Declares a non-retroactive audit applet/service binding for a Realm or Circle effective_scope. Binding is control-plane only and does not make the applet an MLS member or realtime sync recipient. Messages encrypted before activation_frontier_digest / first_auditable_epoch are never eligible for this binding's ck.audit.release.

activation_frontier_digest.description: Accepted Seal coverage digest at which this binding/policy became member-visible. Release requests MUST NOT cover messages or epochs before this coverage point.

first_auditable_epoch.description: First MLS epoch eligible for this binding. Reducers MUST verify it is the epoch created by a ck.mls.commit covering activation_frontier_digest; earlier epochs are permanently ineligible.

retroactive_release.description: v1 audited E2EE never permits a later binding or policy expansion to make pre-activation messages auditable.

eligibility_basis.description: A message is eligible only if it was encrypted after a commit covering this binding/policy frontier.

max_lookback_ms.description: Optional maximum age, measured from session request/authorization time, for otherwise eligible material. Later policy changes may narrow this for future messages but MUST NOT expand already encrypted messages.

max_epoch_span.description: Optional cap on the number of sealed historical epochs a single session/release may cover.

allowed_target_classes.description: Optional target class allow-list for targeted_evidence_release.

audit_session_payload.description: Shared payload class for ck.audit.session.request / authorize / notice / close. The stage field identifies which lifecycle step this event represents; reducers validate the step-specific state machine against the enclosing Event.kind.

approved_recipient_audit_actor_id.description: Audit subject approved to receive release material. Required on ck.audit.session.authorize; ck.audit.release.recipient_audit_actor_id MUST match it byte-for-byte.

approved_recipient_public_key_ref.description: Audit release recipient key approved by ck.audit.session.authorize. MUST resolve to approved_recipient_audit_actor_id's authorized audit-release key; ck.audit.release.recipient_public_key_ref MUST match it byte-for-byte.

audit_release_payload.description: Payload for ck.audit.release. A sealed audit release manifest for a bounded historical window. It records release metadata and wrapped material digests only; plaintext MUST NOT be inlined.

recipient_public_key_ref.description: Release material encryption target. MUST equal the authorize payload's approved_recipient_public_key_ref and resolve to recipient_audit_actor_id's authorized audit-release key.

eligibility_proof.description: Proof summary that the requested release is inside the binding activation frontier, first_auditable_epoch, release_window_policy, and the targets' encryption-time eligibility snapshots.

activation_commit_ref.description: ck.mls.commit that covered the activation frontier and created first_auditable_epoch, when the release covers MLS epoch material.

policy_snapshot_digest.description: Digest of the binding/release window policy snapshot used when authorizing this release.

target_eligibility_digest.description: Digest of the deterministic per-target/per-epoch eligibility set proving no pre-activation material is included.

audit_accessed_payload.description: Strict payload for ck.audit.accessed. It records a specific access or paired privacy-sensitive write. Reducers MUST reject business events that require an audit pair unless this payload identifies the same writer, target, and object/cell in the same ordered submit batch, equivalent control transaction, or an accepted pre-read event with RYW receipt.

late_recovery_original_event_id.description: Required when access_kind=e2ee_late_recovery; identifies the original encrypted event whose plaintext became available through late key recovery.

ryw_required.description: When true, plaintext release or privileged projection MUST wait for an accepted-history RYW receipt before disclosure.

participant_binding.description: Token issuer's signed commitment over (realm_id, call_id, focus_id, actor_id, device_id, participant_identity, expires_at) for a media participant. See crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3 and crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1. v1 uses the single scheme ck.media.participant_binding.v1.

issuer_kid.description: DID URL (with fragment) of the token issuer service signing key. MUST resolve to a service DID present in the current-epoch ck.realm.media_service.service_id.

call_participant.description: A single participant entry in ck.call.state.payload.participants[]. See crypto-media/call-state.md §4/§4.1.

foci_preferred.description: Client-local ordered focus preference list used for the session_focus election (see crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1 and media-service-binding.md §5).

call_state_payload.description: Typed payload for ck.call.state (durable call lifecycle state). state is a controlled enum, participants carry machine-checkable participant_binding, and recording results are carried in a typed recording_result object. See crypto-media/call-state.md §4/§4.1/§5.

session_focus.description: Single authoritative focus_id for this call. reducer write rule per crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1: committed once, any rewrite MUST failed_precondition reason=session_focus_already_committed.

removed_participants.description: Moderator kick / ban audit trail. Each entry records a participant removed by a ck.call.moderate holder. action=ban omits device_id (actor-wide ban); a banned actor MUST NOT be re-issued a join token (call_participant_removed). See crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §3a.

participant_mute_overrides.description: Current durable moderator mute overrides. Each entry records the effective server-enforced audio/video send permission override for one call leg. SFU/token issuer MUST apply these overrides before issuing or accepting media send permissions; clients MUST mirror them locally. See crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §6.1.

recording_state.description: Recording lifecycle, orthogonal to `state` (the recording dimension of a call, independent of call lifecycle). Absent = no recording. 'recording' = capture in progress (after ck.call.recording.start); 'stopped' = recording manually stopped without requiring an artifact; 'ready' = artifact available via the Cokret blob pipeline; 'failed' = recording failed. recording_result SHOULD accompany recording_state ∈ {stopped, ready, failed}. See crypto-media/call-state.md §5.

recording_result.description: Typed recording outcome, present when recording_state ∈ {stopped, ready, failed}. See crypto-media/call-state.md §4.2 / §5: the durable ck.call.state carries recording_start_event_id for every terminal recording segment, and carries content digest, duration, media type, retention policy and a typed artifact when an artifact exists. All fields optional at schema level; prose defines state-specific requirements.

artifact.description: Canonical artifact metadata for recording_state=ready. It binds the Cokret blob, recording exporter context, retention policy and deletion audit surface.

failure_message.description: Human-readable diagnostic for recording_state=failed. It MUST NOT contain recording plaintext or backend direct URLs.

transcript_state.description: Transcription lifecycle, orthogonal to both `state` and `recording_state`. Absent = no transcription. 'transcribing' = capture in progress (after ck.call.transcribe.start); 'stopped' = manually stopped without requiring an artifact; 'ready' = encrypted transcript artifact available via the Cokret blob pipeline; 'failed' = transcription failed. transcript_result SHOULD accompany transcript_state ∈ {stopped, ready, failed}. See crypto-media/call-state.md §5.1.

transcript_result.description: Typed transcription outcome, present when transcript_state ∈ {stopped, ready, failed}. The transcript artifact is encrypted with the MLS-Exporter label ck-rtc-transcript-key/v1 (see exporter-label-registry.json) and strands through the same Cokret blob pipeline as recordings. transcript_start_event_id binds this segment to its ck.call.transcribe.start. All fields optional at schema level; prose defines state-specific requirements. See crypto-media/call-state.md §5.1.

call_summary_payload.description: Typed payload for ck.call.summary (durable end-of-call summary). Written once after a call reaches a terminal `state`; carries duration, peak participant count, and capture status so clients can render a durable call record without replaying ephemeral signaling. See crypto-media/call-state.md §7. started_at/ended_at/duration_ms are nullable: non-active terminal states (missed/cancelled/failed) MUST set them null per call-state.md §7.

final_state.description: The terminal call lifecycle state this summary closes over. MUST be one of the call_state_payload terminal states.

peak_participant_count.description: Highest concurrent participant count observed during the call.

distinct_participant_count.description: Number of distinct (actor_id, device_id) participants that joined at any point.

recording_state.description: Final recording_state at call end, mirrored from ck.call.state for the durable record. Absent = the call was not recorded.

transcript_state.description: Final transcript_state at call end, mirrored from ck.call.state. Absent = the call was not transcribed.

call_recording_start_payload.description: Typed payload for ck.call.recording.start. recording_id is a stable opaque ASCII handle (1–128 bytes, [A-Za-z0-9._-]) that feeds the recording key exporter Context byte-for-byte and MUST NOT be normalized by receivers. capture_kind selects recording vs transcription so both lifecycles share one start event kind. See crypto-media/call-state.md §5 / §5.1.

recording_id.description: Stable opaque recording / transcript lifecycle handle. Canonical byte-for-byte; receivers MUST NOT normalize (case-fold, NFC/NFKC, trim, re-encode) because it is a cross-implementation key-derivation input.

capture_kind.description: Whether this start event opens a recording or a transcription segment. Absent defaults to recording for backward compatibility.

visible_notice.description: Asserts the initiating client will display the capture-in-progress notice to all participants.

board_space_id.description: Board Space that owns the position edge; deduplication key (board_space_id, strand_id) MUST be unique among active edges.

from_space_id.description: Source List Space (optional; reducer infers from current active edge if omitted).

target_space_id.description: Target List Space after move. This is the ONLY payload-level field for the destination; the reducer compiles it into the cas_register cell value as 'list_space_id' on the cell at ck:cell:ck.component.strand.position.v1:<board_space_id>:<strand_id>. Writers MUST NOT put 'list_space_id' directly on the ck.strand.move payload (additionalProperties=false enforces this) — there is exactly one destination input field on the wire.

space_id.description: List Space within which the reorder happens.

strand_watch_set_payload.description: Payload for ck.strand.watch.set. Writes the (strand_id, watcher_actor_id) watch cell. The new cell value is computed from payload.level + payload.level_public: when level is null the effect is set null (clear, equivalent to mentions_only); when level is a string the effect is set { level, level_public? }. Reducer invariants: (1) watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope.actor_id unless writer holds ck.strand.watch.set.others; (2) when watcher_actor_id != envelope.actor_id (.others write), level MUST be one of {mentions_only, participating, all} and level_public MUST be omitted or false — writing muted or level_public=true on behalf of another actor MUST failed_precondition; (3) .others writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ck.audit.accessed event whose payload access_kind=watch_set_others identifies writer / target / cell / before-after heads. See models/strand-and-message.md §8.4.

level.description: Watch level. Required. null clears the cell (equivalent to mentions_only / no record); in that case level_public MUST be omitted.

level_public.description: Opt-in publication of the level value to non-self projection consumers. Default false. muted MUST NOT be exposed even with level_public=true. MUST be omitted when level is null.

expected_value.description: Compiles to cas_register head_eq precondition. Whole-value compare against the cell pre-state: either null (assert no prior record) or { level, level_public? } matching the prior cell value exactly. When omitted, reducers MUST treat it as head_eq null: only the initial write may pass; an existing cell MUST fail_precondition. Omission MUST NOT disable CAS or imply last-write-wins.

allOf.description: level_public MUST be omitted when level is null (clearing a cell does not carry a public-level setting).

schemas/file-transfer.schema.json.title: Cokret File Transfer Account Data
schemas/file-transfer.schema.json.description: Plaintext shape that MUST be encrypted before writing ck.profile.file_transfer.v1 account-data values.

content_digest.description: Digest of the stored blob bytes. For encrypted file transfer this is the ciphertext digest and MUST NOT be a plaintext file hash.

blob_size_bytes.description: Size of the stored blob bytes, usually ciphertext plus AEAD overhead.

media_type.description: Original file media type. This field lives inside encrypted account data; encrypted blob metadata SHOULD use application/octet-stream.

plaintext_size_bytes.description: Original file byte length before client-side encryption.

oneOf.$comment: whole-file AEAD form: single nonce, no stream segment parameters
streaming chunked AEAD form: nonce_prefix and fixed segment parameters, no whole-file nonce

content_key.description: Fresh per-transfer content key carried only inside encrypted account-data plaintext.

oneOf.$comment: whole-file file-transfer key message: single nonce, no stream segment parameters
streaming file-transfer key message: nonce_prefix and fixed segment parameters, no whole-file nonce

enc.description: HPKE KEM encapsulated key for the recipient device.

schemas/grant-constraint.schema.json.title: Cokret Grant Constraint
schemas/grant-constraint.schema.json.$comment: Property ordering is grouped by constraint family to match capabilities.md §6 (the human-readable family map): discriminator/meta, then temporal, field_access, type_restriction, scope_limitation, delegation_control, quota, claim_based, confidentiality, then the moderation cache-invalidation hint. Canonical JSON re-sorts keys lexicographically so this ordering is presentation-only and does not affect the wire (see C13-07).

constraint_id.description: Optional stable identifier of this constraint within the grant; used for diagnostics and overrides.

constraint_type.description: Constraint family discriminator. v1 collapses what were 15 types into 8 by absorbing narrowly-scoped types into their conceptual parent: edit_window → temporal; container_move → scope_limitation; rate_limiting + resource_limit → quota; approval_workflow + accountability + device_session → claim_based (with subtype); encryption_requirement + visibility_control → confidentiality (with subtype). Use the optional 'subtype' field to indicate the original specialization where evaluation logic differs.

evaluation_class.description: Cacheability/dependency hint for the authorization evaluator. stateless = pure function of (constraint, op, now); grant_local = depends on the grant object only; realm_state = depends on Realm frontier (membership, policy_version, etc.); external = depends on data outside the Realm causal frontier (claim revocation status, rate-limit history counts, async approval). Each constraint_type has a canonical evaluation_class declared in constraint-schema.md §2.3; implementations MAY tighten (e.g. grant_local → stateless) but MUST NOT loosen (e.g. external as stateless). Auth evaluators SHOULD use this hint to gate fast-path caching.

subtype.description: Optional discriminator within a constraint_type. Standard values: claim_based.{claim,approval,accountability}; quota.{rate,resource}; confidentiality.{encryption,visibility}; temporal.{window,edit_window,redact_window,session}. Per constraint-schema.md §2.2, device/session binding is NOT an independent subtype: it is the claim_based subtype=claim sub-case expressed via claim issuer = device cross-signing key. Implementations MAY require subtype for these families and fail closed on unknown values.

applies_to_actions.description: Optional restriction of a temporal constraint to specific capability actions (e.g. ['ck.message.revise.own', 'ck.message.redact.own']).

recurrence.description: Recurrence rule for temporal constraints. Used by constraint-schema.md §3.1.

expires_after.description: ISO 8601 duration; used by approval_workflow constraint instead of expires_after_ms.

condition.description: Conditional predicate for field_access and similar constraints. The `kind` value is a registered named condition from constraint-schema.md §4.1; unknown kinds MUST fail closed. Implementations MUST NOT introduce ad hoc string DSL predicates.

allowed_space_kinds.description: Allowed Space kinds (e.g. 'board', 'list', or profile-registered kinds like 'swimlane', 'calendar_bucket'). Reducer/profile MUST validate kind value.

allowed_circle_ids.description: Limits Circle-scoped capability actions to the listed Circle ids. Used by ck.circle.manage / ck.circle.member.manage style grants; unconstrained Realm-wide Circle management grants are not a normal permission shape.

allowed_session_ids.description: Limits agent interop-session status/result/cancel delegation to the listed ck:agent_interop_session ids.

blob_presign_scope.description: Scope limiter for ck.self.blob.command.presign grants: allowed purposes plus optional blob/realm restrictions.

allowed_data_classes.description: Data classification labels this grant may read, export, transform, or send to external endpoints.

allowed_endpoints.description: Allowed outbound endpoint origins or deployment-approved endpoint patterns for applet / agent / connector operations.

max_delegation_depth.description: Maximum remaining delegation hops. Bounded by the canonical delegation chain depth ceiling (4) defined in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md §3 and zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.2; reducers MUST reject grants declaring a larger value at accept time rather than only truncating during DFS.

blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds.description: Maximum TTL, in seconds, that this grant permits for ck.blob.presign. The service must clamp requested max_age_seconds to the smaller of this value and deployment policy.

max_artifact_bytes.description: Maximum artifact size in bytes for applet / agent / export operations.

requires_claims.description: Conditional claim requirements. resource-selector-grammar.md §3.3 caps this array at 32 entries as a normative DoS guard; the schema enforces maxItems:32 so condition-selector grants cannot smuggle in unbounded claim objects.

subject_matches_actor.description: If true, the credential subject DID MUST match the actor DID.

value_constraints.description: Per-field equality / membership constraints on credential claims.

min_encryption_level.description: confidentiality(subtype=encryption) static floor: the minimum content-encryption mechanism the grant requires. Values mirror Realm/Circle encryption_profile. Pure static declaration evaluated as stateless unless cross-checked against the Realm's current encryption_profile (see constraint-schema.md §12).

allow_plaintext_fallback.description: confidentiality(subtype=encryption) static flag: whether the grant permits plaintext when the encryption floor cannot be met. See constraint-schema.md §12.

require_audit_trail.description: confidentiality(subtype=encryption) static flag: whether the grant requires an audit trail (e.g. active Audit Applet Binding). See constraint-schema.md §12.

depends_on_moderation_state.description: Cache-invalidation hint: when true, this grant's authorization decisions depend on the ck.component.moderation_state.v1 cell (see policy-server.md §7.1 and capabilities.md §18.1) and the grant's cache entry MUST be invalidated when that cell changes. Default false: ordinary grants (ck.strand.update / ck.message.create / org membership grants) do NOT take a cache hit on every moderation decision. v1 capabilities.md §18.1 lists three conditions where MUST be explicitly true (moderator-role grants, condition-selector subjects referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue / cell). Schema-side enforcement of condition (2) is in capability-grant.schema.json via if/then on actions[]; conditions (1) and (3) are reducer-side lint. Cache invalidation hint outside the eight constraint families; it does not participate in allow/deny evaluation and is documented in capabilities.md §6 / constraint-schema.md.

allOf.$comment: constraint-schema.md §2.2 / §2.3: claim_based, confidentiality and quota families have NO valid no-subtype form — every row in the §2.3 evaluation_class table carries a subtype (claim/approval/accountability; encryption/visibility; rate/resource). Without this gate a {"constraint_type":"claim_based","effect":"allow"} with no subtype passes schema validation, letting weak implementations cache an external (claim-revocation) constraint on the grant_local fast path (see C05-03 fail-open). temporal is intentionally excluded: a temporal constraint with no subtype is the valid ordinary time-window form.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Aligned with schema-registry.json; lets validators / contract-catalog consumers disambiguate this claim from other DID-bearing envelopes.

handle.description: Cokret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. The @ mention sigil and acct: alias are not part of this field. This pattern is intentionally ASCII-only: it validates the post-IDNA canonical form, where <domain> is the A-label (punycode, xn-- prefix) and <localpart> is the lowercase restricted-ASCII canonical form. Unicode NFC normalization and UTS#39 confusable / script-mixing homograph detection (see zh/identity/identity-handles.md §17) MUST be applied to the U-label BEFORE IDNA conversion; they are not (and cannot be) re-enforced by this ASCII pattern.

handle_aliases.description: Interop aliases such as RFC 7565 acct:. Aliases are never canonical; verifiers MUST normalize to handle before cache lookup, proof comparison, or delivery_binding construction.

subject.description: Holder/principal DID for a user/principal handle. This is the stable DID the handle resolves to; it is not a Realm actor_id, server-local account_id, administrative identifier, service DID, or generic resource id.

issuer_service_did.description: Service DID that signed, served, or vouched for this handle claim when distinct from issuer.

claim_kind.description: Protocol-level kind of holder/principal handle claim. v1 intentionally does not allow the earlier draft service_handle value: service-readable names or resource labels need their own service/resource schema, while organization-assigned user/principal handles use organization_handle.

visibility.description: Default disclosure boundary for this handle claim.

audience.description: Audience binding for the claim. For handle claims used to build a Realm delivery_binding, audience is the target Realm ID, the inviting service DID, or another verifier domain the proofs explicitly bind to. Verifier MUST reject claims whose audience does not match the current invocation context.

claim_scope.description: Optional claim_scope such as organization_id, realm_id, purpose, or allowed operations.

member_delivery_binding.description: Single source for the Principal Server service DID and delivery parameters this handle claim offers to the membership builder. Top-level delivery shortcuts are forbidden; use member_delivery_binding.recipient_service_did, member_delivery_binding.service_acceptance_ref, and member_delivery_binding.policy_event_ref.

schemas/ice-config-response.schema.json.title: Cokret Media ICE Config Result
schemas/ice-config-response.schema.json.description: Result shape for the WebRTC media service ICE config endpoint. Used by ck.profile.webrtc_media.v1; see crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §4.

realm_id.description: Echo of the request Realm id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-Realm replay.

call_id.description: Echo of the request call id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-call replay.

actor_id.description: Actor that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

device_id.description: Device that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

ice_servers.description: STUN / TURN server entries the client may use during this call.

ttl_seconds.description: Validity window for the issued credentials in seconds. Clients MUST refresh before this expires; servers SHOULD pick a value <= 1 hour for normal calls.

refresh_lead_seconds.description: Minimum lead time before ttl expiry at which the client SHOULD initiate refresh. refresh_lead_seconds MUST be strictly less than ttl_seconds (servers MUST NOT issue refresh_lead_seconds >= ttl_seconds, otherwise the client would judge the credential stale at issuance and storm refresh). Defaults SHOULD be ttl_seconds / 4. The recommended floor (60s) applies only when ttl_seconds is large enough that floor < ttl_seconds still holds; for small ttl (e.g. the 60s minimum) the server MUST shrink refresh_lead_seconds below ttl_seconds (see webrtc-signaling.md §4.2). Required so all clients refresh at consistent cadence and servers can plan secret rotation grace windows.

issued_at.description: Server-issued timestamp (RFC 3339 UTC). Bound into the ICE config signature.

issued_at_bucket.description: Coarse UTC bucket start used for TURN pseudonym derivation. MUST equal floor(issued_at / bucket_seconds) * bucket_seconds. Bound into the signature so TURN usernames cannot be correlated across buckets by rewriting metadata.

bucket_seconds.description: TURN pseudonym bucket size in seconds. v1 fixes the default and interoperable value at 300s; clients SHOULD refresh before crossing the next bucket.

expires_at.description: Convenience field equal to issued_at + ttl_seconds. MUST match within signature validation.

force_turn.description: When true, clients MUST disable host/srflx ICE candidates and only relay through TURN. Used by high-privacy Realms to prevent IP leakage.

next_retry_at.description: Set when the response is a soft failure (e.g. turn_credential_expired). Clients MUST NOT retry before this time.

signature.description: Detached signature by the media service DID over the canonical bytes of this response (excluding `signature`).

urls.description: STUN/TURN server URL(s). Schemes: stun:, stuns:, turn:, turns:.

username.description: TURN ephemeral credential username. v1: <expiry-unix>:<per-call-pseudonym>. MUST NOT contain principal DID, handle, email, or any cross-call stable identifier.

credential.description: TURN ephemeral credential password (HMAC-SHA256 of username with per-tenant turn shared secret in REST-style).

kid.description: Verification method id, typically <media_service_did>#<key-id>. Bare DID is accepted (resolves to the controller's current key); DID URLs with key fragment are RECOMMENDED. The optional `#<key-id>` fragment is allowed (charset aligned with the token-exchange service_signature.kid pattern).

alg.description: Signature algorithm. Values MUST be active proof_alg entries in signature-alg-registry.json. Default v1 deployments use EdDSA; stronger or deployment-specific profiles MAY require another registered algorithm while preserving the exact signing input defined in webrtc-signaling.md §4.1.

signature_input.description: Domain-separation label prepended to the ICE config signing bytes. v1 fixes this to ck.media.ice_config.v1 and it MUST NOT be reused for participant binding signatures.

payload_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the RFC 8785 canonical ICE config response object with the top-level signature field removed. This is the canonical payload covered after the signature_input label and 0x00 separator.

sig.description: base64url-encoded detached signature over canonical response bytes.

schemas/identity-link.schema.json.title: Cokret Minimal-Metadata Identity Link
schemas/identity-link.schema.json.description: Encrypted application-message or MLS private-extension payload that binds a Realm-scoped pairwise DID to the real principal DID for ck.profile.mls.minimal_metadata_realm.v1. The binding is scoped to both realm_id and trust_domain so the same pairwise mapping cannot be replayed across deployments. This object is never written to public Realm history unless a separate disclosure policy explicitly permits it.

pairwise_did.description: Realm-scoped pairwise DID used in Event.actor_id and MLS leaf credential. The v1 boundary is the Realm, not a Matrix-style Room.

principal_id.description: Real principal DID that controls or has disclosed the pairwise DID.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain. Receiver MUST require this value to match the current Realm / service trust_domain before accepting a pairwise DID -> principal DID mapping.

strand_id.description: Optional application-message context marker for the Strand carrying the identity link. It does not create independent membership or key scope; key scope is determined by effective_scope.

track_name.description: Optional display-track context marker for application routing. Track names do not create independent membership, policy, or MLS key scope.

mls_group_id.description: Optional MLS group identifier (base64url RFC 9420 GroupID) for diagnostic / cross-implementation correlation. NOT used by the reducer for authorization — authoritative MLS group state lives in ck.mls.genesis / ck.mls.commit events. Provided here so audit projections can quickly correlate an identity-link with its MLS group without replaying the full epoch chain.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a key controlled by principal_id or by a disclosure proof accepted by Realm policy. Fragment is REQUIRED (this is a DID URL, not a bare DID). DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical input bytes: utf8('ck-identity-link-v1\n') || canonical_json(identity-link object with proof.signature omitted). The signed object includes trust_domain.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Aligned with schema-registry.json; lets validators distinguish identity registry receipts from other receipt envelopes (e.g. audit-ryw-receipt, event-batch-receipt).

witness_role.description: Issuer's role in the DID registry consensus group. Required so verifiers can apply role-specific freshness / quorum rules; an absent role would force the verifier to guess writer vs replica semantics.

audience.description: Optional audience binding (verifier DID, service DID, or domain). When present, verifiers MUST reject the receipt outside that audience context to prevent cross-protocol reuse.

schemas/inclusion-list.schema.json.title: Cokret InclusionList
schemas/inclusion-list.schema.json.description: FOCIL-style control-plane inclusion list. A non-proposer notary signer lists pending Control Move digests that passed its local verification; the next Seal MUST include, signed-reject, or prove batch pre-state verification failure for every listed digest, otherwise receivers MUST reject that Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.3). single_did notary profiles cannot provide this mechanism. The list is an accountability object, not a Seal: it never advances governance state by itself.

signer_id.description: Notary signer issuing the list. MUST be an eligible non-proposer signer of the Realm's multi-signer notary profile at issue time.

list_seq.description: Per-signer monotonic inclusion-list sequence. Two different canonical lists from the same signer with the same (realm_id, list_seq) constitute equivocation evidence under the section 7.1 slot rule.

event_digests.description: Canonical ascending list of pending Control Move event digests that passed the issuer's local verification and hold a valid receipt.

expiry_seal_count.description: Number of subsequent Seals within which the obligation must be discharged. Default deployment value is 1 (the next Seal).

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical InclusionList bytes with signature omitted.

schemas/invite-delivery-request.schema.j.title: Cokret Invite Delivery Request
schemas/invite-delivery-request.schema.j.description: Private service-to-service request used by an inviter-side Principal Server to deliver a Realm invite to the invitee-side Principal Server. The request carries an explicit invite address and introduction evidence; raw locator tokens are never written into durable Realm events.

invite_event.description: The ck.invite.create EventEnvelope or equivalent accepted event view being delivered.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the invite recipient. v1 core defaults principal DIDs to did:webvh; did:web is only valid for principal identity when an explicit deployment profile or resolver policy allows it.

recipient_service_did.description: Principal Server service DID that accepts invite delivery for subject_id.

recipient_service_type.description: v1 only allows Principal Server invite delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.
v1 only allows Principal Server invite delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.

consent_grant_ref.description: Event ref of the invitee-issued ck.consent.grant (scope invite or any) that authorizes the inviter to send Realm/Strand invites. High-trust evidence: it is material the invitee actively issued to the inviter, equivalent in trust to a locator_ref.

consent_id.description: Optional consent cell id locating the holder consent cell, to speed up receiver verification of the active grant dot.

handle.description: Canonical handle string the inviter used as the human-readable entry point.

handle_claim.description: Verified handle claim proving that handle resolves to invite_address.subject_id. The receiver MUST verify binding_state, proofs, expiry, issuer trust, visibility/audience policy, and that handle_claim.handle equals handle.

member_delivery_binding_candidate.description: Optional builder evidence returned by a Directory or trusted issuer for intent=invite. When present, verifiers MUST check subject_id, handle, recipient_service_did, audience, issuer_service_did, expiry and proofs against this delivery.

resolved_by.description: Optional Directory or issuer service DID that supplied the handle resolution.

status.description: Generic receive status. It MUST NOT reveal whether subject_id exists or whether policy quarantined/dropped the invite unless receiver policy explicitly allows disclosure via disclosed_outcome.

disclosed_outcome.description: Optional graded-disclosure result. Present ONLY when the subject invite_receive_policy disclosure level for this introduction trust tier is 'outcome'. Omitted (opaque) for low-trust tiers and always omitted for blocked_subjects hits. delivered: invite reached the holder surface awaiting acceptance; blocked: rejected by block list or policy; quarantined: held for review.

schemas/invite-receive-policy.schema.jso.title: Cokret Invite and Contact Receive Policy
schemas/invite-receive-policy.schema.jso.description: Subject-private policy used by a Principal Server to decide which invite delivery or first-contact request introduction evidence may notify the holder. This policy is not written into the target Realm durable event log or the public contact fact log.

subject_id.description: Principal DID whose private invite receive policy this object configures. v1 core defaults principal DIDs to did:webvh; did:web is only valid for principal identity when an explicit deployment profile or resolver policy allows it.

allowed_introduction_kinds.description: Allowlist of introduction evidence kinds that may reach holder notification or review.

explicit_address_behavior.description: Default behavior for explicit_address evidence. Deployments SHOULD default to quarantine or drop, not notify.

handle_claim_behavior.description: Default behavior for handle_claim evidence. Omitted means quarantine. A subject MAY set notify to allow verified handle-based requests to reach the holder, but the effective value is capped by receive_policy_constraints.

unknown_invites.description: Behavior for invite/contact delivery requests without compliant introduction_evidence.

allowed_handle_domains.description: Optional subject-private allowlist for canonical handle domains accepted as handle_claim evidence. Empty or omitted means no subject-level domain restriction; deployment constraints may still restrict the effective set.

blocked_handle_domains.description: Subject-private denylist for canonical handle domains. Matches are rejected before allowed_handle_domains is evaluated.

trusted_handle_issuers.description: Optional subject-private allowlist of handle claim issuers accepted for handle_claim evidence.

trusted_directory_services.description: Optional subject-private allowlist of Directory service DIDs accepted as resolved_by for handle_claim evidence.

blocked_subjects.description: Per-subject block list (peer principal DIDs). Invite delivery whose inviter is in this list MUST be dropped, and disclosure MUST be forced to opaque regardless of the disclosure policy, to avoid leaking the block via a side channel.

disclosure.description: Graded disclosure policy. Controls whether the invite/contact delivery outcome reveals a real result (delivered/blocked/quarantined) to the requester, by introduction trust tier. Omitted means the default: high_trust=outcome, discovery_trust=opaque, low_trust=opaque.

domain_name.description: Canonical IDNA A-label domain. Subdomains are not implied; list each accepted domain explicitly.

disclosure_level.description: opaque: only a generic accepted-for-processing status is returned, indistinguishable across exists/not-exists/policy outcomes. outcome: the real delivered/blocked/quarantined result is disclosed to the inviter.

high_trust.description: Disclosure level for the high-trust introduction tier: consent_grant, locator_ref, shared_realm. Default outcome.

discovery_trust.description: Disclosure level for public or restricted discovery evidence: handle_claim. Default opaque.

low_trust.description: Disclosure level for the low-trust introduction tier: same_principal_server, explicit_address, and missing/non-compliant evidence. Default opaque.

receive_policy_constraints.description: Deployment/admin upper bound applied to subject-private receive policies. The effective receive policy is the intersection of the subject policy and these constraints; constraints can only make a subject less reachable, never more reachable.

applies_to.description: Surfaces governed by this constraint object. Omitted means both invite_delivery and contact_request.

permitted_introduction_kinds.description: Maximum set of introduction evidence kinds this deployment permits. Omitted means no deployment-level kind cap.

handle_claim_max_behavior.description: Maximum behavior allowed for handle_claim evidence using the order drop < quarantine < notify.

explicit_address_max_behavior.description: Maximum behavior allowed for explicit_address evidence using the order drop < quarantine < notify.

allowed_handle_domains.description: Deployment-level allowlist for handle domains accepted as handle_claim evidence. Empty means no handle domain is accepted.

invite_delivery_target.description: Public durable target for private invite delivery. invitee is the subject; this object carries only the recipient Principal Server service DID.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Digest of private invite delivery introduction_evidence. Raw locator tokens and receive-policy state MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent invite state update.

third_party_invite.description: Wire-level 3PID/OOB invite binding. No plaintext email/phone/SMS code is allowed here. `oob_code_kind` distinguishes offline high-entropy token validation from server-side lookup short-code validation.

display_name_hint.description: Non-identifying UI hint only; MUST NOT contain plaintext 3PID.

token_commitment.description: Salted commitment to a high-entropy invite token. Required for offline_token mode.

token_salt_id.description: Opaque handle for the verification service's private salt record. The salt value itself MUST NOT appear on wire.

lookup_table_ref.description: Opaque verification-service lookup table reference for short-code mode. The raw short code MUST NOT appear on wire.

pepper_id.description: Server-private pepper generation identifier for lookup mode; the pepper value itself is never on wire.

oob_code_kind.description: offline_token means the out-of-band code is itself >=128-bit entropy and validated against token_commitment. lookup means the human-readable code is only an index into a server-private lookup table protected by rate limits and pepper/HMAC storage.

token_entropy_bits.description: Required for offline_token mode. Entropy estimate excluding separators.

verification_public_key.description: Ephemeral public key or DID verification method used by the verification service to sign claim results.

schemas/key-backup-active-series.schema..title: Cokret Key Backup Active Series Record
schemas/key-backup-active-series.schema..description: Signed principal-control record selecting the canonical backup series for one (actor_id, backup_class). This closes the rollback gap when multiple series exist after compromise rotation or migration. Receivers MUST verify this record before choosing a series from list results.

previous_series_ids.description: Retained old series used only for read-old-data or erasure transition. MUST NOT be treated as a primary recovery source.

frontier_ref.description: Principal control stream frontier under which active_series_id was selected.

signature.description: base64url signature over canonical_json(record without auth_data.signature).

ssk_generation.description: Accepted ck.cross_signing.publish.generation used to authorize this active-series selection.

schemas/key-backup-plaintext.schema.json.title: Cokret Key Backup Plaintext Keybag
schemas/key-backup-plaintext.schema.json.description: Canonical plaintext carried inside ck.schema.key_backup.v1 ciphertext after AEAD/HPKE open. The public envelope contents[] is only an index; this keybag is the import truth source.

secret_b64u.description: base64url(no padding) encoded secret bytes. The item_type and metadata define how receivers import the bytes.

schemas/key-backup-unlock-proof.schema.j.title: Cokret Key Backup Unlock Proof
schemas/key-backup-unlock-proof.schema.j.description: Proof presented before a recovery strand downloads or unlocks a key-backup envelope. It binds a backup read/decrypt action to one recovery_session_id, requesting device, backup object, selected series, ciphertext digest, and the proof transcript accepted by the recovery session.

proof_digest.description: Digest of the canonical recovery proof transcript that moved the session to verified.

challenge.description: Optional echo of the recovery-session challenge; when present it MUST match the session snapshot.

verification_method.description: DID URL for either the accepted requesting device key after authorization, or the recovery-session proof key before did_recovery unlock.

signature.description: base64url signature over canonical_json(unlock proof without auth_data.signature).

mixed_secret_storage.description: True only for the personal_node exception where one encrypted backup envelope contains both identity-signing material and E2EE / MLS history material. Non-personal deployment profiles MUST reject this flag. When true and recipient_method=passphrase_kdf, the stricter Argon2id floor below applies.

series_id.description: Stable identifier for one immutable chain of backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_class). A pair MAY have multiple series during compromise rotation or migration; active series selection is outside this envelope and MUST come from the signed active-series record in identity/key-management.md §7.6. Receivers use (actor_id, backup_class, series_id) to detect server-side rollback / withholding within the selected series.

series_seq.description: 0-based, strictly monotonically increasing sequence number within (actor_id, series_id). Genesis envelope of a series MUST set 0. Receivers MUST reject envelopes whose sequence does not strictly exceed the previously accepted sequence in the same series.

supersedes.description: backup_id of the immediate predecessor in the same series_id. MUST be absent for series_seq=0; MUST be present, non-null, and reference an existing predecessor for series_seq>0.

supersedes_digest.description: Required when supersedes is non-null. Hash of the canonical_json of the predecessor envelope (excluding auth_data.signature). Receivers MUST recompute and reject mismatches as `series_chain_broken`.

frontier_ref.description: Optional reference to the principal control stream frontier at envelope creation time. Improves rollback detection by sealing the envelope to a verifiable control-stream position.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Required for backup_class=did_recovery and optional as a signed recovery-strand hint for other backup classes. Binds the backup envelope to the active recovery policy version under which it was produced. Receivers MUST compare this tuple to the currently accepted recovery policy before using a did_recovery envelope; when present on other classes, mismatch fails as recovery_policy_mismatch but the field does not replace active-series, frontier, Realm/MLS authorization, or device-state checks. This is intentionally separate from frontier_ref and ssk_generation: it binds the recovery authorization surface, not only the device trust generation or control-stream position.

hpke_suite.description: Registered active HPKE suite (KEM x KDF x AEAD per RFC 9180) selector; the value space is the active rows of artifacts/registry/hpke-suite-registry.json. Applies only to recipient_method=recovery_public_key. When absent it denotes the default-MUST row ck.hpke_x25519_aead_xchacha20poly1305.v1. aead.name MUST equal the selected suite's AEAD. An unregistered or inactive suite MUST be rejected (unsupported_hpke_suite). Absent / ignored for the symmetric methods (passphrase_kdf / secret_storage_key).

aead_profile.description: Optional AEAD profile id that binds algorithm version, nonce length, tag length, key length, and AAD construction. Receivers that do not support the profile MUST fail closed instead of inferring semantics from name alone.

nonce.description: base64url AEAD nonce. Required for the symmetric methods (passphrase_kdf / secret_storage_key). For recipient_method=passphrase_kdf this MUST equal HMAC-SHA256(HKDF(derived_key, info='cokret-key-backup-aead-nonce-v1'), canonical_json({backup_id, actor_id, device_id, backup_class, backup_version, created_at, aead.name, aead.aead_profile?, aead.nonce_salt}))[0:N_AEAD]; receivers recompute and reject mismatches. Absent for recovery_public_key (HPKE derives its nonce internally).

nonce_salt.description: Producer-generated base64url random salt (at least 128 bits before encoding) included in the passphrase_kdf nonce derivation transcript. Required when recipient_method=passphrase_kdf; not secret, signed as envelope metadata, and prevents nonce reuse from duplicate business metadata tuples.

enc.description: base64url HPKE KEM encapsulated key. Required for recipient_method=recovery_public_key; the KEM/KDF/AEAD are pinned by encryption.hpke_suite (default ck.hpke_x25519_aead_xchacha20poly1305.v1) per artifacts/registry/hpke-suite-registry.json. Absent for the symmetric methods.

domain_separation.description: Signed key-backup domain separation transcript. Binds HKDF info and AEAD/HPKE AAD to the envelope fields used by key-management.md §7.1 / §7.5 so implementations do not infer subdomain semantics from ciphertext or local state.

recipient_method.description: SEC-04: the envelope's encryption.recipient_method bound into the AEAD AAD so a ciphertext can never be cross-opened under the wrong recipient interpretation. Sealer and opener reconstruct it byte-identically from the stored envelope; receivers MUST fail closed on a method/AAD mismatch.

recipient_key_ref.description: SEC-04: the envelope's encryption.recipient_key_ref (recipient key / verification method) bound into the AEAD AAD so the recipient identity is part of the authenticated context.

secret_version.description: Monotonic version of the backed-up secret (e.g. mls_account_secret). Used by clients for deterministic preferred-backup selection and anti-rollback ordering (key-management.md §9.1). Present on versioned secret items; absent on share-style items such as recovery_key_share.

verification_method.description: DID URL identifying the device signing key.

signature_algorithm.description: Raw signature algorithm name; MUST be a value generated from an active signature-alg-registry row (Ed25519 / ES256 / ML-DSA-65). EdDSA is the proof_alg label, not a raw signature_algorithm value. ML-DSA-65 is gated behind the PQ migration profile.

signature.description: base64url-encoded signature over canonical_json(envelope without auth_data.signature).

signed_fields.description: Names of envelope fields covered by the signature; MUST include backup_id, actor_id, backup_class, backup_version, series_id, series_seq, encryption, domain_separation, contents, ciphertext_digest, and when present supersedes, supersedes_digest, frontier_ref, and recovery_policy_ref.

ssk_generation.description: Accepted ck.cross_signing.publish.generation of the self-signing key generation that authorized the device signing this backup. Exactly one of auth_data.ssk_generation and auth_data.device_authorize_event_id identifies the device trust root.

device_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted ck.device.authorize event id anchoring the service_attested/enrollment-authority device signing this backup. Exactly one of auth_data.ssk_generation and auth_data.device_authorize_event_id identifies the device trust root.

then.description: mls_history backups MUST use secret_storage_key or recovery_public_key (key-management.md §7.5.2 / §7.5.3 and device-lifecycle.md §12); passphrase_kdf, threshold_recovery, hardware_wrapped_key, and the removed device_snapshot_secret are rejected. recovery_policy_ref MAY appear as a signed hint, but is not required for mls_history.

did_recovery backups MUST use recovery_public_key (key-management.md §5.0.1 first-backup gate), MUST carry recovery_policy_ref matching the active recovery policy, and MUST cover that field in auth_data.signed_fields. passphrase_kdf and secret_storage_key are forbidden for did_recovery; threshold_recovery and hardware_wrapped_key are recovery policy / proof-layer factors, not key-backup recipient methods.

schemas/key-view-proof.schema.json.title: Cokret KeyViewProof
schemas/key-view-proof.schema.json.description: Inclusion proof for one KeyView record against a Seal's data_view_root (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md sections 6.4 and 10). data_view_root is the RFC 6962 Merkle root over canonical KeyView leaves sorted by cell_id; this proof lets a light client verify 'this Seal observed and committed this local join result for this cell' without global state. The proof is observational: absence of a KeyView never invalidates a DataEvent, and verifiers MUST NOT treat it as finality.

data_view_root.description: MUST equal the data_view_root field of the referenced Seal; the verifier checks the Seal signature separately.

audit_path.description: RFC 6962 Merkle audit path from the canonical KeyView leaf to data_view_root. Leaf input is H(0x00 || canonical_json(key_view)); interior nodes are H(0x01 || left || right).

heads.description: Exposed head digests for multi-value cells. Mutually exclusive with value_digest.

value_digest.description: Digest of the canonical single join value. Mutually exclusive with heads.

last_covered_event.description: event_digest of the latest DataEvent the notary observed for this cell within the Seal window.

schemas/keypackage-operations.schema.jso.title: Cokret MLS KeyPackage Operation DTOs
schemas/keypackage-operations.schema.jso.description: Closed request and response DTOs for ck.keys.keypackages.{upload,claim,consume,revoke}. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.

object_ref.description: Opaque content-addressed or service-scoped reference. Hash-shaped refs MUST use keypackage_digest for digest bytes.

key_package.description: Base64url encoding of the canonical MLS KeyPackage bytes.

last_resort.description: When true, this entry is a reusable last-resort KeyPackage (RFC 9420 Section 10). It is not consumed single-use; it cycles between published and claimed until rotated, expired, or revoked. Optional capability gated by ck.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1. See encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

When true, this claim record returns a reusable last-resort KeyPackage (RFC 9420 Section 10) because the single-use pool was empty. The package may be reused within the same intended_realm_id and is not transitioned to consumed; the holder MUST rotate it and trigger group updates on next online. Optional capability gated by ck.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1. See encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

schemas/keys-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Device Key Operation DTOs
schemas/keys-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for ck.keys.{upload,query,claim} and ck.keys.backups.{put,list,delete}. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.

did_key.description: Authoritative device signing key as an Ed25519 did:key (multibase base58btc, multicodec ed25519-pub). Mirrors ck.device.authorize.payload.device_public_key (device-lifecycle.md §5.2 / §5.4). This is the verify key receivers resolve via verification_method `{actor}#{device_id}` where the fragment is the full ck:device:<uuidv7> id, to check ck.call.signal / ephemeral envelope and durable Event proofs.

device_status.description: Directory status of the (principal_id, device_id) pair at query time. active = device.authorize present and not revoked; revoked = a ck.device.revoke is in effect. Servers MUST omit device_signing_key for any non-active (revoked / unverified) device.

query_device_record.description: Per-(principal_id, device_id) entry in keys_query_outcome. Carries the prekey bundle under `algorithms` plus the convenience signing-key directory fields `device_signing_key` / `device_status` at the same level as the algorithm dimension (not repeated per algorithm). The directory facet is populated only for verified, non-revoked devices; see device-lifecycle.md §8.

hpke_key.description: The device HPKE public key used for secret / key envelope sealing, echoed verbatim from the authoritative ck.device.authorize.payload.hpke_key (device-lifecycle.md §5.2/§5.4). MUST only be returned for verified, non-revoked devices; services MUST NOT substitute this value in projection.

trust_algorithms.description: The canonical (UTF-8 bytewise sorted, deduplicated) algorithm ids echoed verbatim from ck.device.authorize.payload.algorithms; together with device_signing_key and hpke_key this is the material the §5.2 ck-device-trust-bind-v1 transcript covers. Distinct from the sibling `algorithms` prekey-bundle map.

device_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted ck.device.authorize event id anchoring the current device-set projection. For service_attested / enrollment-authority devices this pairs with enrollment_authority_binding and identifies the accepted authorization event whose payload.device_public_key is exposed as device_signing_key.

encryption.description: Non-secret recipient metadata so the client can categorize a backup (recovery_public_key vs passphrase_kdf vs secret_storage_key) without downloading the ciphertext. The aead/kdf material is withheld from the list summary.

cross_signing.description: Tier-2: {principal_id} -> that principal's current accepted-generation ck.cross_signing.publish payload (device-lifecycle.md §5.1). Lets receivers anchor the SSK to the DID control set before trusting cross_signing_binding. See device-lifecycle.md §8.3.

keys_backups_unlock_request_body.description: Request body for ck.self.keys.backups.command.unlock. The unlock proof MUST validate as ck.schema.key_backup_unlock_proof.v1 and MUST be verified against the recovery session, caller, requesting device key, active-series record, and target envelope before the full ciphertext is returned (key-management.md §7.7.1 / §7.8). The path backup_id and proof.backup_id MUST match.

cross_signing_binding.description:
Tier-2 device trust binding echoed from ck.device.authorize.payload.cross_signing_binding (device-lifecycle.md §5.2). The accepted-generation SSK signs `"ck-device-trust-bind-v1
" + canonical_json({principal_id, device_id, device_public_key, ssk_generation})`. Absent for inception bootstrap devices (§5.0.1).

verification_method.description: DID URL of the self-signing key (SSK) that produced the binding signature, e.g. did:webvh:...#ck_self_signing_v1.

ssk_generation.description: cross_signing.publish generation under which the SSK signed this device binding; compared to the principal's accepted generation per device-lifecycle.md §5.2.1.

schemas/list-handles-for-subject-respons.title: Cokret Directory Subject Handle List
schemas/list-handles-for-subject-respons.description: Result body for ck.find.directory.query.list_handles_for_subject. It lists currently visible handle claims for a disclosed holder/principal subject DID in the caller's context. Every claim in claims[] MUST have claim.subject byte-for-byte equal to this response subject.

subject.description: Holder/principal DID used as the reverse lookup key. This is not a Realm actor_id.

claims.description: Current context-visible signed handle claims. Each item MUST have subject equal to the top-level subject; mismatches MUST be dropped or fail the response closed.

primary_handle.description: Optional canonical primary handle selected from claims[] by identity-handles.md section 3.2.1 for the same context/as_of. The @ mention sigil is not part of this field.

as_of.description: As-of timestamp used to build the visible claim set and primary handle selection.

not.$comment: byte counts use size_bytes

thumbnails.description: Bound thumbnail / preview descriptors. Producers SHOULD prefer this over preview_blob_ref for private or E2EE media.

schemas/media-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Realtime Media Operation DTOs
schemas/media-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request DTOs for realtime media service operations. ck.self.media.query.ice_config responses use ice-config-response.schema.json.

schemas/member-delivery-binding-candidat.title: Cokret Member Delivery Binding Candidate
schemas/member-delivery-binding-candidat.description: Builder-side candidate object that ferries Handle resolution output (intent=member_add | invite) or a trusted-issuer-signed equivalent into the Realm member_add / invite pipeline. Produces a Realm-scoped member_delivery_binding only after the reducer independently re-validates against Join Policy. See identity-handles.md §3.7.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the addressee. Materialised as payload.actor_id / cell subject in ck.member.state{membership=join}.

handle.description: Cokret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. acct: aliases and @ mention spelling are rejected here.

handle_aliases.description: Optional interop aliases (RFC 7565 acct:). Never used for cache keys, signature transcripts, or delivery_binding materialisation.

binding_source.description: MUST NOT be did_document_default — handle-resolved candidates and DID Document fallback are independent materialisation paths.

issuer_service_did.description: Service DID that signed the candidate (Directory service DID, Principal Server service DID, or Organization service DID).

audience.description: Target Realm ID or inviting service DID. Verifier MUST reject candidates whose audience does not match the current invocation context.

issued_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp marking when the issuer signed the candidate. Required: paired with expires_at to give verifiers a replay-protection window and to detect retro-dated candidates. issued_at MUST be <= expires_at.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp. Expired candidates MUST NOT enter the builder.

source_refs.description: Event references at the issuer / Directory / Organization that back this candidate; clients SHOULD re-verify against the truth source.

proofs.description: At least one proof binding handle, subject_id, member_delivery_binding.recipient_service_did, audience, issuer_service_did, issued_at, expires_at and (when present) claim_digest. issued_at MUST be inside the signed transcript so an MITM cannot widen the replay-protection window by rewriting it; verifiers MUST reject proofs whose canonical transcript omits issued_at.

claim_digest.description: sha256 digest over JCS(semantic_projection(upstream handle claim)) per zh/identity/identity-handles.md ?3.2.1; it is not a digest over the whole upstream handle claim object.

intent.description: Builder entry point. Advisory for audit / telemetry; reducer behaviour does not branch on this field.

schemas/member-identity.schema.json.title: Cokret Member Identity
schemas/member-identity.schema.json.description: Realm-scoped, actor-scoped full member_identity segment. It is carried by ck.member.identity.update in plaintext or inside encrypted-envelope.schema.json. Replacement events that name segment=member_identity MUST carry this complete object. This object discloses subject_id and display_profile for Realm UI projection; handle lifecycle is intentionally excluded and is governed only by ck.schema.handle_claim.v1 issuer claims. Mention / reply / quote / actor attribution MUST use subject_id (the principal DID), never a handle string.

actor_id.description: Effective member actor DID in this Realm. MAY be a Realm-scoped pairwise DID.

subject_id.description: Principal DID or disclosed holder DID represented by actor_id for display purposes. Authorization and audit continue to use the Event actor and member state.

payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of this MemberIdentity object with the top-level proof field excluded. The signature MUST cover the same canonical bytes.

schemas/message.schema.json.title: Cokret Message

anyOf.$comment: forbidden encrypted content carrier; canonical name is encrypted_content
forbidden track key; canonical name is track_name
forbidden Message extension metadata; canonical path is metadata.fields or encrypted_metadata

track_name.description: Strand track key for this Message. v1 Message objects are restricted to the Strand discussion track. Profiles that need another timeline kind MUST register a separate object/event profile instead of overloading Message.track_name.

effective_scope.description: Reducer-stamped immutable effective scope of this Message, materialized from the scope_circle_id effective at create time (models/circle.md §6.1-§6.2). kind='realm' for Realm-default scope; kind='circle' when the message's Strand was Circle-scoped at write time. Immutable: a later Strand scope rebind MUST NOT reinterpret already-written messages — each message retains its write-time effective_scope and old-scope history/key eligibility. MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied submit payload (reducer-managed, reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed); the reducer stamps it on accept.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is the Message ContentBlock.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a message_metadata object.

state.description: Top-level lifecycle state for messages. Messages do not have a separate deleted/tombstone state; retention or moderation removal uses ck.message.redact and state=redacted so the message slot and audit metadata remain stable.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ck.message.redact Event. Aligns with the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

revision_root.description: First revision in this message's edit chain. The first revision MUST have revision_root == id. Maintained by ck.message.revise reducer.

redaction_ref.description: Required when state=redacted; references the ck.message.redact event that produced this state. MUST be absent for other states.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent materialized message update, such as ck.message.revise or ck.message.redact.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug used by @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>. Not a global handle or authorization subject.

subject_id.description: Authoritative mention target principal DID. For native personal agent selectors this is the agent principal DID, not the controller DID.

controller_subject_id.description: Audit metadata for @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> inputs. MUST NOT replace subject_id for routing, authorization, or attribution.

not.$comment: Mirror of event-payload.schema.json $defs.content_block: reject discriminator field `type` (canonical: `kind`), composite child array name `blocks` (canonical: `parts`), and byte-count field `size` (canonical: `size_bytes`). Keeps materialized Message and Event payload schemas in lockstep so that the materialized Message.content cannot smuggle through wire-forbidden field names.

message_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Message metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

metadata_fields.description: Profile-defined Message metadata fields. Reducer-owned lifecycle and revision fields are forbidden here to avoid dual sources of truth.

schemas/message.schema.json.$comment: Top-level uses unevaluatedProperties (not additionalProperties) because the top-level oneOf branches contribute evaluated properties; additionalProperties at the top level would not see those and could wrongly reject legitimate oneOf-branch fields (JSON Schema additionalProperties/oneOf pitfall).

schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.title: Cokret MIMI Interoperability
schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.description: Provider directory, room binding, and content mapping receipt objects for ck.profile.mimi_interop.v1.
schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.$comment: Intentionally relaxed interop-extension surface: this profile tracks evolving IETF MIMI Internet-Drafts (see zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §1), so additionalProperties is left open at the top level and on the mimi/binding_scope/payload subtrees to forward-carry draft fields without a breaking schema bump. Known fields are pinned; unknown draft fields are tolerated rather than rejected. The proof object below gives a minimal required core so the openness is limited to known extension subtrees and does not mask a missing signature.
