Unknown fields anywhere on this surface are security-inert (see zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §9.2): receivers MUST ignore them for all security decisions and MUST NOT let them affect authorization, identity binding, policy_root, MLS epoch/group state, routing, or any signature/digest transcript.

room_binding.description: MIMI room binding effect payload. In CBA/Lattice state, the cell subject is payload.mimi_room_uri for ck.component.mimi.room_binding.v1.

status.description: Room binding lifecycle status. Initial status MUST be proposed or accepted; legal transitions are proposed->accepted, proposed->revoked, accepted->migrating, accepted->revoked, migrating->accepted (verified migration proof), migrating->revoked. revoked is the only terminal state; illegal transitions are rejected with mimi_room_binding_status_transition_invalid. Normative state machine: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2.

migration_outcome.description: Outcome of a migrating->accepted transition: completed (new topology in effect) or rolled_back (original topology restored). MUST be present on a migrating->accepted Control Move so the result is auditable; MUST be absent on other transitions. Normative: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2.

schemas/mimi-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret MIMI Operation DTOs
schemas/mimi-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for MIMI provider interop operation bindings.

schemas/moderation-appeal.schema.json.title: Cokret Moderation Appeal
schemas/moderation-appeal.schema.json.description: Payload shapes for the four ck.moderation.appeal.* event kinds (submit / review / decision / close) that close the moderation appeal loop. Each kind writes the ck.component.moderation.appeal.v1 cell on a deterministic state machine: (none) → submitted → under_review → decided → closed; close from submitted/under_review is allowed only for appellant withdrawal (closer == appellant and close_reason=appellant_withdrawn). The decided state additionally records the verdict (uphold / overturn / modify); overturn MUST be paired in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction with a ck.moderation.decision.lift event referencing the original decision. All payloads carry realm_id and reducers MUST require it to equal the enclosing Event.realm_id and the appealed decision's Realm. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal strand). Capability: ck.moderation.appeal.submit (any member, low risk) for submit; ck.moderation.appeal.review (moderator) for review/decision/manual reviewer close after decided; appellant withdrawal is authorized by closer == appellant.

decision_ref.description: Reference to the ck.moderation.decision event being appealed.

target_ref.description: The original moderation target (message, strand, member, blob, etc.) — same typed-id form as the appealed decision's target.

evidence_visibility.description: Who may decrypt / read the appeal evidence narrative. Default per Realm policy; SHOULD be reviewers_only for sensitive disputes. The visibility tag MUST enter projection / redaction decisions; it does NOT change wire encryption of the envelope, only the plaintext audience for evidence fields.

submit_payload.description: ck.moderation.appeal.submit — opens the appeal. Writes appeal cell (state=submitted). MUST be issued by an appellant who is the original moderation target's controller (member appealing their own ban / message removal) or by an authorized advocate listed in Realm policy. A Realm member appellant is admitted by baseline membership; a non-member advocate MUST be authorized by Realm policy / ck.moderation.appeal.submit capability.

appellant.description: Actor lodging the appeal. MUST be the original moderation target's controller or an authorized advocate.

reason_text_ref.description: Reference (typically blob_ref or in-line short string) to the appeal narrative / supporting argument. For E2EE Realms this is an encrypted reference.

evidence_refs.description: Optional supporting evidence (blob refs, prior message ids, witness DIDs).

review_payload.description: ck.moderation.appeal.review — reviewer takes the appeal under review. Transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Reviewer MUST hold ck.moderation.appeal.review capability; the same actor MUST NOT review their own moderation decision (separation of duties enforced by reducer).

decision_payload.description: ck.moderation.appeal.decision — reviewer's verdict. Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Verdict semantics: uphold = original decision stands, no further action; overturn = original decision reversed, this event MUST be paired in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction with a ck.moderation.decision.lift event whose target equals decision_ref (reducer rejects with appeal_overturn_missing_lift otherwise); modify = original decision adjusted (parameters revised), modify_decision_ref MUST point to a new ck.moderation.decision event in the same batch that supersedes the original.

reason_text_ref.description: Reference to the verdict rationale. MUST be present for audit trail; visibility follows evidence_visibility on the submit event.

modify_decision_ref.description: Required iff verdict=modify. Points to the replacement ck.moderation.decision event in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction.

close_payload.description: ck.moderation.appeal.close — closes the appeal from decided, or from submitted/under_review only for appellant withdrawal. Reviewer close and a deployment's authorized close service use the review capability after the appeal is decided; appellant withdrawal is authorized by closer == appellant plus close_reason=appellant_withdrawn while state is submitted or under_review. close is a manual/authorized action: the protocol does not mandate any auto-close timer, timeout duration, or cool-off duration — deployment/Realm policy decides those. Idempotency only: the same (decision_ref, appellant) pair MUST NOT have two non-closed appeals concurrently; a fresh appeal_id is allowed once the prior appeal cell is closed.

closer.description: Actor or service closing the appeal (reviewer, appellant, or a deployment's authorized close service). Reducer authorizes the close via the normal capability gate (or closer == appellant for withdrawal); the protocol does not mandate any timer service DID or timeout window.

auto_closed.description: Informational marker: true iff the close was emitted by a deployment's automated close service rather than a human actor. The protocol attaches no special timer/window enforcement to this flag; deployment policy defines when (if ever) automated close fires.

close_reason.description: Machine-readable close cause. appellant_withdrawn is valid only when closer is the appellant and the appeal is still submitted or under_review; timer_expired is an optional label for a deployment's automated close (auto_closed=true) and carries no protocol-mandated timeout semantics.

status.description: Authoritative moderation queue-item lifecycle. v1 is intentionally minimal: 'submitted' = report accepted and awaiting handling; 'resolved' = handling complete (terminal). The disposition (action taken vs no violation) lives on the separate ck.moderation.decision event; the appeal loop lives in the independent ck.moderation.appeal.* subsystem (§5.5). Additional intermediate states MAY be introduced in a later revision if a workflow phase needs them. See governance/content-moderation.md §3.3.

effective_scope.description: Governance boundary for this report. When absent, the report is Realm-default. Circle-scoped targets MUST resolve to the target Circle and route only to scoped moderators/admins.

franking_proof.description: Optional franking proof metadata block. Mirrors the franking_proof object spec'd in zh/governance/content-moderation.md §3.4. It proves service receipt of ciphertext metadata; it does not prove plaintext authorship and does not grant moderators any MLS epoch/exporter secret.

status.description: Non-authoritative status mirror for client / UI convenience. The authoritative moderation lifecycle (submitted → resolved) lives on the moderation-queue-item produced by the reducer (see schemas/moderation-queue-item.schema.json + governance/content-moderation.md §3.3). Reducers MUST NOT read this field for routing or state-machine decisions; if present on submit it MUST be either absent or 'submitted'.

routing_metadata_digest.description: Digest of canonical event routing metadata covered by the receiving service.

mls_group_id_digest.description: Digest of the MLS group id; raw group ids MUST NOT appear in franking proofs.

replay_nonce.description: Opaque anti-replay nonce generated by the receiving service and covered by the franking proof signature.

signature.description: Receiving service signature over the canonical franking proof transcript.

schemas/morph-customer-risk-ext.schema.j.title: Cokret Morph Customer Risk Extension Example
schemas/morph-customer-risk-ext.schema.j.description: Reference additive extension business-field schema for the morph.md customer_risk example, used by the ck.morph.schema_migrate transformation conformance vectors. It declares the optional fields a transformation migration may introduce (renamed score / backfilled priority) on top of ck.schema.morph.customer_risk.v1.
schemas/morph-customer-risk-ext.schema.j.$comment: Logical schema id is ck.schema.morph.customer_risk.ext.v1 (dotted, used in schema_refs[]); the artifact file name uses hyphens (morph-customer-risk-ext.schema.json). Do not derive the id from the file name. This is a v1 additive extension profile, not a version bump of customer_risk.v1.

schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.title: Cokret Morph Customer Risk Example
schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.description: Reference business-field schema for the morph.md customer_risk example. It constrains the fields object carried by a ck.schema.morph.v1 container.
schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.$comment: Logical schema id is ck.schema.morph.customer_risk.v1 (dotted, used in schema_refs[]); the artifact file name uses hyphens (morph-customer-risk.schema.json). Do not derive the id from the file name.

anyOf.$comment: forbidden Morph top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.title or encrypted_metadata
forbidden Morph top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.summary or encrypted_metadata
forbidden encrypted content carrier; canonical name is encrypted_content

scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle that defines this Morph's effective scope. Omitted means Realm-default scope. Reducer enforces scope_circle_id.realm_id == Morph.realm_id and stamps immutable effective_scope onto emitted events.

schema_refs.description: Authoritative schema set for Morph fields and transition validation. Reducers MUST validate fields against exactly these refs; morph_type and facets are not a replacement for schema_refs.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a morph_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata when the effective metadata_encryption_floor is e2ee_required.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a ContentBlock for Morph content.

state.description: Morph lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: ck.morph.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=morph_not_active); ck.morph.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else morph_not_archived); ck.redaction targeting the morph MUST come from {'active','archived'} (else morph_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ck.morph.archive / ck.morph.restore / redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

stage.description: Morph business-progression stage. Orthogonal to top-level 'state' (physical lifecycle). Required on ck.morph.create (no protocol-level default). The only wire path that mutates stage is the dedicated ck.morph.stage.set event; ck.morph.update / ck.morph.schema_migrate patches on stage / stage_changed_at MUST be rejected (schema_violation, single-source). Stage transitions intentionally do NOT carry a reason / note field — the ck.morph.stage.set event log is the audit source; human-readable explanations belong in a Message on an associated discussion track that references the event. See models/common-fields.md §5.3 for full semantics.

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition. MUST be ignored when present on wire; reducer overwrites with the triggering ck.morph.stage.set event's created_at. Same-value self-transitions MUST NOT update this field.

morph_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Morph metadata. Morph business fields stay in the top-level fields object; metadata carries display-oriented fields such as title and summary. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields and Morph business fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

Reject discriminator field `type`, composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`; canonical content blocks use `kind`, composite children use `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes`.
Strand track keys use track_name on current wire.

source_ref.description: Optional canonical-object reference for clients that want to render the notification target without resolving source_event_id. Reducers MUST treat source_event_id as authoritative; source_ref is a render-only hint.

strand_id.description: Optional Strand context for routing the notification.

track_name.description: Optional Strand track key on the source Strand.

preview.description: Render summary. Under E2EE / redaction / history-limited scopes this MUST be empty or an authorized redacted digest; sender/reducer-enforced. A notification projection MUST NOT widen the plaintext visibility of the source Message. See models/private-objects.md §3.4.

schemas/patch.schema.json.title: Cokret Field Patch (ck.schema.patch.v1)
schemas/patch.schema.json.description: Canonical field-patch format embedded in event payloads (typically at payload.patch) for non-create updates. This is a registered schema id (ck.schema.patch.v1) describing the structural form of a patch map; the embedded format identifier 'ck.patch.v1' remains the in-prose name for the same wire shape. Implementations MUST resolve ck.patch.v1 references in spec prose to this schema artifact. Grammar, parser responsibilities, selector semantics, redactable-field protection and reducer-managed-field protection are defined normatively in zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.

propertyNames.$comment: Patch path syntax. Snake_case identifier, optional dot-separated segments, optional stable-key selectors (`field[<key>=<canonical-json-string>]`) and backtick-quoted literals for non-snake_case keys. Full ABNF in zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.2.1. Maximum length 1024 bytes, maximum nesting depth 16 segments — exceeding either MUST yield reason_code patch_path_invalid.

oneOf.$comment: Direct value form: equivalent to {"$op":"set","value":<value>}. Any JSON value EXCEPT a JSON object containing a $op discriminator may use this form.
Explicit op object form. $op is required; value is required for set/add/remove; value MUST be absent for unset.

schemas/peer-contact-delivery-request.sc.title: Cokret Peer Contact Delivery Request
schemas/peer-contact-delivery-request.sc.description: Private service-to-service request used by an issuer-side Principal Server to deliver a signed contact fact (ck.contact.requested / ck.contact.accepted / ck.contact.rejected / ck.contact.tombstoned) to the target holder's Principal Server. The recipient projects the original signed envelope into the target holder's contact projection (pending_incoming / accepted / rejected / tombstoned); it MUST NOT re-sign the fact as its own. Contact facts are principal-scoped and cross-Realm, so this carrier is the federation delivery path for the contact fact log, separate from invite delivery.

contact_event.description: The issuer-signed contact fact EventEnvelope being delivered with its original signature, so the recipient can verify and project it without re-signing.

fact_kind.description: The contact fact kind carried by contact_event. MUST equal contact_event.kind.

introduction_evidence.description: Required when fact_kind is ck.contact.requested. Explains why the requester may attempt first contact; the recipient applies its subject-private receive policy and deployment constraints before notifying the holder.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the contact fact recipient (the request target, or the original requester for an accept/reject travelling back). The recipient Principal Server projects the fact into this holder's contact projection.

recipient_service_did.description: Principal Server service DID that hosts subject_id and accepts contact delivery for it.

recipient_service_type.description: v1 only allows Principal Server contact delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.

consent_grant_ref.description: Event ref of a target-issued ck.consent.grant whose scope covers the requested contact action, or any.

handle.description: Canonical handle string the requester used as the human-readable entry point.

handle_claim.description: Verified handle claim proving that handle resolves to contact_address.subject_id. The receiver MUST verify binding_state, proofs, expiry, issuer trust, visibility/audience policy, and that handle_claim.handle equals handle.

resolved_by.description: Optional Directory or issuer service DID that supplied the handle resolution.

status.description: Generic receive status. It MUST NOT reveal whether subject_id exists or whether the holder's receive policy suppressed the fact, beyond the optional disclosed_outcome graded disclosure that mirrors ck.peer.invites.command.submit.

disclosed_outcome.description: Optional graded-disclosure result, present only when the subject's receive policy disclosure level for this trust tier is 'outcome' and the subject did not block the issuer. Omitted (opaque) otherwise.

schemas/personal-productivity.schema.jso.title: Cokret Personal Productivity Account Data
schemas/personal-productivity.schema.jso.description: Plaintext shapes that MUST be encrypted before writing ck.profile.personal_productivity.v1 account-data values.

policy_rule.description: Closed policy rule. Extension rules must carry an explicit schema_ref/profile_ref instead of adding undeclared fields to the signed policy body.

domain_name.description: Lowercase DNS A-label domain. Matching semantics are label-boundary based and defined by governance/content-moderation.md.

server_selector.description: Selector for federation server policy rules. Domain rules match normalized DNS labels only; service_did exact rules take precedence in policy evaluation.

schemas/principal-locator.schema.json.title: Cokret Principal Locator
schemas/principal-locator.schema.json.description: Signed online locator returned from a holder-controlled Principal Server locator ref. It asserts the invite address used for private invite delivery; it is not a Realm membership grant and not a member_delivery_binding.

subject_id.description: Principal DID of the invite recipient. v1 core defaults principal DIDs to did:webvh; did:web is only valid for principal identity when an explicit deployment profile or resolver policy allows it.

recipient_service_did.description: Principal Server service DID that accepts invite delivery for subject_id.

recipient_service_type.description: v1 only allows Principal Server invite delivery. Omit by default; if present, the value MUST be principal_server.

expires_at.description: Time after which the locator MUST NOT be used to initiate invite delivery.

locator_ref_digest.description: Digest of the private locator ref material. The raw locator token MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

delivery_modes.description: Invite-delivery capability hints only; join-time member_delivery_binding is still materialized by Realm policy.

display_hint.description: UI-only display hint. It is not identity authority and MUST NOT be used for authorization.

proofs.description: At minimum contains recipient_service_acceptance. High-assurance deployments SHOULD also require subject_locator_authorization.

proof.description: Detached proof over canonical_json(principal_locator_without_proofs). proof.payload_digest MUST equal that canonical payload digest.

locator_token.description: Opaque base64url locator token with at least 128 bits of entropy. It SHOULD be a server-side handle and MUST NOT plaintext-encode subject_id, recipient_service_did, expiry, policy state, or other invitee-identifying material. It MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string.

schemas/push-operations.schema.json.title: Cokret Push Gateway Operation DTOs
schemas/push-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for ck.edge.push.command.register_device, ck.edge.push.command.unregister_device, and ck.push.notify.

push_target_id.description: Pairwise pseudonym for one (recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route) tuple. It MUST NOT be a DID, DID URL, Realm id, Strand id, Message id, Event id, or stable cross-Realm correlation key.

push_route_token.description: Opaque service-generated routing token. It MUST NOT contain, encode, or be reversibly derived from a DID, DID URL, Realm id, Circle id, Strand id, Message id, Event id, handle, platform push token, or stable cross-context correlation key.

registration_id.description: Push gateway local registration id. It is not a registered ck:<kind> protocol object id.

badge.description: Coarse unread indicator. Under blind_wakeup it MUST NOT carry a plaintext absolute unread count (activity side channel); only a boolean presence flag or a policy-declared bucket string is allowed. See push-notifications.md §5.1.

target_route_token.description: Gateway-internal mention-redirect routing token for this device route. Paired with notification.route_tokens.mention_redirect_target_route_tokens to drive the fail-closed per-device routing gate. MUST be stripped before any provider call; MUST NOT be forwarded to a provider. See push-notifications.md §4.5 / §5.1.

visible_notification_opt_in.description: Receiver device authorization state for ck.profile.push_gateway.visible_notification.v1. Missing or false means this device MUST receive only blind_wakeup output even if the caller service is plaintext-visible; visible metadata requires an explicit per-device opt-in.

route_tokens.description: Gateway-internal opaque routing fragment shared by blind and visible notifications. Every field here drives gateway-side routing / dedup / circuit-breaker state and MUST be stripped before the gateway calls any push provider; it MUST NOT be forwarded to a provider. Tokens are issued by the recipient Sync or Principal Service and bound to recipient_service_did, push gateway service DID, purpose, scope, and salt epoch.

realm_route_token.description: Opaque token for Realm-level routing / dedup / circuit-breaker keying.

scope_route_token.description: Opaque token for the effective Realm or Circle scope of this wakeup.

mention_redirect_target_route_tokens.description: Mention-redirect routing allow-list. When non-empty, each device's device_route.target_route_token MUST appear here or that device is failed closed (no provider call, no body decryption). Gateway-internal; MUST be stripped before any provider call. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

delivery_binding_frontier_token.description: Opaque token representing the receiver's delivery-binding frontier for stale-route detection.

audit_envelope.description: `ck.audit.accessed` envelope routing fragment carried alongside a notify request. When present, the request is an audit-pipeline event (e.g. an `e2ee_late_recovery` access notice), not a push notify: the gateway writes the audit event, acks 200, and skips the push pipeline.

access_kind.description: ck.audit.accessed.access_kind. The gateway branches on `e2ee_late_recovery` to skip the push pipeline.

late_recovery_original_event_id.description: REQUIRED (at the application layer) when access_kind == e2ee_late_recovery. References the original event the late recovery targets.

push_hint.description: Sanitized hint sentinel. When the value is "l10n_key" the actual localization key MUST be carried in push_hint_l10n_key (this enum value is a form selector, not a literal display token). See push-notifications.md §5.1 / §4.5.

push_hint_l10n_key.description: Localization key value, only present (and required) when push_hint == "l10n_key". MUST be an l10n key token, never plaintext body or any identifying metadata.

evaluation_locus_unresolved.description: Set true when the client has been woken but server-side rule matching is not yet resolved (E2EE client-side rule fallback). Pure local-evaluation signal; carries no metadata. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

push_hint.description: Sanitized hint sentinel. When the value is "l10n_key" the actual localization key MUST be carried in push_hint_l10n_key (this enum value is a form selector, not a literal display token). See push-notifications.md §5.1 / §4.5.

push_hint_l10n_key.description: Localization key value, only present (and required) when push_hint == "l10n_key".

evaluation_locus_unresolved.description: Set true when the client has been woken but server-side rule matching is not yet resolved. See push-notifications.md §4.5.

push_notify_request_body.description: Closed Cokret notify body. Product-private notification bodies, provider adapter payloads, APNs/FCM/WebPush data dictionaries, `content`, `content_*`, `provider_payload`, DND/snooze state, and push-rule plaintext are outside this wire surface and MUST be consumed before this body is built. Provider-facing payloads are reconstructed by the gateway from this closed shape and MUST strip route_tokens / reason_code / event_kind / audit_envelope before provider dispatch.

event_kind.description: Originating Event kind (e.g. `ck.message`) used by the gateway to route Phase-P2 `ck.agent.*` lifecycle / actor-private kinds to a no-fanout ack. Coarse routing selector; carries no Realm / sender / event identifier.

reason_code.description: Caller-supplied wire-safe reason code. The well-known value `historical_only` marks a diagnostic replay that MUST NOT trigger a fresh push fanout (the gateway answers a 200 idempotency-style ack). Other values are honored only where the operation defines them.

schemas/query.schema.json.title: Cokret Query / Search Request Shapes
schemas/query.schema.json.description: Canonical wire schema for client query / projection and search request bodies and their reusable building blocks (filters, sort, relation query). The OpenAPI document references these $defs so there is a single source of truth. Human-readable semantics: zh/conformance/query-schema.md. facet_name / view_renderer are copies of the shared OpenAPI enums (kept local so this file is self-contained); the authoritative facet / renderer enums also live in the OpenAPI components and MUST stay in lockstep.

key_view_ref.description: Optional root/proof reference for the data-plane KeyView used by this projection.

context_ref.description: Optional timeline / renderer context object reference. This is not a Seal.

schemas/range-completeness-attestation.s.title: Cokret Range-bound Completeness Attestation
schemas/range-completeness-attestation.s.description: A range-bound completeness attestation. Event kind: ck.attestation.range_completeness (active in event-kind-registry; the event kind itself carries NO .v1 suffix). Payload schema id: ck.schema.range_completeness_attestation.v1 (schemas keep the .v1 versioning). The attestation asserts that the issuer (and any witnesses) have observed every reducer-input event in a declared range — (from_frontier, to_frontier) bounded by explicit per-actor seq intervals — where each frontier is a Realm-scoped frontier (property name realm_frontier; the security/replication boundary for completeness in v1 is the Realm, not an in-Realm Space container). Distinct from ck.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity over an arbitrary chosen subset) and ck.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event RYW hint). Used when verifiers need a completeness claim — i.e., 'no event has been silently withheld from this range' — not just 'the events given are unmodified'. Standalone single-issuer attestations are NOT sufficient for sovereign / multi-writer trust models; deployments requiring strong completeness MUST use a witness_attestation block following the ck.audit.ryw_receipt model (zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1.1).

schema.description: Payload schema id (versioned). The owning Event kind in event-kind-registry.json is ck.attestation.range_completeness (NO .v1 suffix on the event kind).

from_frontier.description: Lower bound of the range (exclusive). The attestation covers events causally after this frontier.

from_seq_exclusive.description: Per-actor seq lower bound (exclusive). -1 means 'from actor genesis'.

to_seq_inclusive.description: Per-actor seq upper bound (inclusive). Issuer asserts completeness of every actor_seq in the half-open interval (from_seq_exclusive, to_seq_inclusive].

actor_seq_ranges.description: Per-actor seq intervals attested. Silent forks frequently appear as a missing slice in a single actor's seq sequence while the global frontier still advances monotonically — explicit per-actor ranges close that gap. MUST cover every actor that produced reducer-input events in (from_frontier, to_frontier].

root.description: Canonical Merkle root over the sorted set of (actor_id, actor_seq, event_id, event_digest) tuples for every reducer-input event in scope. Digest algorithm agility per Realm.digest_algorithm.

count.description: Number of reducer-input events in scope. MUST match the number of leaves used to compute root.

observed_at.description: When the issuer finished observing the scope and computed the attestation.

kind.description: Same semantics as ck.audit.ryw_receipt.witness_attestation: 'federation_witness_attested' requires witnesses[].length >= 2 with pairwise-distinct issuer/controlling_organization/verification_method, each listed by Realm policy in audit.range_completeness_witnesses[]. 'single_source' is the honest declaration for self-attested deployments. Mismatch between kind and witnesses[] cardinality / distinctness / policy listing MUST be rejected. Receivers SHOULD treat single_source attestations as advisory only and not as a sovereign-grade completeness proof.

schemas/read-cursor-operations.schema.js.title: Cokret Read Cursor Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/read-cursor-operations.schema.js.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface read cursor operations (ck.self.read_cursor.*). set builds a ck.read_cursor.advance actor-private write; the durable cursor object model and read_scope / position field shapes are read-cursor.schema.json. See spec/v1/zh/discovery/read-receipts.md.

kind.description: Read-scope object kind per zh/models/private-objects.md §2.2. Track-scoped read cursors use kind='strand' plus track_name. Thread cursors use kind='thread' with ref = the thread root message id (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §5); thread is a projection selector over the reply sub-timeline, not a first-class protocol object. Shares the read-scope discriminator family with read-receipt.schema.json; each schema declares its own supported subset.

ref.description: Required when kind is circle, space, strand, or thread; omitted for kind='realm'. Thread read scopes reference the root message.

track_name.description: Required when kind='strand' AND the cursor scopes a single track (e.g. 'discussion', 'synthesis', or any profile-registered track name). Track names MUST match the Strand's registered tracks; unknown tracks MUST be rejected with schema_violation.

schemas/read-cursor.schema.json.title: Cokret Read Cursor
schemas/read-cursor.schema.json.description: Actor-private multi-device read cursor. Stored in encrypted account data or actor-private stream; NEVER published into a shared Realm Event history. Bound to (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope, position, HLC, device_id) per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §6.6 so that concurrent updates from multiple devices converge by HLC max.

device_id.description: Originating device. Required for multi-device convergence: when two devices race on the same (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope) the receiver picks the entry with greater HLC; device_id provides a deterministic actor_id-scoped tiebreaker when HLCs are equal.

kind.description: Read-scope object kind per zh/models/private-objects.md §2.2. Track-scoped read cursors use kind='strand' plus track_name. Thread cursors use kind='thread' with ref = the thread root message id (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §5); thread is a projection selector over the reply sub-timeline, not a first-class protocol object. Shares the read-scope discriminator family with read-receipt.schema.json; each schema declares its own supported subset.

ref.description: Required when kind is circle, space, strand, or thread; omitted for kind='realm'. Thread read scopes reference the root message.

track_name.description: Required when kind='strand' AND the cursor scopes a single track (e.g. 'discussion', 'synthesis', or any profile-registered track name). Track names MUST match the Strand's registered tracks; unknown tracks MUST be rejected with schema_violation.

schemas/read-receipt.schema.json.title: Cokret Read Receipt
schemas/read-receipt.schema.json.description: Public/shared read receipt for Strand timeline UI hint. NOT canonical truth, NOT a multi-device cursor (see read-cursor.schema.json for that). MUST NOT generate push notifications. Privacy is governed by Realm policy: Realms MAY allow public, members-only, or actor-private receipt sharing.

event_id.description: ID of the most recent Event the actor has read. Causality implies all causal predecessors are also read.

hlc.description: Optional. HLC of the read position; required when Sync Service must compare receipts under merge / debounce rules across devices for the same actor.

kind.description: Read-scope discriminator from the same family as read-cursor.schema.json; each schema declares its own supported subset (receipt additionally supports view/message/morph; cursor additionally supports circle/space). kind='thread' selects the reply sub-timeline rooted at a message (zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §5); thread is a projection selector, not a first-class protocol object.

ref.description: Required when kind is anything other than 'realm'. Thread read scopes reference the root message.

track_name.description: Required when kind='strand' and the receipt scopes a single track.

track_scope.description: Only valid when kind='strand'. Use track_scope='all' for an entire Strand regardless of track.

schemas/realm-join-candidate.schema.json.title: Cokret Realm Join Candidate
schemas/realm-join-candidate.schema.json.description: Time-bounded routing hint for submitting Realm join, invite-accept, knock, or restricted-join material through a qualified Realm service. This object is not membership authorization and is distinct from member_delivery_binding.

realm_id.description: Realm this candidate is bound to. Verifiers MUST reject a candidate used for any other Realm.

service_did.description: Service DID that can receive or relay join-side submissions for this Realm.

service_type.description: Service class. principal_server is the normal candidate; sync_node and notary are allowed only when Realm policy authorizes them to receive join-side submissions.

role.description: Routing role within the Realm candidate set. This is a hint for ordering and diagnostics, not an authorization grant.

endpoint.description: Optional endpoint hint. Callers MUST re-resolve the service DID document before transport and MUST NOT treat this field as authority.

operations.description: Endpoint-callable operation ids available at this candidate. Join-side routing requires ck.events.submit.

join_methods.description: Join-side strands this candidate claims to support for this requester and Realm.

priority.description: Lower values are preferred. Ties are broken deterministically by service_did.

source.description: Where this routing hint came from. Receivers still validate against current Realm policy and service DID documents.

source_refs.description: Realm or directory source events that justify this candidate, such as discovery, service-binding, or sync endpoint state.

frontier_ref.description: Optional digest of the candidate service's advertised Realm frontier at as_of; used only to detect stale hints.

seal_basis.description: Full single-leaf Control Move basis for the candidate service's current accepted Realm Seal at as_of. Principal-server candidates MUST include this so pre-join Realm join / invite-accept Control Moves can be signed without a separate membership-gated frontier read. This is a routing/anchoring hint, not membership authorization: the receiving service still validates the submitted basis and invite.

as_of.description: Time when the issuer observed or refreshed this candidate.

expires_at.description: Time after which clients MUST NOT use this candidate without re-resolving the Realm.

proofs.description: Optional proof set binding realm_id, service_did, role, operations, join_methods, as_of, and expires_at. Required when the candidate is carried outside a freshly resolved Directory response.

schemas/realm-link-operations.schema.jso.title: Cokret Realm Link Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-link-operations.schema.jso.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface cross-Realm link operations (ck.self.realm_link.*). Each write builds a ck.realm.link Move and routes it through the local accept pipeline so the reducer's realm_link_* validators (cycle detection, self-reference, kind validation) run. The durable link payload is the canonical ck.realm.link; see spec/v1/zh/models/realm-links.md.

commitment.description: Optional opaque commitment / proof reference linking this edge to an external attestation.

realm_effective_policy_outcome.description: Merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ck.realm.inheritance_policy declaration.

inheritance_mode.description: explicit when the Realm has projected a ck.realm.inheritance_policy; none otherwise (implicit inheritance is forbidden).

schemas/realm-organization-operations.sc.title: Cokret Realm Organization-Relationship Read Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-organization-operations.sc.description: Closed response DTO for the self-surface Realm organization-relationship read operation (ck.self.realm_organization.query.list). Returns the projected ck.realm.organization statements (active / revoked / expired) for a Realm plus the declared owning_organizations hints that have no verified statement. The verified rows mirror the canonical realm_organization_payload field order; lifecycle_phase is reducer-derived. A row here is a projection only: an organization relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active, and actual Realm control still requires the corresponding Realm policy / notary / capability / service-binding event. See spec/v1/zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.3.0 and schemas/event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/realm_organization_payload.

lifecycle_phase.description: Reducer-derived lifecycle phase of the projected statement. verified_active = latest accepted statement for (organization_id, relationship) is status=active and within its validity window. revoked_or_expired = the relationship has been revoked or is outside its not_before/expires_at window. Declared-only organization hints with no statement are carried in declared_organization_hints, not as rows.

delegation_ref.description: Resolved authorization.delegation_ref for delegated issuer roles (governance_service / account_authority).

relationships.description: Projected ck.realm.organization statement rows (verified_active and revoked_or_expired), latest-per-(organization_id, relationship).

declared_organization_hints.description: owning_organizations declared hints (realm-and-space.md §2.3.0) that have NO verified ck.realm.organization statement. These are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.

schemas/realm-policy-server-operations.s.title: Cokret Realm Policy-Server Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-policy-server-operations.s.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Realm policy-server config operations (ck.self.realm_policy_server.*). The PUT builds a ck.realm.policy_server Move (admission capability ck.policy.manage). This admin DTO is a simplified projection of the canonical ck.realm.policy_server payload (server_id/endpoint/public_keys/applies_to/fail_mode); see spec/v1/zh/authz/policy-server.md §2.

from_org_fallback.description: True when the config was resolved via the governed_by / org-fallback chain rather than a row on the Realm itself.

schemas/realm-read-operations.schema.jso.title: Cokret Realm Read + Moderation-Policy Operation DTOs
schemas/realm-read-operations.schema.jso.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Realm read operations and moderation-policy management (ck.self.realm.*). Realm read returns the lifecycle projection; export returns a full event-log + operation dump; effective moderation-policy returns the organization-inherited merged view; the moderation-policy override write builds a ck.realm.moderation_policy fact (subject to organization approval). See spec/v1/zh/models/realm-and-space.md and spec/v1/zh/governance/content-moderation.md.

operations.description: Operation dump rows {operation_id, realm_id, object_type, operation_type, payload, created_at}.

events.description: Event-log dump rows {event_id, realm_id, event_kind, operation_type, operation_id, sender, payload, created_at}.

realm_effective_moderation_policy.$comment: Open extension surface: the merged moderation-policy view carries deployment-defined organization/realm policy layers and fanout metadata; additionalProperties intentionally true so servers may surface implementation-specific layer detail without a wire-breaking change.

inheritance_chain.description: Organization DIDs (or deployment-local organization identifiers) contributing policy layers, parent-first.

realm_moderation_policy_replace_request_.$comment: Open extension surface: the ck.realm.moderation_policy document body is a free-form governance object (rules[], targets[], allow_override[], organization_approval[]); additionalProperties intentionally true so the override schema can evolve without a wire-breaking change. The document is canonical-JSON validated server-side.
realm_moderation_policy_replace_request_.description: Realm moderation-policy override body. Free-form ck.realm.moderation_policy document. When the override targets actions an organization policy denies, it requires explicit organization approval embedded in the document.

not.$comment: forbidden Realm authorship field; canonical name is created_by

security_class.description: Optional security class. 'high_assurance' forbids federation_policy=open and SHOULD use stricter resolver/E2EE/audit defaults. Omitted = 'standard'.

trust_domain.description: Immutable deployment trust domain captured by ck.realm.create. Receivers MUST require this to match the current Realm trust domain before accepting cross-domain replay-sensitive proofs.

owning_organizations.description: Declared or projected organization principals associated with this Realm. Each DID MUST resolve to an Organization principal. This field alone is not a verified ownership/governance endorsement; clients and directories MUST require an active ck.realm.organization statement for verified badges or organization-controlled semantics.

fields.description: Product/profile fields. Security-relevant discriminators such as purpose=principal_control are schema constrained below; other product fields remain extension-defined.

relation_profiles.description: Optional Relation cardinality and conflict profiles declared by this Realm schema/profile.

on_conflict.description: Conflict handling for mutually unreachable Relation candidates. deterministic_winner selects the candidate with the bytewise-greatest canonical event_digest per the single canonical tie-break rule (zh/conformance/encoding.md §4.2); it MUST NOT use HLC, actor id, event_id, local receive order, database id, or service insertion order.

preview_policy_id.description: Optional materialized pointer to the effective preview / peek policy. Canonical writes use ck.realm.preview_policy; absence means directory card / stripped state only, no history stub/snippet preview.

default_strand_id.description: Optional / nullable. AUTHORITATIVE single pointer to the Realm's default discussion Strand (last value projected from ck.realm.set_default_strand; cell ck.component.realm.set_default_strand.v1, cas_register, bottom=reject). A single pointer avoids multi-default dirty state. null / absent means the Realm has no designated default Strand. The reducer rejects a set_default_strand whose strand_id does not resolve to a projected non-tombstoned Strand in this Realm (failed_precondition), so this pointer never dangles. The Strand projection's derived is_default flag is computed as strand_id == this value; clients discover the default Strand deterministically from this field (or the Strand is_default marker) and MUST NOT rely on any Strand-reuses-Realm-UUID implementation detail. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md (default-Strand discovery).

content_scheme.description: Content-envelope encryption scheme for MLS-backed Realms (crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.10). Orthogonal to encryption_profile, which only declares whether an MLS group exists. mls-rfc9420 = MLS PrivateMessage (per-message forward secrecy, NOT shareable to later joiners; only valid with history_visibility=joined/restricted on MLS-backed Realms). mls-exporter-aead-v1 = MLS-Exporter-derived per-epoch history_secret AEAD (history shareable to authorized later joiners via ck.realm_key.share; per-epoch forward secrecy; does not itself force pre-join delivery). MUST be carried in the MLS governance binding policy_root so receivers can determine, per epoch T0, which scheme applies. Absent: mls-rfc9420 for encryption_profile=mls_rfc9420 Realms; not applicable when encryption_profile=none/external.

content_encryption_floor.description: Realm-wide content encryption floor (models/circle.md §7, models/realm-and-space.md §4). This is the Realm's actual content-encryption on/off switch. When e2ee_required, the effective_scope of Strand / Message / Morph / Blob content MUST be MLS-backed (Realm-default MLS or Circle MLS); reducer MUST failed_precondition (reason=content_encryption_floor_violation) on plaintext content. Independent of encryption_profile, which only declares the encryption MECHANISM (whether an MLS group exists), not which Cokret fields enter ciphertext. One-way ratchet: once the effective value has reached e2ee_required, a later policy write lowering it back to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected with content_encryption_floor_downgrade. Defaults to allow_plaintext when absent.

metadata_encryption_floor.description: Realm-wide metadata encryption floor (models/circle.md §7), binary and symmetric with content_encryption_floor. allow_plaintext lets user-readable metadata stay wire-plaintext; e2ee_required forces it into encrypted_metadata. Comparison order allow_plaintext < e2ee_required. Effective floor = max(parent Realm value, Circle metadata floor, Space child_scope_policy floor, object profile requirement); any write below the effective floor MUST failed_precondition (reason=metadata_encryption_floor_violation). MUST NOT be relaxed by Circle, Space, or object profile. One-way ratchet: once the effective value has reached e2ee_required, a later policy write lowering it back to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected with metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade. When absent, reducers default to e2ee_required for mls_rfc9420 or content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required Realms, otherwise allow_plaintext.

agent_participation.description: Realm agent participation ceiling: { native_agent: { reply, accept_third_party_mention, act_on_behalf } } — the maximum native personal agent behavior permitted Realm-wide, written by a holder of ck.realm.admin via ck.realm.policy_components. It is the top of the deployment ⊇ Realm ⊇ Circle ⊇ Strand tighten-only chain (inner ceilings MUST NOT widen it; reducer rejects with agent_participation_ceiling_widen). When absent, inherits the deployment-default ceiling (deny-default under sovereign profiles). native_agent and applet_agent ceilings MUST be declared separately. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md.

durability_policy.description: Realm Recovery Key (RRK) durability policy (models/realm-and-space.md §2.3.1, crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.10.8). Declares who can recover Realm history after all member devices are lost or all members leave. Confidentiality-axis durability, orthogonal to notary / notary.recovery_* (finality axis: who signs Seals). Recovery recipients are offline HPKE public keys, NOT MLS members. Only effective (mode != none) when content_scheme=mls-exporter-aead-v1; declaring mode != none on an mls-rfc9420 Realm MUST failed_precondition (durability_scheme_incompatible). Granularity = organization composition (point a sensitive Realm's owning_organizations at a finer org), not a per-Realm knob; parent-org retention = list the parent org RRK in recovery_recipients (explicit, member-visible). Written via ck.realm.policy_components.

mode.description: none = no organizational recovery path (total member loss = permanent loss). org_recovery_key = single org RRK. threshold = k-of-n recovery recipients.

recovery_recipients.description: Recovery recipients (RRK holders). MUST be non-empty when mode != none. Each verification_method MUST point to a verification method designated by an active CokretRealmHistoryRecoveryKey service entry published by principal_id, domain-separated from the principal's did_recovery key.

threshold.description: k-of-n threshold parameters, required when mode=threshold. k <= n and n MUST equal len(recovery_recipients).

then.$comment: The arithmetic rule 1 <= k <= n == len(recovery_recipients) is reducer/conformance validation because JSON Schema cannot compare threshold.n to array length portably.

sync_endpoints.description: Realm-level service binding list for shared notary / sync / mirror / federation peer surfaces. Directory resolve responses expose a requester-filtered join_candidates projection for join-side ingress; raw sync_endpoints are not a public candidate list. Member-level delivery_binding remains on ck.member.state and MUST NOT be inferred from this list.

notary_profile.description: Create-locked Seal finality profile. single_did and threshold deployments require signed Seal single-chain uniqueness; open_set deployments allow multiple Seal leaves and deterministic joined control views; mixed deployments use a primary notary plus fallback recovery notary.

digest_algorithm.description: Create-locked digest suite (canonicalization x hash tuple) used for DataEvent ids, Control Move ids, Seal ids, state_root, and Merkle leaves within this Realm. Defaults to sha256. Value space is the active rows of artifacts/registry/digest-suite-registry.json (this enum MUST be regenerated when a row flips active, e.g. cbor.sha256); bare ids denote canonical-JSON canonicalization, dotted ids denote alternate canonical encodings. Exactly one live suite per Realm; migration uses a control-plane suite-transition Control Move finalized by Seal, see event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.2.

notary.description: Genesis value for the Realm notary cell. Subsequent changes are Control Moves finalized by the previous notary. For single_did profiles, recovery_members and controller organization evidence are required so reducer/authz can reject single-organization recovery setups.

forensic_attribution.$comment: Required for type=threshold (enforced by allOf below). MUST be quorum_intersection when 2*threshold > members.length (two conflicting quorums then intersect in at least one attributable double-signer; see authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1 and BFT Protocol Forensics). MUST be waived when 2*threshold <= members.length, declaring that automatic culprit attribution is unavailable. JSON Schema cannot compare threshold against members.length, so the arithmetic side is reducer/conformance validation (ck.vector.cba_lattice.threshold_forensic_attribution.v1).
forensic_attribution.description: Equivocation culprit-attribution mode for threshold notary committees: quorum_intersection (2k>n, automatic attribution available) or waived (k<=n/2, deployment explicitly waives automatic attribution and relies on committee-level handling).

controller_organization.description: DID of the organization controlling the primary notary, when the resolver or deployment policy can derive it. Required for single_did profile so recovery diversity can be verified.

recovery_controller_organizations.description: Organization DIDs controlling recovery_members. Reducer MUST verify at least one differs from controller_organization for single_did profile.

revocation_freshness_window_ms.description: Realm-level maximum control-plane seal distance/time window for accepting DataEvents whose seal_ref predates an observed revocation seal. Receivers evaluate this window by seal topology and policy (the notary-committed seal-time delta along the Seal DAG per authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 4.3), not by unverified event signing time. risk_tier=high capabilities get no grace (effective 0). High-risk Realms SHOULD use a short value or move the affected cell family to control plane.

receipt_sla_ms.description: Realm-level deadline within which a pending control-plane Control Move MUST receive a signed receipt or signed rejection (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Measured by notary-committed seal time, not local receive time. Silent omission past this SLA (modulo bounded defers, see max_receipt_defers) is censorship evidence.

max_receipt_defers.description: Maximum cumulative number of signed defers a single pending Control Move may receive before include / signed-reject is mandatory (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Exceeding it without include/signed-reject is treated as silent omission / censorship evidence.

seal_compaction_max_interval_ms.description: Structural obligation, not advisory: maximum interval between compaction Seals (Seals carrying covered_event_digests[] or an equivalent verifiable full-coverage manifest). Because the cumulative control-plane covered set is defined recursively from predecessor_refs + delta, compaction Seals are the only bounded bootstrap points for new verifiers; a notary that exceeds this interval degrades bootstrap to walking the chain to genesis. open_set deployments MUST use <= 86400000 (24h); threshold deployments MUST use <= 604800000 (7d); single_did SHOULD use <= 86400000. Receivers SHOULD raise governance health alarms when the live chain exceeds the declared interval. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 6.2 and conformance vector ck.vector.cba_lattice.seal_compaction_interval_enforced.v1.

max_delegation_lifetime_ms.description: Realm-level maximum lifetime window used when an otherwise unbounded parent grant first delegates. Reducers freeze delegation_expiry_seal = first_delegation_sealed_at + effective max_delegation_lifetime_ms and MUST NOT refresh it on re-delegation. Effective value is the minimum of this field and any stricter grant, policy, deployment, or profile override. Defaults to 86400000 ms (24h). See zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.1.

bottom_escalation_after_ms.description: Optional timeout after which unresolved bottom diagnostics should be escalated to recovery governance. Expiry does not choose a winner automatically.

cell_lattices.description: Optional Realm-specific lattice declarations for extension cell families.

co_write_policy.description: Optional whitelist constraining which cell families may be written by the same Move.

allOf.$comment: single_did notary profiles bind one DID as the primary notary. controller_organization / recovery_controller_organizations / recovery_members are required ONLY when the deployment can derive a controlling organization (see notary.controller_organization 'when ... can derive it'; decisions/0003 §7 — personal / orgless Realms legitimately omit them and fall back to per-user recovery). When a controller_organization IS declared, an explicit recovery-notary diversity path MUST accompany it. The distinct-controller arithmetic stays semantic/reducer validation because JSON Schema cannot compare DID-controller derivations across resolver evidence.
Org-controlled single_did Realms MUST declare the recovery-notary diversity path alongside the controlling organization.

Threshold notary committees must declare their equivocation culprit-attribution mode at Realm create time. The arithmetic rule (quorum_intersection iff 2*threshold > members.length) is reducer/conformance validation; see notary.forensic_attribution $comment.

Principal control Realms are ordinary ck.schema.realm.v1 objects, but the profile discriminator must be closed at schema level: fields.purpose and schema_refs must appear together, the Realm MUST be MLS-backed, and both encryption floors MUST be pinned to e2ee_required (key-management §4.1 / §5.0.1, realm-and-space §2.8.1). There is no plaintext-floor PCR in v1.
The inverse guard prevents a profile-tagged Realm from omitting the machine-readable purpose discriminator, and pins the encryption floors symmetrically with the forward guard.
content_scheme is only meaningful for MLS-backed Realms. Plaintext or external encryption Realms MUST NOT declare an MLS content envelope scheme.

recipient_id.description: Realm-unique stable id for this recovery recipient.

principal_id.description: Principal holding the RRK private key. SHOULD resolve to an Organization Principal for org_recovery_key/threshold; MAY be a personal principal for personal Realms.

verification_method.description: Reference to a verification method in principal_id's DID Document designated by an active CokretRealmHistoryRecoveryKey service entry (identity/identity-did.md §8.3). The RRK HPKE public key; history-recovery domain, separate from did_recovery.

controller_organization.description: Organization DID controlling this recovery recipient, when derivable; receiver MAY use it to verify org attribution.

cell_role.description: Semantic role declared by Realm schema. authorization_root / policy_root / notary_root / membership / lifecycle MUST NOT use lattice types lww_register or rga (enforced by allOf below). ui_affordance / content / draft / cosmetic MAY use lww_register or rga.

plane.description: CBA plane for this cell family. authorization_root / policy_root / notary_root / membership / lifecycle MUST be control. Ordinary content / draft / cosmetic cells SHOULD be data unless sealed=true.

sealed.description: Opt-in control-plane finality for an otherwise data-like cell family. When true, plane MUST be control.

initial_value.description: Optional cell schema initial value (cas_register only). When defined, the cas_register `join` algorithm initialises `current` to this value (rather than null) before applying any Move. Combined with a `head_eq: <initial_value>` predicate on the first set Move, this implements singleton-once-set cells via the empty sentinel pattern. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.1.

sentinel_writers.description: Optional companion to `initial_value` (cas_register only). When `initial_value` is declared, set ops whose effect equals the sentinel are rejected by default (initial_value_reserved). Listing event_kinds here permits those event_kinds to write the sentinel back — typically the cleanup event_kind in a singleton-once-set / explicit-reset workflow. Capability authorization remains a separate independent check. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.1.

allOf.$comment: Security-root roles are always control-plane.
sealed=true is the explicit data-to-control opt-in.
initial_value is only defined for cas_register (see event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.1). Other lattices reject the field.

sentinel_writers is the companion of initial_value; it only makes sense on a cas_register cell that has declared initial_value. Reject declarations on other lattices, and reject declarations on cas_register cells that lack initial_value (since there is no sentinel to authorise writing back).

schemas/recovery-policy.schema.json.title: Cokret Recovery Policy
schemas/recovery-policy.schema.json.description: Normative grammar for a principal's recovery policy. Bound to the Principal Control Realm via signed publish / rotate / revoke control events; receivers MUST reject `recover`, `rotate`, `ck.device.authorize` and Cross-Signing Reset evidence whose proof family / threshold / approval requirement is not allowed by the currently accepted recovery policy. See identity/key-management.md §3.3 / §7 / §8 and crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

version.description: Monotonically increasing counter scoped by principal_id. Receivers MUST reject a publish whose version is not strictly greater than the currently accepted policy.

supersedes.description: Predecessor policy_id. Null only for the genesis policy of a principal.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier the policy applies to. Cross-domain proofs MUST fail.

allowed_proof_kinds.description: Which proof families this policy authorizes for recovery and cross-signing reset. Each entry constrains the matching proof kind defined in device-lifecycle.md §14. Empty array is valid only for an explicit revocation policy that also sets expires_at.

threshold.description: Threshold-recovery configuration. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'threshold_recovery'.

k.description: Minimum share count required to reconstruct the recovery secret. MUST be >= 2; threshold=1 is forbidden because it collapses to a single-holder bearer.

n.description: Total number of shares issued. MUST equal shares.length and MUST be >= k.

vss_root_commitment.description: Optional VSS root commitment binding all shares' polynomial commitments. SHOULD be present for Feldman / Pedersen schemes.

reshare_policy.description: Proactive secret sharing / re-share cadence. Holders MUST be able to refresh shares without reconstructing the secret. Implementations SHOULD re-share at least once per `max_share_age_seconds`.

device_quorum.description: Device-quorum configuration. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'device_quorum'.

trusted_recovery_services.description: Recovery services explicitly declared in the principal's DID Document (or sovereign trust seal). Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'trusted_recovery_service'.

recovery_keys.description: Recovery signing keys this principal authorizes to satisfy a 'recovery_unlock' proof. Each entry binds a verification method (24-word Recovery Key derived signing key, or hardware-released equivalent) to the principal. A recovery_unlock proof's recovery_secret_ref MUST resolve to one of these entries that is non-revoked and within its validity window at the proof's binding time; the proof signature MUST verify under that entry's public key. Required when allowed_proof_kinds contains 'recovery_unlock'. See identity/key-management.md §7.5.2 and crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4 / §15.

approval_requirement.description: Two-person rule / cooldown enforcement layered on top of cryptographic proofs.

cooldown_seconds.description: Minimum wall-clock window between recovery announcement and effective key change. Receivers MUST reject control-stream Events whose accepted_at is earlier than announcement_at + cooldown_seconds.

announcement_required.description: When true, recovery MUST be announced on the principal control stream and visible to authorized devices before effective key change.

audit.description: Where the recovery strand MUST emit auditable records (recovery announcement, holder participation, completion receipt).

receipt_required.description: When true, recovery completion MUST produce a ck.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 record.

verification_method.description: DID URL identifying the principal signing key (or quorum coordinator) that issued the policy.

recovery_key_entry.description: A recovery signing key the principal authorizes for 'recovery_unlock' proofs. The verification_method is the stable recovery_secret_ref a recovery_unlock proof MUST reference; the proof signature is verified under this entry's public key resolved via verification_method.

verification_method.description: DID URL (e.g. `did:webvh:...#recovery-1`) identifying this recovery signing key. This is the value a recovery_unlock proof carries in recovery_secret_ref / verification_method and MUST be unique within recovery_keys[].

alg.description: Signature algorithm the recovery key signs with. v1 fixes this to Ed25519.

not_before.description: Earliest instant this recovery key may authorize a recovery_unlock proof.

expires_at.description: Instant after which this recovery key MUST NOT authorize a recovery_unlock proof.

revoked_at.description: When set, the entry is revoked from this instant onward and MUST NOT satisfy any recovery_unlock proof whose binding time is at or after it.

recovery_policy_summary.description: Read-model summary of the currently accepted recovery policy. `policy` carries the original ck.schema.recovery_policy.v1 object when the service can disclose it to the caller.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Convenience tuple equivalent to `{policy_id, policy_version: version}`. When present, it MUST match policy_id/version.

policy.description: Full accepted ck.schema.recovery_policy.v1 object. Omitted only when the caller is authorized to learn that a policy exists but not to receive holder/share details.

control_frontier.description: Optional principal control-stream frontier under which the active policy was observed.

recovery_policy_active_outcome.description: Response for ck.root.identity.recovery_policy.resource.get. `active_policy=null` is a successful read meaning no accepted recovery policy currently exists for the resolved principal.

principal_id.description: Resolved principal. Required when the request used an explicit principal_id selector; SHOULD be present on all authenticated reads.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Convenience tuple for the active policy. MUST be absent or null-equivalent when active_policy is null, and MUST match active_policy.policy_id/version when active_policy is present.

recovery_policy_publish_outcome.description: Response for ck.root.identity.recovery_policy.command.publish after accepting a ck.schema.recovery_policy.v1 publish or rotation.

holder.description: DID of the share holder. MAY be a user, a hardware module identified by did:key, or a custodial service. The holder DID does NOT inherit any business capability of the principal.

schemas/recovery-receipt.schema.json.title: Cokret Recovery Receipt
schemas/recovery-receipt.schema.json.description: Signed completion receipt for a principal recovery strand. Bound to the recovery_session_id used by every proof, backup unlock, and MLS Welcome replay action; written to either the audit Realm declared by the active recovery policy or — when audit policy permits — as an actor-private record on the Principal Control Realm. Formal recovery receipts are signed only after the recovering device has been accepted via ck.device.authorize; pre-authorization failures use server outcome/audit evidence instead. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15 step 7.

recovery_session_id.description: Stable session identifier used by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof, and MLS Welcome replay during this recovery. Receivers MUST reject receipts that reuse a session id already accepted for the same principal.

proof_digest.description: Canonical-JSON digest of the proof transcript used to satisfy the active recovery policy. Auditors recompute against the originating proof event to verify.

quorum_size.description: Required for device_quorum and threshold_recovery; equals the number of participating members / shares.

share_ids.description: When kind=threshold_recovery, the share_ids that participated. MUST be a subset of the active policy's shares[].

welcome_count.description: Number of MLS Welcomes successfully replayed for the recovering device.

outcome_reason_code.description: Free-form reason code; MUST be present when outcome != 'completed'.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the new_device_id's accepted device key. Receivers MUST resolve it through the principal control stream and verify that ck.device.authorize for new_device_id was accepted before this receipt was signed; service keys and unauthorised fresh-device keys MUST NOT sign a formal recovery_receipt.

schemas/recovery-session.schema.json.title: Cokret Recovery Session
schemas/recovery-session.schema.json.description: Wire contract for the device recovery session state machine. The root object is the recovery session state shape; request body/result helper shapes and kind-specific recovery proof transcripts live in $defs. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

challenge.description: base64url(no padding) encoding of 256 bits from a CSPRNG. The value is single-use and bound to one recovery_session_id.

proof_digest.description: Digest of the canonical recovery proof transcript that satisfied this session.

ssk_generation.description: Accepted cross-signing generation snapshotted when the session is created. Reducers MUST reject completion if the current accepted generation no longer equals this value.

rejection_reason_code.description: Closed enum. proof_failed: proof verification failures reached the server policy limit; operator_rejected: explicit operator/admin rejection; risk_policy: server risk policy rejection; superseded: replaced by a newer recovery session for the same principal/device.

expires_at.description: Session expiration. Default TTL is 900 seconds; deployments MAY shorten it and MUST NOT lengthen it unless a future recovery_policy field explicitly permits the override.

created_at.description: Recovery session creation/signing time. This is the created_at value used in the recovery proof transcript.

expected_recovery_policy_ref.description: Optional client CAS hint. Servers MUST snapshot the currently accepted policy; if this hint is present and differs, the request fails with recovery_policy_mismatch.

challenge.description: Echo of the server-issued session challenge. Mismatch fails as recovery_session_challenge_mismatch.

verification_method.description: Principal-grade DID control verification method authorized by the active recovery policy.

recovery_secret_ref.description: DID URL or recovery-policy key ref for the recovery key entry authorized at the session's created_at.

unlock_commitment.description: Public binding hash over the session transcript and recovery_secret_ref. Possession is proven by signature; this commitment prevents proof-shell substitution.

attestation_ref.description: Reference to service attestation evidence when required by the active recovery policy.

transcript_digest.description: Digest of the holder's share release transcript bound to share_id, holder, recovery_session_id, requesting_device_id, audience, and issued_at. For threshold_recovery / recovery_unlock the requesting device may be a not-yet-authorized new device; holder validation binds proof-of-possession and the recovery session instead of requiring an existing device record.

proof.description: Kind-specific recovery proof. Receivers reconstruct the canonical transcript from stored session state and the proof body, then verify that the active recovery policy allows this proof kind and its threshold/service/share constraints.

device_authorize_material.description: A complete, client-signed ck.device.authorize payload used by the recovery strand. It MUST also validate against event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/device_authorize_payload. The recovering client unlocks the self-signing key (SSK) from the did_recovery backup during the proof/verify phase, signs the new device's cross_signing_binding with it, submits the resulting ordinary Event Envelope to the principal control stream, and passes only the accepted authorization_event_id to recovery_session_complete_request_body. The server MUST verify before completing the recovery session: (a) device_id == session.requesting_device_id; (b) recovery_session_id == this session's id; (c) principal_id == session.principal_id; (d) cross_signing_binding.ssk_generation == session.ssk_generation (else device_recovery_ssk_generation_mismatch). Recovery is never a bootstrap-first-device case, so cross_signing_binding (not bootstrap_binding) is required.

device_signature.description: New-device self-signature proving possession of device_public_key. Satisfies event-payload.schema.json device_authorize_payload's proof/device_signature anyOf.

recovery_session_complete_request_body.description: The recovering client first submits, to POST /events on the principal control realm, (1) a `ck.device.authorize` (shape per $defs/device_authorize_material, also event-payload.schema.json device_authorize_payload) signed with the SSK unlocked from the did_recovery backup, and (2) a `ck.device.list_update` for the new device — both as ordinary signed Event Envelopes carrying the next actor_seq on the principal control stream. Completion then REFERENCES the resulting durable event ids; the server resolves each from the event store and verifies it is the right kind, bound to this recovery_session_id + requesting_device_id, and (for authorize) that its cross_signing_binding verifies against the accepted SSK. The server does not author/sign control events on the principal's behalf.

authorization_event_id.description: event_id of the client-submitted, accepted ck.device.authorize.

device_list_update_event_id.description: event_id of the client-submitted, accepted ck.device.list_update.

authorization_event_id.description: Accepted ck.device.authorize event emitted to the principal control stream.

device_list_update_event_id.description: Accepted ck.device.list_update event emitted to the principal control stream.

created_at.description: Session creation/signing time, not client proof creation time.

generic_recovery_transcript.description: Canonical transcript field set shared by recovery_unlock, device_quorum, trusted_recovery_service, and threshold_recovery proofs before adding kind-specific proof_body. Producers and receivers MUST bind exactly this session tuple.

proof_body.description: The selected proof object with signature bytes omitted where the kind-specific verification rule says so.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional intra-Realm Circle (models/circle.md) defining this Relation fact's effective scope, supplied in the submit payload. For weak-semantic privacy edges (confidential_discussion_of, agent_sidecar_of) the relation fact MUST be submitted with scope_circle_id pointing to the private Strand's Circle, so effective_scope=circle and non-members cannot enumerate the edge from the public endpoint (relation.md §3.2). For structural relations the resulting effective_scope MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope (circle.md §6.1).

effective_scope.description: Reducer-stamped immutable effective scope of this Relation fact, materialized from scope_circle_id at create time (circle.md §6.1-§6.2). For structural relations it MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope. Immutable across any later scope rebind. MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied submit payload (reducer-managed, reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed); the reducer stamps it on accept.

relation_kind.description: Relation semantic. The standard kind vocabulary (kind list, cardinality class, truth-source class, weak_semantic flag) is machine-indexed in artifacts/registry/relation-kind-registry.json; detailed dedupe/scope/conflict semantics in models/relation.md §3-§6. Cross-Realm constraint: structural relations 'contains' and 'belongs_to' MUST NOT cross Realm (resolved from_ref and to_ref MUST share the same realm_id); weak_semantic=true kinds per the registry MAY cross Realm subject to two-sided authorization. Stays a free string so extension profiles can add kinds; unregistered kinds are opaque edges (unknown_relation_kind), never container/visibility semantics.

rank.description: Top-level rank string for ordered relations (e.g. contains-list-strand position). Encoding follows conformance/encoding.md §9. Aligned with Space.rank so all rank-bearing canonical objects expose rank at the top level instead of fields.rank.

fields.description: Edge metadata. MUST NOT contain a 'rank' key — rank moved to the top level in v1 to align with Space.rank.

state.description: Relation state. 'tombstoned' covers both deletion and redaction; the originating reason is preserved on the ck.relation.tombstone / ck.redaction event, not on the materialized object.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ck.relation.tombstone / redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

ref.description: Typed canonical reference. Allowed kinds: realm, space, actor_profile, strand, message, morph, relation, event, view, blob metadata ID, content-addressed blob ref (active digest suites per artifacts/registry/digest-suite-registry.json; v1: sha256 / blake3), or DID. Space is a valid Relation endpoint (board/list containers, e.g. board --contains--> list). The blob ref suite set is aligned with blob.schema.json and notification.schema.json so any content-addressed blob ref accepted in those schemas is also accepted as a Relation endpoint.

RelationConflictDiagnostic.description: Projection-only conflict diagnostic emitted for deterministic_winner losers and require_review output. reducer_input MUST be false; MUST NOT be treated as canonical event bytes or dedupe authority. See zh/models/relation.md §6.

dedupe_key.description: Canonical projection of the dedupe key under which these candidates collided.

winner.description: The deterministic winner (event_digest bytewise-greatest per the single canonical tie-break rule, zh/conformance/encoding.md §4.2), or omitted-equivalent for require_review where no canonical winner is projected.
