losers.description: Conflict losers retained for audit and explicit repair. Bounded by the conflict fanout limit (v1 public profile: 16 total candidates including the winner).

event_digest.description: Canonical signed Event digest (<digest-suite>:<hex>), the bytewise tie-break key.

reason.description: Optional reason code for this candidate's disposition (e.g. relation_conflict_fanout_exceeded).

object_ref.description: Canonical object reference. Acceptable typed-id kinds match the v1 resource selector kind enum (see resource-selector-grammar.md §3.1). Notably MUST NOT include 'actor_profile' (use the 'actor' selector with did pattern), nor non-canonical 'board' / 'list' / 'card' / 'subject' / 'room' kinds — board / list / swimlane / calendar bucket are Space objects and MUST use the 'space' kind together with the 'allowed_space_kinds' constraint to restrict which Space kinds the grant covers.

actor_id.description: Concrete principal / service / agent DID. v1 forbids actor:*; actor selectors MUST NOT use a wildcard subject.

match_scope.description: Selector match breadth. exact matches only the named resource; children matches immediate children; subtree matches descendants including nested children; realm_wide is valid only when realm_id is present and limits matching to the named Realm. The normative algorithm is zh/authz/resource-selector-grammar.md ?6.

allOf.$comment: resource-selector-grammar.md §3.1: notification / read_cursor selectors are realm-scoped and the object part is *-only (notification:<realm>:* / read_cursor:<realm>:*). A bare {"kind":"read_cursor"} with no realm_id would otherwise match every principal's read cursors across all Realms (see C04-07). Force realm_id and forbid a precise object id (no notification_id / read_cursor_id field exists; selection is realm-wide *-only).
resource-selector-grammar.md ?3.1/?4.2/?6: space and circle selectors are Realm-scoped in v1; wildcard space/circle selectors MUST carry realm_id to avoid cross-Realm authorization expansion.

resource-selector-grammar.md §4.8/§8.1: actor:* is forbidden and an actor selector MUST carry a concrete principal DID. Force actor_id present so a bare {"kind":"actor"} is rejected at the schema layer rather than only at the reducer (selector_actor_wildcard_forbidden).

schemas/seal-transparency.schema.json.title: Cokret SealTransparency
schemas/seal-transparency.schema.json.description: Seal transparency wire objects (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.4): an append-only log entry binding one accepted Seal tuple, and an independent auditor attestation over a log range. The log makes split-view attacks (showing different Seal chains to different receivers) detectable: an operator must either publish consistently or fork the log, and a log fork is provable from two signed entries with the same log_index. Top-level object is a log entry; auditor attestations use #/$defs/auditor_attestation.

log_id.description: Stable identifier of the transparency log (operator URL, DID, or registry name).

log_index.description: Zero-based append-only position. Two differently-signed entries with the same (log_id, log_index) are a provable log fork.

prev_entry_digest.description: Digest of the previous entry's canonical bytes (hash chain). null only for log_index 0.

auditor_attestation.description: Signed statement by an independent auditor (peer Realm or third party) that it verified the log range [from_index, to_index]: append-only consistency, Seal signature validity, control_event_set_root extension monotonicity, and completeness_root per-actor monotonicity. Clients accept grade=witnessed only when deployment policy's required attestation count is met.

head_entry_digest.description: Digest of the entry at to_index, binding the attested range head.

checks.description: All checks MUST be true; an auditor that cannot assert a check MUST NOT issue the attestation.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical entry / attestation bytes with the signature field omitted.

schemas/seal.schema.json.title: Cokret Seal
schemas/seal.schema.json.description: Wire shape of a Cokret CBA Seal. It finalizes only control-plane Events. `delta[]` is the canonical set of new control-plane event_digest values introduced by this Seal; cumulative coverage is derived recursively as covered_set(S)=set(S.delta) union covered_set(predecessor_refs[]). `control_event_set_root` authenticates that recursive covered_set and is used for basis, inclusion and non-membership proofs. Optional data_* roots are observational only and MUST NOT gate DataEvents. Identity & signature model (see zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §6): the typed `id` (`ck:seal:<algo>:<hex>`) is content-derived — its hex equals H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm. Seal canonical bytes are the canonical JSON of every signed top-level field EXCEPT id and notary_signature. The `notary_signature` is NOT part of canonical bytes. Receivers MUST recompute H(seal_canonical_bytes) and verify the notary signature over the same bytes.

id.description: Content-derived typed reference. hex part MUST equal H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm, where seal_canonical_bytes is the canonical JSON of every signed body field EXCEPT `id` and `notary_signature`. Receivers MUST recompute and verify; mismatch → digest_mismatch. NEVER include `id` in the hash input — that would create a self-reference.

delta.description: Canonical bytewise-sorted set of new control-plane event_digest values introduced by this Seal. DataEvent digests MUST NOT appear here. Receivers MUST reject the Seal if any delta entry is already covered by a predecessor, if any entry is not a known valid Control Move digest, or if the list is not canonical sorted and duplicate-free.

control_event_set_root.description: Authenticated root over the recursive covered_set of this Seal. Default construction is RFC6962 Merkle root over canonical bytewise-sorted covered_set(S); inclusion uses Merkle audit path and non-membership uses sorted-neighbor proof. The root is not computed over delta[] alone.

state_root.description: Merkle root of control-plane cell state only.

completeness_root.description: Control-plane per-actor interval / chain-head completeness commitment. It does not prove absence of unknown actors.

notary_seq.description: Per-signer or committee slot sequence used for equivocation detection. Same signer and same realm_id MUST NOT sign two different canonical Seal bodies with the same notary_seq.

data_view_root.description: Optional observational root of KeyView records keyed by data cell id. It is not a DataEvent admission gate.

data_event_set_root.description: Optional observational root over DataEvent digests seen in this seal window. Missing DataEvents are not invalid.

coverage_scope.description: Optional observational coverage declaration for data_view_root / data_event_set_root. The object is intentionally closed only by deployment profiles; core verifiers treat it as signed diagnostic material.

covered_event_digests.description: Optional compaction materialization of the full recursive covered_set(S), canonical bytewise-sorted and duplicate-free. When present, receivers MUST verify it equals set(delta) union all predecessor covered sets and that control_event_set_root is computed over this exact set. Non-compaction Seals normally omit it.

previous_state_root.description: Hash-algorithm transition only: present iff this Seal is a Transition Seal under ck.profile.hash_transition.v1. When present, MUST be computed with the previous digest_algorithm algorithm over the same recursive covered_set as state_root, and MUST equal the receiver-recomputed root under that algorithm before the new state_root is accepted. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.2.

previous_digest_algorithm.description: Profile id of the previous hash algorithm. Required iff previous_state_root is present; absent on non-transition Seals.

notary_signature.description: Signature over seal_canonical_bytes (every signed body field EXCEPT `id` and `notary_signature`). MUST NOT enter the canonical bytes itself — signatures never sign themselves. Seal is not an Event Envelope, so its signature uses the generic non-Event proof field `payload_digest`; that value MUST equal H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm. Event Envelope proofs use `event_digest` instead.

sealed_at.description: Wall-clock timestamp at which the notary signed this Seal. Used only for reducer-derived projection timestamps and freshness diagnostics; not a lattice winner input.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key. Bare DID is not valid for signatures because verifiers need a stable verification method, not only a controller DID.

payload_digest.description: Hash of seal_canonical_bytes for this non-Event Seal signature. Do not rename to event_digest: event_digest is reserved for Event Envelope proofs.

leakage_class.description: Machine-readable search leakage class. ck.profile.search.blind_index.v1 uses deterministic_token; ck.profile.search.forward_private.v1 requires forward_private; access_hiding is reserved for explicit PIR/ORAM-backed profiles.

token_rotation_cadence_ms.description: Maximum intended interval between search token generations for profiles that rotate index keys or OPRF blinds.

schemas/service-describe.schema.json.title: Cokret Service Describe
schemas/service-describe.schema.json.description: Canonical service describe response returned by ck.server.query.describe and per-surface describe operations. It combines stable service metadata (service_did, service_type, protocol_version, profiles, bindings, auth, limits, plaintext visibility and rate-limit policy) with claim-level partitions: implemented_features, claimed_profiles, verified_profiles, experimental_features and compat_surfaces. The `supported_operations` field MUST list endpoint-callable operation_ids. Constraint: when `development_mode=true`, the service MUST NOT advertise any `verified_profiles` entry, and clients MUST verify the referenced verification artifacts before treating verified_profiles as production conformance. See service-surface.md §3.0.

service_did.description: DID of the service endpoint making this describe claim.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain for this service. Receivers use it as the canonical receive-context replay boundary for cross-deployment proofs and federation transactions.

service_type.description: Registered lowercase service_type such as principal_server, sync_node, directory_service, push_gateway, applet_service, archive_node, key_recovery_service or recovery_service.

supported_operations.description: operation_ids that this endpoint can actually be invoked with. Element format SHOULD match the canonical operation_registry ids (e.g. `ck.self.events.command.submit`).

supported_bindings.description: Transport binding declarations for this service.

supported_features.description: Feature identifiers (`ck.feature.*`) the service supports. Distinct from profile claims.

auth_metadata.description: Authentication and session metadata needed by clients before calling protected operations.

methods.description: Authentication methods offered for this principal/account surface. Methods describe proof providers, standard discovery, and the proof kind accepted by the Account Authority. Cokret gate/account routing is always derived from account_authority.

limits.description: Operational limits such as body size, batch size, TTL, pagination or retention bounds.

max_get_query_selectors.description: Maximum total selector count (`realms[]` + `actors[]`) that this service accepts on GET /_cokret/self/events. Clients SHOULD use POST /_cokret/self/events/query when the selector count exceeds this value or filters are sensitive enough to avoid URL logging. If omitted, clients use the v1 default of 8.

plaintext_visibility.description: Plaintext boundary declaration. Omission is not allowed: callers use this object to decide whether the service may be registered as plaintext-visible. An empty object means the service claims no plaintext classes; Realm plaintext_visible_services entries MUST match non-empty data_classes here.

data_classes.description: Closed machine-checkable classes of plaintext or reversible derived content this service is implemented to receive.

max_visibility.description: Maximum plaintext visibility class the service claims it can receive. Omitted is treated as none unless data_classes is non-empty.

privacy_derivation.description: Machine-readable privacy-preserving identifier derivation claims. Secret material is never published here; only profile and epoch metadata needed for audit and rotation checks.

secret_scope.description: The HMAC salt/pepper is unique to this service context and MUST NOT be shared across Principal Servers, organizations, or push routes.

salt_epoch_id.description: Opaque public epoch label for the active secret. This is not the secret salt value.

receive_policy_constraints.description: Deployment/admin upper bound for subject-private invite/contact receive policies. Principal Servers SHOULD expose this in describe so clients can show which user reachability preferences are capped by server policy.

rate_limit_policy_id.description: Identifier for a cacheable, verifiable rate-limit policy object with the same minimum fields as rate_limit_policy. See zh/sync/api-conventions.md §8.

rate_limit_policy.description: Inline rate-limit policy. If the service can return rate_limited, entries[] MUST expose at least endpoint or operation_id, rate_limit_scope, a window/limit tuple or a retry hint; an empty entries[] explicitly means no predictable endpoint-level rate limit beyond generic abuse protection.

egress_network_policy.description: Coarse outbound-network policy for SSRF protection. Public describe MAY omit sensitive allowlist entries; authenticated operator describe MAY return the complete policy. Normative semantics are defined in zh/sync/api-conventions.md §11.2.

resource_types.description: Directory-service resource classes indexed by ck.find.directory.query.describe. Required when service_type=directory_service.

discovery_profiles.description: Directory discovery profiles and extension profile ids advertised by ck.find.directory.query.describe. Required when service_type=directory_service.

restricted_query_proof.description: Whether the directory requires holder-approved proof for restricted or privacy-sensitive query classes.

ingest_modes.description: Directory ingest modes supported by this instance.

accept_policy_kind.description: Directory resource acceptance policy advertised by ck.find.directory.query.describe.

accept_policy_ref.description: Optional human-readable or governance reference describing how a resource obtains directory acceptance.

default_ttl_seconds.description: Default directory entry TTL in seconds.

max_ttl_seconds.description: Maximum accepted directory entry TTL in seconds.

revalidation_grace_seconds.description: Grace period for refreshing indexed resources after TTL expiry.

accepted_resource_kinds.description: Subset of resource kinds accepted by this directory instance.

accepted_did_methods.description: Principal/governance DID methods accepted by this directory instance.

takedown_contact.description: Operator takedown notification or appeal contact, expressed as a DID or URL.

rate_limits.description: Readable per-DID, per-organization or per-IP directory quota limits.

implemented_features.description: feature_ids the service has implementation code for but does NOT necessarily claim conformance for. Tooling that builds a conformance matrix MUST treat this strictly weaker than `claimed_profiles`.

claimed_profiles.description: Profiles the service self-claims membership in. `claim_kind` MUST be `self_claimed`; verified-only assertions belong under `verified_profiles` and MUST NOT appear here.

verified_profiles.description: Profiles for which a Conformance Verifier run (conformance-suite.md §6.2) has produced a passing verification artifact. Each entry MUST identify the verification run, artifact hash, artifact retrieval reference, verifier DID, verifier signature, and verification timestamp. When the service is in `development_mode=true` this array MUST be empty.

artifact_ref.description: URI or transparency-log reference from which the verification artifact can be fetched.

verifier_did.description: DID of the Conformance Verifier that signed the artifact statement.

signature.description: Signature over profile_id, verification_run_id, artifact_digest, artifact_ref, verifier and timestamp.

experimental_features.description: feature_ids that the service exposes but explicitly does NOT promise stable interop for. Clients MUST treat these as non-load-bearing for protocol-level decisions.

compat_surfaces.description: External-interop surfaces this service exposes outside its claimed Cokret v1 conformance.

development_mode.description: Mirror of the service's development_mode flag. When true, `verified_profiles` MUST be empty.

cidr.description: IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR string. Parsability and address-family semantics are enforced by the egress policy evaluator.

origin.description: Absolute origin of the client-visible Account Authority.

gate_account_base.description: Absolute base URL from which all client-visible /_cokret/gate/account/* endpoints MUST be derived.

schemas/service-operation-dtos.schema.js.title: Cokret Service Operation DTOs
schemas/service-operation-dtos.schema.js.description: Canonical request and response DTOs for service operations. OpenAPI components reference this artifact so SDK and conformance tooling use one schema source.

grant_jwt.description: The near-expiry DPoP-bound session grant to rotate. Presented with a DPoP holder proof for the key bound into the grant's cnf.jkt.

audience.description: Optional; MUST equal the grant's bound audience if present (audience MUST NOT change across rotation, else audience_mismatch).

device_id.description: Concrete authorized device restoring the soft-logged-out grant chain. MUST match the persisted grant device binding.

proof_kind.description: Fresh proof kind for soft-logout recovery. Current Account Authority implementations MUST accept did_bound_signature or paired_device_proof and fail closed on unsupported kinds.

request_canonical_digest.description: Digest of the soft-logout restore request transcript bound by the proof.

audience.description: MUST equal the session grant audience.

expires_at.description: MUST be after issued_at and no more than 300 seconds later.

signature.description: Detached JWS over the soft-logout proof transcript.

verification_method.description: Optional DID URL expected to match the detached JWS kid; the DID component MUST match the session grant subject.

grant_jwt.description: Rotated grant: same subject/scope/audience, cnf.jkt unchanged, fresh minutes-to-hours expiry.

session_public_key.description: JWK the rotated grant is bound to (the device holder key).

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the holder key (equals the grant's cnf.jkt).

previous_grant_id.description: The prior grant, single-use revoked on success.

AuthSessionLogoutRequestBody.description: Service-to-service Account Authority to Auth Server request that logs out the Auth-side session owning a ck.session.grant rotation chain.

grant_jwt.description: Session grant used to locate the Auth-side session and its rotation chain.

logout_request_digest.description: Optional digest of the validated client-visible account /logout request that caused this S2S sub-operation.

validated_at.description: When the Account Authority validated the client-visible account /logout request.

reason_code.description: Reason for logging out the Auth-side session. v1 defines only account_logout for this S2S sub-operation.

grant_chain_terminated.description: Whether the grant rotation chain is now unable to refresh, including the already-terminated idempotent case.

auth_session_logged_out.description: Whether the underlying Auth-side browser/auth session is now logged out, including the already-logged-out idempotent case.

SessionGrantIntrospectRequestBody.description: Server-to-server session-grant introspection request. Exactly one of id / grant_jwt identifies the grant.

id.description: Grant id. Mutually exclusive with grant_jwt.

grant_jwt.description: The signed grant JWT to introspect. Mutually exclusive with id.

audience.description: Audience the caller is validating the grant for; a mismatch yields status audience_mismatch.

proof.description: Optional S2S holder confirmation signed by the session key bound into the grant. Principal Servers validating /_cokret/self/* grant+DPoP requests do not require a client-carried introspection proof; they verify the request DPoP locally against the returned cnf_jkt.

proof_jwt.description: JWS over ck.session_grant.introspection_proof.v1 claims (grant_id, grant_jwt_hash, audience, challenge, issued_at, expires_at).

active.description: Whether the grant is currently valid for the requested audience. READ-ONLY: introspection never consumes the grant.

proof_required.description: Whether an additional S2S holder proof is required to confirm the grant active for this introspection request. Default Principal Server grant+DPoP validation uses the request DPoP instead of this field.

one_time_use_consumed.description: Always false: introspection is read-only and never consumes single-use state (rotation is the refresh endpoint's job).

SessionGrantIntrospectGrant.description: Non-secret grant metadata returned to the validating Principal Server. Never includes the grant JWT, refresh token, or session private key.

session_public_key.description: Session signing key (JWK) for RFC 9421 PoP verification on /_cokret/self/* (api-conventions §3.2). Server-to-server only.

cnf_jkt.description: RFC 7638 JWK SHA-256 thumbprint of the holder (DPoP) key the grant is bound to (cnf.jkt); the Principal Server uses it to verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_cokret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3). Server-to-server only.

revoked.description: Whether a live device session was revoked.

redirect_url.description: Deployment-controlled browser handoff URL. This outcome MUST NOT contain SessionGrantOutcome, ck.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance is only via SessionGrantRequestBody.proof.proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange.

AuthzCheckRequestBody.description: ck.self.authz.query.check input — local capability projection / preflight / diagnostic query. `resource` is optional because some actions (e.g. `ck.realm.create`, identity-scoped actions) have no Realm-bound target. The result is not a signed Policy Server decision and MUST NOT be used as Event auth_context, reducer accept proof, or cross-service authorization fact; dynamic policy obligations use ck.self.policy.query.check.

actor_id.description: Subject DID whose authorization is being checked.

resource.description: Optional resource selector (Realm / Strand / Space / Morph / etc.).

context.description: Optional decision context — claim presentations, frontier reference, request metadata.

AuthzCheckOutcome.description: ck.self.authz.query.check diagnostic/preflight decision. See zh/authz/capabilities.md §18. This shape may include freshness and obligation hints, but any obligation that affects reducer admission or external state MUST be re-issued and signed through PolicyCheckOutcome.

decision.description: `allow` / `hard_deny` are terminal decisions. `soft_deny` is an evaluated policy soft refusal. `quarantine` / `require_review` are Policy Server-mediated soft outcomes (the request enters async review). Transient dependency or freshness failures are reported through `freshness_state`, `reason_code`, and `retry_after_ms`, not as policy decision values.

freshness_state.description: Frontier freshness classification for revocation-sensitive decisions; see zh/authz/capabilities.md §18.2.

last_known_frontier_age_ms.description: Age of the newest revocation/auth frontier evidence used for this decision. Present when freshness_state is stale or unknown.

notary_status.description: Coarse status of the notary/frontier source used to diagnose stale or unknown revocation freshness.

reason_code.description: Registered reason code. High-risk stale or unknown revocation freshness returns revocation_freshness_unknown.

retry_after_ms.description: Set when `freshness_state ∈ {stale,unknown}` or a retryable `reason_code` is present; client SHOULD back off this amount before retry.

obligations.description: Policy server obligations (challenge / rate_limit / drop_attachment) the caller MUST satisfy before the action proceeds.

blob_ref.description: Target blob. MUST be a content-addressed ref or visible blob metadata id.

realm_id.description: Realm binding for Realm-owned blobs. Servers MUST include the same realm_id in the presign envelope and reject mismatches with blob metadata; only deployment-public/global blobs may omit this field.

max_age_seconds.description: Client-requested TTL upper bound. Server clamps to the smaller of this value, the issuing grant's `blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds` constraint, and the deployment-level cap.

purpose.description: Intended rendering / download mode. Servers MAY apply purpose-specific Content-Disposition or rate limits.

url.description: Fully-qualified URL clients can pass to browser primitives. Contains the `presign` query parameter, `blob_ref`, and a presign envelope bound to `realm_id` for Realm-owned blobs.

expires_at.description: Server-determined expiry; SHOULD be earlier than `now() + max_age_seconds`.

type.description: Backend binding type identifier (livekit / cokret-native / etc.).

backend_token.description: Opaque to Cokret protocol; type-specific (e.g. LiveKit JWT).

participant_identity.description: SFU-local short handle, scope `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`. UUIDv7-form rtc_participant typed ID.

messages.description: DeviceMessageEnvelope items; not Event Envelope objects. This endpoint does not serve the durable Event timeline.

ack_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever messages[] is non-empty. Covers this page plus all previously delivered messages for the authenticated device. Queue deletion happens only through ck.self.device_messages.command.ack with this token, never through the from= read cursor (client-sync.md §10.1).

next_cursor.description: Read-only continuation position; advancing it MUST NOT delete queued messages.

lost.description: SHOULD be true when unacknowledged messages were dropped (expiry or capacity) since the device's last acknowledged position; clients SHOULD trigger key recovery paths.

ack_token.description: Acknowledgement token previously issued to the same (principal_id, device_id) via an account subscribe to_device batch or a device_messages get page. Acknowledgement is cumulative and monotonic: the server prunes all delivered messages up to and including the token's bound queue position. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens MUST be rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything. Naturally idempotent; no Idempotency-Key required.

ok.description: True when the acknowledgement was accepted, including the legal no-op case of re-acking the same or an older token (the acknowledged position MUST NOT move backward).

pruned_count.description: Number of queued messages actually deleted by this acknowledgement.

did_method.description: DID method discriminator (e.g. web, webvh, key). Verifiers dispatch method-specific validation from this value and the did prefix.

seq.description: Optional method sequence number when the DID method exposes one.

prev_event_digest.description: Optional previous operation hash / key-log head, when required by the DID method.

operation.description: DID method-specific raw operation object. This is not a generic JSON Patch and MUST be validated by the selected DID method adapter.

policy_context.description: Optional resolver / registry policy context bound into authorization and audit.

seq.description: New method sequence number when available.

discovery_state.description: Signed ck.{kind}.discovery payload, including its proof.

governance_proof.description: Signature proof by the resource governance key, equivalent strength to announce.discovery_state.proof.

withdrawal_ref.description: Directory-local audit reference for the withdrawal; not a registered ck:<kind> typed ID.

DirectoryTakedownAppealRequestBody.description: Resource-side appeal packet against an operator takedown; the bound fields and governance signature are normative per discovery-directory.md §8.7.

takedown_id.description: The operator takedown_id from the takedown notice.

argument_digest.description: Digest of the appeal argument / evidence bundle (sha256:<hex>).

governance_proof.description: Signature by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate, equivalent strength to withdraw.governance_proof.

DirectoryTakedownAppealOutcome.description: Signed decision receipt acknowledging an appeal submission per discovery-directory.md §8.7 step 3.

appeal_id.description: Directory-local audit reference for the appeal; not a registered ck:<kind> typed ID.

decision_receipt.description: Signed Directory decision receipt; status pending until adjudicated.

EphemeralSubmitOutcome.description:
Result of ck.ephemeral.send. `accepted=true` means the Sync Service
admitted the short-lived signal into its ephemeral fanout path. No
Event ID, actor_seq, Seal coverage, or durable receipt is minted.

dispatched_to.description: Optional implementation hint for fanout recipients queued locally.

EventView.description: Result of ck.self.events.resource.get — a single complete Event Envelope, RedactedEventView, or ReferenceLockedEventStub with optional visibility / receipt hints. Redacted / locked variants are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be used as reducer input.

visibility.description: Caller-visible policy hint for this event (history visibility class, E2EE envelope class).

receipts.description: Event batch receipts witnessing this event, if visible.

realms.description: Filter by Realm IDs. UNION within, intersection with `actors[]`.

actors.description: Filter by Actor DIDs. UNION within, intersection with `realms[]`.

before.description: Return events strictly older than this cursor position (exclusive).

after.description: Return events strictly newer than this cursor position (exclusive).

order.description: Same semantics as the GET form `order` query parameter.

include_completeness.description: Request range-completeness attestation references covering the returned page (service-http-binding.md §3.3.6). Only effective when the service advertises events_query_range_completeness in supported_features; services that do not advertise it MUST ignore this parameter.

EventsQueryOutcome.description:
Result of ck.self.events.query.scan (GET form) and ck.self.events.query.scan_body (POST/body
form). Ordering follows the "近邻先返回" rule unless `order` was
explicitly set on the request; see service-http-binding.md §3.3.3.

prev_cursor.description: Absolute-direction cursor toward older events; pass to next request's `before=`.

next_cursor.description: Absolute-direction cursor toward newer events; pass to next request's `after=`.

has_more.description: True if more events remain in the `prev_cursor` (older) direction; SHOULD ignore `next_cursor` direction (subscribe / poll instead).

range_completeness.description: Optional. Present only when the request set include_completeness=true, the service advertises events_query_range_completeness, and at least one ck.attestation.range_completeness attestation covers the returned page's range (service-http-binding.md §3.3.6). Absence means the range is un-attested — neither an error nor a completeness confirmation. Clients verify per operations-sync.md §6.4.4 (root recompute, actor_seq_ranges check, witness_disagreement fail-closed).

attestation_refs.description: Event ids of ck.attestation.range_completeness events whose union of scopes covers the returned page. Over-coverage is legal; clients intersect scopes during verification.

attestations.description: Optional inline complete ck.attestation.range_completeness EventEnvelope objects for the referenced attestations. Every inline event's event_id MUST appear in attestation_refs and clients MUST verify the EventEnvelope signature / event_digest before using its payload. Servers MAY omit this field and let clients backfill the attestation events by id.

EventsResolveRequestBody.description: ck.self.events.query.resolve request body. At least one of event_ids or event_digests MUST be non-empty.

EventsResolveOutcome.description: ck.self.events.query.resolve result. `events[]` and `missing[]` plus optional `unauthorized[]` form a partition of the requested set.

missing.description: IDs / hashes that were requested but do not exist or are not visible (indistinguishable per visibility rules).

unauthorized.description: Optional split of missing into a separately-named bucket when policy explicitly distinguishes auth failure from non-existence.

EventsSubmitOutcome.description:
Result of ck.events.submit. Tracks per-event acceptance / duplication /
rejection along with the post-write frontier and an optional barrier
cursor for read-your-writes.

accepted.description: Event IDs that entered the accepted set for the first time. Idempotent re-submissions of identical bodies are sealed via duplicate[], not re-listed here.

duplicate.description: Event IDs whose canonical bytes matched a prior accepted event (idempotent no-op).

quarantine.description: Event IDs deferred to async / human verification.

actor_frontier.description: Per-actor frontier after this submit (subset of full frontier visible to caller).

realm_frontier.description: Per-Realm frontier after this submit. In v1 the replication/security boundary is the Realm, not an in-Realm Space container; the `space_frontier` field name is forbidden on the wire.

cursor.description: Optional barrier cursor (purpose=barrier) bound to the most recently accepted event.

original_outcome.description: Present only when status="historical_only" (idempotency-cache replay after origin key revoke / binding or peer-policy change, see sync/federation.md section 8.5.1): carries the originally cached outcome verbatim as historical diagnostics. The nested outcome's status MUST NOT be "historical_only"; the top-level accepted[] MUST be empty in that case. Absent for all other status values.

IdentityDocumentView.description: Result of ck.root.identity.document.resource.get — current DID Document plus normalized view hints.

did_document.description: Raw DID Core document with W3C field names preserved.

normalized_view.description:
Optional Cokret normalized principal view (snake_case) — derived
projection only, NOT a re-publishable DID Document. See
zh/identity/identity-did.md §6.

method_evidence.description: Method-specific proof material (e.g. did:webvh history head, witness signatures).

IdentityLogListOutcome.description: Result of ck.root.identity.log.query.list — paginated DID key-log entries for the requested DID.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor for the next page when has_more=true.

IdentityReceiptListOutcome.description: Result of ck.root.identity.receipts.query.list — witness receipts for a DID key-log head.

threshold_met.description: True when the returned receipt set satisfies the method or deployment witness threshold for the requested head. Omitted when the registry cannot evaluate threshold policy for this query.

PolicyCheckRequestBody.description: ck.self.policy.query.check input bound to a Realm authorization context.

source_ip_digest.description: Keyed, unlinkable derivation of the request source IP (e.g. HMAC-SHA256 under a service-private, salt-epoch-rotated secret bound to the calling service_did), encoded as sha256:<64 hex>. The sha256: prefix denotes the 32-byte digest container, NOT a bare SHA-256 of the IP address; unkeyed IP hashes are forbidden. Derivation, rotation and namespace rules: zh/authz/policy-server.md §3.1. High-privacy (relay/OHTTP) deployments MAY omit this field.

PolicyCheckOutcome.description: Result of ck.self.policy.query.check — signed decision bound to authorization, policy, and membership frontier hashes.

bound_to.description: Request context covered by the policy decision signature. Allows receivers to verify a forwarded decision without guessing transcript fields.

auth_state_digest.description: Accepted authorization state hash used when producing the decision.

policy_frontier_digest.description: Policy source frontier / digest used when producing the decision.

membership_frontier_digest.description: Membership / role frontier digest used when producing the decision.

kid.description: DID URL of the Policy Server verification method.

sig.description: Detached signature over the policy decision transcript.

principal_id.description: Principal DID the grant is requested for. REQUIRED for every proof_kind EXCEPT oidc_code_exchange: for first sign-in via oidc_code_exchange the client MAY omit principal_id and the Account Authority derives/mints the principal DID from the verified id_token and returns it in SessionGrantOutcome.principal_id. When present for oidc_code_exchange it MUST match the principal the Account Authority resolves for the verified subject.

agent_key_authorization_ref.description:
`ck.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay (CKP-0008 §4.6). Event ref of the accepted
`ck.agent.key.authorize` that authorized the runtime key. REQUIRED when
`proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; MUST be omitted for human session grants.

agent_scope_request.description:
`ck.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay (CKP-0008 §4.6). Narrowing hints for the
issued session scope; the server still intersects with the agent's accepted
capability grants and Realm policy. REQUIRED when `proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`;
MUST be omitted for human session grants. `track_names` is a request-side
narrowing field only — the materialized session grant MUST express track scope
via the canonical `allowed_tracks` constraint, not via a new `track_names` grant.

applet_delegation.description: Applet-specific delegated session binding. When present, the session grant, proof digest, persistence row, introspection metadata, and revoke selector are bound to the same applet_id, effective_scope, and registration_epoch.

proof_kind.description:
`agent_key_proof` selects the `ck.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay branch (CKP-0008 §4.6).
Implementations MUST route `agent_key_proof` to an independent validator and MUST NOT
fall back to password / OIDC / passkey validators for this branch.

issuer.description: OIDC issuer selected from ServiceDescribe.auth_metadata.methods[].issuer. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

client_id.description: OIDC public client id selected from the advertised auth method. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

redirect_uri.description: Redirect URI used in the authorization request. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

state.description: OIDC authorization response state. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

nonce.description: OIDC nonce bound to the authorization request and id_token. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

authorization_code.description: OIDC authorization code. Account Authority exchanges this code at the issuer token_endpoint when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

code_verifier.description: PKCE code_verifier corresponding to the authorization request. Required when proof_kind is oidc_code_exchange.

verification_method.description:
`ck.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay (CKP-0008 §4.6). DID URL of the runtime
signing key (`<agent_principal_id>#<key-fragment>`). REQUIRED when
`proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; the DID component MUST bit-identically equal
`principal_id` after stripping the fragment / query — otherwise the endpoint
returns `verification_method_principal_mismatch`. MUST be omitted for human
proof kinds.

allOf.description:
Machine-enforceable agent_key_proof branch selector. When `proof.proof_kind` is
`agent_key_proof`, the request MUST carry the `ck.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay
fields (`agent_key_authorization_ref`, `agent_scope_request`, `proof.verification_method`);
when it is any other enum value, those fields MUST be absent. SDKs and server-side
validators MUST reject violations at schema-validation time, not at proof-validator
time.

Machine-enforceable OIDC code exchange branch. Account Authority, not the client, exchanges the authorization code at the issuer token_endpoint and validates issuer, state, nonce, redirect_uri, principal binding, device binding and request canonical digest before issuing SessionGrantOutcome.

session_grant.description: Short-lived bearer/session grant bound to the requested principal, device and audience.

grant_id.description: Stable id of the issued session grant. Returned for every grant (human and agent) so the client can reference, refresh, introspect or revoke this exact grant without re-parsing the opaque session_grant. Mirrors SessionGrantRefreshOutcome.grant_id.

session_public_key.description: JWK of the holder/session key the grant is bound to (the device holder key). The client needs this to perform RFC 9421 PoP and to derive the DPoP cnf.jkt for /_cokret/self/* requests (api-conventions.md §3.2 / §3.3); returning it at issue time avoids a mandatory introspect round-trip before the first self-path request. Equals the grant's bound session_public_key for both human and agent grants. Mirrors SessionGrantRefreshOutcome.session_public_key.

audience.description: Audience the grant is bound to (the Principal Server / service the grant is valid for). MUST equal the grant's bound audience. Mirrors SessionGrantRefreshOutcome.audience.

scope_details.description:
`ck.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay (CKP-0008 §4.6). Materialized narrow scope
actually granted to the agent runtime session, after intersecting `agent_scope_request`
with capability grants and Realm policy. Present iff the request was the
`proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"` branch; absent for human session grants.

participation.description: `ck.profile.agent_participation_policy.v1` overlay (CKP-0016, service-surface.md §10.1). Present when the agent session scope covers participation-aware scope. Each entry is isomorphic to agent_participation_entry ({participation_scope, selection, ceiling, effective}). The runtime MUST treat this array as a behavioral contract; the server still enforces capability grants, dispatcher gates and reducer checks as the hard boundary.

ActorDid.description: Bare DID used as a Cokret actor/principal identifier. DID URL fragments belong in verification_method, not actor_id/principal_id.

allOf.description:
Actor-supplied ck.self.events.command.submit input envelope. It reuses the base Event
shape for actor intent fields but forbids reducer-managed accepted-output
projections such as actor_kind and effective_scope. Services stamp those
fields only after accept and expose them on read/query/sync envelopes.

frontier.description:
Either an actor frontier (`{actor_id, actor_seq, event_id}`) or a
Realm Seal view (`{realm_id, seal_id, control_event_set_root,
state_root, hlc?}`) shape depending on which selector was passed;
servers MUST NOT leak frontiers across visibility boundaries.
The Realm shape is the registered account-client source for minting
a single-leaf Control Move `seal_basis` (`leaves=[seal_id]`) and a
DataEvent `seal_ref`; for the caller's own principal control realm
the Principal Server MUST serve it (an initialized Realm always has
at least its genesis Seal). Clients MUST fail closed when this
source is unavailable instead of fabricating a basis.

EventsFrontierFederationPeerState.description: Federation peer ck.peer.events.query.frontier response. Requires S2S signed trust-domain headers.

heads.description: Current federation-visible head Event IDs for this Realm.

max_hlc.description: Maximum HLC observed by the issuer at this frontier, when available.

frontier_root.description: Hash commitment returned to an authorized federation peer.

actor_seq_upper_bounds.description: Per-actor sequence upper bounds returned to an authorized federation peer.

witness_receipts.description: Optional witness or receipt-service attestations over the observed frontier.

signature.description: Service signature over the peer frontier response.

EventReadItem.description: A readable event item. Complete EventEnvelope is the only reducer input shape. RedactedEventView and ReferenceLockedEventStub are projection/completeness evidence for callers that may know the source event exists but may not receive its full canonical payload bytes.

event_digest.description: Digest of the complete canonical Event Envelope bytes with proofs and unsigned removed. The caller cannot recompute it from this redacted view; it is a commitment used with inclusion / availability proofs.

payload_digest.description: Optional digest commitment to the canonical payload object before masking.

inclusion_proof.description: Optional proof that the committed event_digest is included in an Event set / Seal / range-completeness root visible to the caller.

reducer_input.description: Redacted views are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be fed into a reducer as Event Envelope input.

event_id.description: Present only when the source event id is already visible to the caller; omitted when even the event id would distinguish target existence.

realm_id.description: The source Realm boundary visible to the caller. Target Realm identifiers hidden by reference-disclosure policy MUST NOT appear.

event_digest.description: Optional source-event commitment when the source event is known but its payload is locked.

reason_code.description: Reasons that would reveal target existence MUST be collapsed to not_found_or_unauthorized for unauthorized callers.

inclusion_proof.description: Optional non-disclosing proof commitment. MUST NOT contain hidden target refs or target Realm metadata.

reducer_input.description: Locked stubs are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be fed into a reducer as Event Envelope input.

EventsSubmitBatchRequestBody.description: Batch ck.self.events.command.submit request used by account clients.

FederationServiceBindingRef.description:
Request-level service binding snapshot carried by federation
service-to-service ck.peer.events.command.submit calls. This is metadata for the
receiver to verify the sender's delivery decision; client writes omit it.

reducer_profile_digest.description: SHA-256 over the Cokret canonical JSON bytes of the matching digest_input object in artifacts/registry/reducer-profile-registry.json. Receivers MUST recompute from their effective Realm reducer profile and reject the whole federation batch with reducer_profile_mismatch on mismatch.

ProjectionAssignedToRelation.description: Read-model edge backing a Strand assigned_to Relation. relation_id is needed by clients to tombstone the assignment; actor_id mirrors the Relation to_ref.

title.description: Derived display title from plaintext-visible Strand metadata.title; null when metadata is encrypted or hidden from the service profile.

summary.description: Derived display summary from plaintext-visible Strand metadata.summary; null when metadata is encrypted or hidden from the service profile.

board_space_id.description: Derived board Space id from ck.component.strand.position.v1; not canonical Strand object state.

list_space_id.description: Derived list Space id from ck.component.strand.position.v1; not canonical Strand object state.

rank.description: Derived rank within list_space_id from ck.component.strand.position.v1.

assigned_actor_ids.description: Derived current assignee Actor DIDs from visible active Relation(relation_kind=assigned_to, from_ref=strand_id). Empty or absent means the Strand is unassigned for this projection caller. This is read-model state, not canonical Strand object metadata.

assigned_to_relations.description: Read-only active assigned_to Relation edges backing assigned_actor_ids. Clients use relation_id to tombstone assignments.

is_default.description: DERIVED, not independent storage: true iff strand_id == the parent Realm projection's default_strand_id (the authoritative pointer written by ck.realm.set_default_strand). The projector computes this from Realm.default_strand_id; a stale/dangling pointer never resolves to is_default=true because the reducer rejects set_default_strand against a non-existent Strand. Clients identify the Realm's default discussion Strand deterministically from this flag (or equivalently from Realm.default_strand_id) and MUST NOT infer the default from any Strand-reuses-Realm-UUID or other implementation detail. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md (default-Strand discovery).

kind.description: Space kind such as `board`, `list`, `folder`, or a profile-registered kind.

ServiceDid.description: Bare DID identifying a service endpoint.

SnapshotBootstrap.description: Optional ck.self.events.query.scan acceleration hint for federation pull / backfill. snapshot_ref is an external pointer and MUST equal the Snapshot manifest id. Verifier MUST validate signature, state_digest, snapshot_frontier, chunk digests, created_by, created_at, and authority_binding before use (manifest fields are bound by the manifest signature transcript — see schemas/snapshot.schema.json).

snapshot_ref.description: External pointer to the Snapshot manifest; MUST equal schemas/snapshot.schema.json#/properties/id.

created_by.description: DID of the snapshot issuer; bound by the manifest signature transcript.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp ending in 'Z' when the manifest was sealed; bound by the manifest signature transcript.

authority_binding.description: Snapshot issuer authority evidence bound by the manifest signature transcript; mirrors schemas/snapshot.schema.json#/properties/authority_binding.

security_class.description: Snapshot verification class. high_assurance requires verification_hints with inclusion challenge and non-accepted-input digests.

state_digest.description: Hash of the canonical reducer-derived state at the snapshot frontier (Lattice cell values keyed by cell_family/cell_subject, plus reducer_profile / schema_profile_refs). This binds *what the state is*. Paired with event_set_commitment which binds *which events produced it*: a verifier replays the events covered by event_set_commitment under reducer_profile and MUST obtain the same state_digest. The two digests are independent and BOTH required — state_digest alone cannot detect missing-event tampering, event_set_commitment alone cannot detect reducer divergence.

frontier.$comment: This is a true frontier (boundary head event ids of the snapshot), not a cumulative covered-set enumeration; it is unrelated to the retired Seal-coverage enumeration (Seal coverage is recursive via predecessor_refs + delta).

event_set_commitment.description: Commitment to the *set of events* whose replay produces state_digest. Algorithm + root + covered_event_count name the canonical reduction of those events; covered_event_ids / actor_seq_ranges narrow which event ids and per-actor sequences are bound. Paired with state_digest (see state_digest description): both fields are independently required because state_digest binds reducer output and event_set_commitment binds reducer input.

covered_event_ids.description: When present, MUST denote the same event id set as the top-level frontier.event_ids (set equality): both bind the same snapshot frontier. Consumers MUST reject the snapshot on any mismatch (cross-field consistency enforced by snapshot-schema.md section 5, not by JSON Schema). Renamed from covered_seals: the members are boundary event ids, not Seal ids; the old spelling is hard-rejected (migration/renames.json) and is unrelated to the MLS covered_seals_cell (ck.component.covered_seals.v1), which keeps its name.

created_by.description: DID of the snapshot issuer (server / Realm notary / federation witness). Required because the snapshot signature transcript binds this field via x-canonical-bytes-include.

created_at.description: Issuer-local timestamp when the snapshot manifest was sealed. RFC 3339 UTC, MUST end with 'Z'. Required because the snapshot signature transcript binds this field via x-canonical-bytes-include.

authority_binding.description: Evidence that created_by was authorized to seal this snapshot at created_at. Verifiers MUST reject the snapshot when this binding cannot be checked against Realm policy / witness quorum at or before created_at.

issuer.description: MUST equal top-level created_by. Aligns with the canonical 'issuer' DID field used by audit-ryw-receipt, range-completeness-attestation, capability-grant, etc. (see common-fields.md §4.2).

auth_state_digest.description: Hash of the authorization state used to verify snapshot issuer authority.

auth_frontier.description: Realm auth/policy frontier proving the signer authority at created_at.

signature.description: Detached proof over the JCS canonical snapshot manifest bytes with only the signature field omitted. The signed transcript therefore binds id, realm_id, reducer_profile, schema_profile_refs, state_digest, frontier, event_set_commitment, chunks (chunk_ref / digest / size_bytes), security_class, verification_hints, created_by, created_at, and authority_binding. Because security_class is signed (and required), a high_assurance -> standard downgrade cannot be performed without invalidating the signature.

schemas/space.schema.json.title: Cokret Space
schemas/space.schema.json.description: A Space is a structural grouping object inside a Realm. Boards, lists, swimlanes, calendar buckets, document outline groups, etc. are all Spaces. Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership/policy/E2EE group; its metadata may be placed in an existing Realm/Circle effective scope via scope_circle_id.

realm_id.description: Home Realm that stores, syncs, and authorizes this Space object's own metadata. This is also the fallback default Realm for new resources under this Space when default_realm_id is absent.

default_realm_id.description: Optional default Realm for resources created under this Space. Omitted means inherit from the nearest ancestor Space with default_realm_id, falling back to realm_id. This field does not grant membership or decryption rights.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional Circle scope for this Space object's own metadata and scoped structural relation facts. Space still does not own a security boundary; it only places its metadata into an existing Circle scope. Omitted means Realm-default scope.

default_scope_circle_id.description: Optional default Circle scope for newly created child resources. MUST belong to the Space's effective default_realm_id for those child resources (which may be inherited); it is not necessarily the Space metadata home Realm when cross-Realm defaults are configured. This is a creation hint, not an authorization or placement constraint; use child_scope_policy for reducer-enforced requirements.

child_scope_policy.description: Reducer-enforced placement/encryption policy for child resources created in or moved into this Space.

parent_space_id.description: Optional parent in the structural hierarchy. Parent MAY live in a different Realm; such a link is navigation only and never propagates membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.

kind.description: Space kind. v1 standard kinds include 'space', 'project', 'folder', 'board', and 'list'. Profile-defined kinds (e.g., 'swimlane', 'calendar_bucket', 'page_group') MAY be added via Realm schema/profile and MUST be registered. Unknown kind MUST schema_violation.

rank.description: Fractional-index rank within parent. See encoding.md §9.

schema_refs.description: Optional schema/profile references that further constrain this Space's contained Strand types, fields, or position invariants.

fields.description: Space kind-specific fields, e.g., { 'wip_limit': 5 } for kind=list, { 'view_id': 'ck:view:...' } for kind=board's default view. MUST NOT contain a 'rank' key (rank is a top-level Space field; see relation.md §2 for the symmetric Relation constraint and forbidden-wire-fields.json `fields.rank/space_payload`).

state.description: Space lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. State transitions are reducer-enforced per common-fields.md §5.1: ck.space.archive MUST come from state=='active' (else failed_precondition reason=space_not_active); ck.space.restore MUST come from state=='archived' (else failed_precondition reason=space_not_archived); ck.space.tombstone MUST come from {'active','archived'} AND must have no live dependents (failed_precondition reason=space_already_terminal for terminal source, space_has_live_dependents for live refs). Same-state self-transitions (archive on archived, etc.) MUST fail; clients re-archive by restore-then-archive. Tombstoned is irreversible (MUST NOT be restored). The transition timestamp lives on the writing Move and on state_changed_at.

state_changed_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent state transition. Required when state != 'active'.

anyOf.$comment: forbidden Strand top-level field; canonical name is content
forbidden Strand top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.title or encrypted_metadata
forbidden Strand top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.summary or encrypted_metadata
forbidden Strand top-level extension metadata; canonical path is metadata.fields or encrypted_metadata
forbidden encrypted content carrier; canonical name is encrypted_content

scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle (see models/circle.md) that defines this Strand's effective scope. When set, ALL Strand tracks (synthesis, discussion, etc.) share that Circle's membership, history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and encryption_profile. When unset, the Strand lives in Realm-default scope. The referenced Circle MUST have realm_id == this Strand's realm_id (reducer enforces; otherwise schema_violation reason=circle_realm_mismatch). Reducer stamps the immutable effective_scope onto each emitted Event; rebinding scope_circle_id is forbidden by default (failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden). For 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion' scenarios use two Strands linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation (circle.md §7.2).

agent_participation.description: Optional agent participation ceiling for this Strand: the maximum native personal agent behavior permitted in this Strand. When omitted, inherits the enclosing Circle ceiling (or Realm-default ceiling when scope_circle_id is unset). Each bit MAY only tighten, never widen, the parent ceiling (reducer rejects a widening write with agent_participation_ceiling_widen). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a strand_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata when the effective metadata_encryption_floor is e2ee_required.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a ContentBlock for Strand synthesis content.

tracks.description: Active Strand tracks, keyed by track name. Tracks are pure section pointers (synthesis vs discussion timeline) — they do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE. The entire Strand shares a single effective scope determined by Strand.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md); there is no per-track security boundary. At most one track entry may explicitly set is_primary=true; when none does, the reducer derives the primary track by the deterministic rules in models/strand-and-message.md §4.5. The map MUST contain at least one entry; track names are validated by propertyNames.

state.description: Strand lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: ck.strand.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=strand_not_active); ck.strand.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else strand_not_archived); terminal state is reached only via a ck.redaction event targeting the strand (MUST come from {'active','archived'} else strand_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ck.strand.archive / ck.strand.restore / ck.redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

stage.description: Optional Strand business-progression stage. Orthogonal to top-level 'state' (physical lifecycle): archive does NOT change stage; stage=done does NOT auto-archive. ck.strand.create MAY omit stage; when present it must be one of the protocol-level enum values and has no protocol-level default. The only wire path that mutates stage after creation is the dedicated ck.strand.stage.set event; ck.strand.update patches on stage / stage_changed_at MUST be rejected (schema_violation, single-source). Stage transitions intentionally do NOT carry a reason / note field — the ck.strand.stage.set event log is the audit source, and human-readable explanations belong in a Message on the discussion track that references the event. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond the core reducer hard invariants (terminal state freeze, non-active reject) defined in models/common-fields.md §5.3.3. See models/strand-and-message.md §3.2 for full semantics and models/common-fields.md §5.3 for the protocol-level enum / bucket mapping.

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition. MUST NOT appear without stage. MUST be ignored when present on wire; reducer overwrites with the triggering ck.strand.stage.set event's created_at. Same-value self-transitions (stage value unchanged) MUST NOT update this field.

not.$comment: Reject discriminator field `type`, composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`; canonical content blocks use `kind`, composite children use `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes`.

strand_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Strand metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

metadata_fields.description: Profile-defined Strand metadata fields. Reducer-owned fields are forbidden here to avoid dual sources of truth.

strand_track.description: Strand track entry — a pure section pointer (synthesis vs discussion timeline). The track's stable name is the map key in Strand.tracks; this object holds the track's per-entry config. Tracks do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE. The whole Strand has a single effective scope determined by Strand.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md); there is no per-track security boundary. To represent 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion', create two Strands linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation per models/circle.md §7.2.

enabled.description: Whether this track currently accepts new writes (synthesis edits / discussion messages). Default true when omitted. Setting enabled=false MUST cause the reducer to reject subsequent writes to this track with 'track_disabled' until enabled is set back to true. Disabling a track does NOT delete prior history; it freezes new writes only. UI MAY hide a disabled track or render it read-only.

metadata.description: Track-local UI metadata only. The reducer NEVER interprets its keys; it does not create membership, history visibility, access, or E2EE scope. Access-like keys are rejected at the wire layer to prevent a pseudo-access surface (tracks have no independent access — see models/strand-and-message.md §4.4).

not.$comment: Forbid access-like keys so strand_track.metadata cannot smuggle a pseudo-access surface; track access is always derived from the Strand effective scope, never from track metadata.
Legacy track-local extension field; canonical name is metadata.

visibility.description: View sharing visibility. Private views are actor-private account data; shared views are canonical Realm objects.

collection_grouping.description: Grouping / lane / time-bucket / matrix configuration; mirrors models/views.md §3.3. Conditional required-ness is enforced per mode.

item_order_by.description: Stable item ordering; mirrors models/views.md §3.2. Drag-ordered collections SHOULD sort by rank.

display_fields.description: Display columns (dot path + format); see models/views.md §3.2.
